GOAT Group is seeking a Sr. Performance Marketing Specialist to run our paid social and video acquisition strategy. You will own and operate Meta, TikTok, and YouTube Ads. You will also develop the creative testing roadmap and leverage incrementality to measure performance. This role reports to the AVP of Growth.

We expect AI fluency in practice. As targeting, bidding, and placement have moved inside the platforms’ models, creative has become the main lever you control. Leveraging AI tools for strategic research and automating operations will be key to success. Much of our process is being automated through internal AI workflows, so this role will have more emphasis on workflow oversight.

In this role, you will:

- Run day-to-day paid social and video across Meta, TikTok, and YouTube: campaign build, budget pacing, audience and placement setup, and optimization against incrementality KPIs.

- Run structured tests — holdouts, geo splits, incrementality reads — supporting the AVP of Growth, and interpret the results honestly against platform-reported numbers.
- Flag new formats, placements, and platform features worth testing, and make the case for trying them.

How Success Is Measured

- Incrementality. To truly understand the performance of our efforts, we rely on incrementality methods, such as geolift. We then leverage platform metrics as multipliers based on the measurement outcomes for daily operational KPIs.
- Creative performance. Leverage platform metrics to build creative narratives to explain how they performed and what we should do next.
- Operational reliability. Campaigns should launch accurately and on time. With AI automated more operations, this person must be have final oversight before campaigns launch.

We are looking for:

- 3+ years of hands-on performance marketing experience with Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, and/or YouTube Ads.
- Experience with incrementality and/or MMM to measure true lift or causal performance.
- Comfort working in performance data — pivot tables, dashboards, and enough rigor to catch a number that looks wrong before it reaches a deck.
- AI fluency in practice. You use LLMs and AI tooling in your daily workflow for briefs, copy variants, creative iteration, and reporting, and you can tell us specifically what it changed about your output and what you had to watch for.
- Strong written and verbal communication. You can explain a result, including a disappointing one, to people who do not live in the ad platforms.

About this role

Luxury Presence is building the AI growth platform for real estate. More than 90,000 real estate professionals, including over 30% of the WSJ Real Trends top 100 agents in the United States, use us to run and grow their business.

Role Overview

We’re looking for a Staff Product Manager to own the SEO and AI visibility solutions we build for our clients: more than 20,000 real estate websites that rank independently, each in its own market, with its own authority, its own competitors, and a real business depending on the outcome. This is not the SEO of a single corporate domain or one large marketplace. It is a platform product, where one change to a template, a schema implementation, or the way we render content moves thousands of domains at once.

The mandate is an excellent organic discovery platform: technical foundations, page experience, conversion, content, measurement, migrations, and experimentation. AI search is a growing part of that. Our clients are evaluated by Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode, by ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini, and by every prospective seller who asks an assistant which agent they should call. The best people in this job design for three constituencies at once: the people who visit these sites, the crawlers and AI agents that read them, and the real estate business whose revenue depends on both.

This is not a job for someone who runs audits and hands recommendations to other people. You will set the strategy, ship with your own engineering team, and build the defaults, standards, and safeguards that make quality hold across the entire fleet. Most real estate professionals will never hire a technical SEO of their own. Our platform is how they get one.

What You’ll Do

- Own the product strategy and roadmap for organic discovery and AI visibility across every site on the platform, including what clients can see, control, and get credit for
- Own the technical foundations across every page type we generate: crawlability, indexation, rendering, internal linking, structured data, and page performance
- Productize what repeats. When the same issue or workflow shows up across the fleet, solve it once through better defaults, automation, shared capabilities, or safeguards
- Make our clients’ brands, listings, and expertise legible to AI assistants, and define how we measure citations and visibility across answer engines
- Run a real experimentation program: prove changes on representative cohorts of sites, establish incremental impact, then scale what works rather than shipping broadly and inferring impact afterward
- Own migration quality and regression prevention, including the standards, acceptance criteria, and automated checks that hold search quality as the platform ships
- Partner with the team building the next generation of our website platform so search is designed in from the start, and give every product team a low-friction path to the right implementation
- Set platform-level goals for organic performance, AI visibility, and client outcomes, and report against them to leadership

Who You Are

- 8+ years combined across SEO and product management, including 3+ years as a product manager shipping alongside engineering teams
- You have owned search for a platform that hosts many independent customer domains, such as a website builder, a hosting or commerce platform, or a multi-location or franchise network. Running search for one large marketplace or corporate domain is valuable experience, but the fleet problem is a different job and it is the one we have
- Deep technical foundation across rendering and JavaScript SEO, crawl and index management, information architecture, structured data, page performance, and migrations
- You treat bots and AI agents as users of a website alongside people, and you design for both without trading one against the other
- Obsessive about experimentation and measurement, including cohort testing, causal impact analysis, Search Console data at scale, log analysis, and the discipline to tell a result from a coincidence
- A current point of view on AI search, including how models discover, interpret, and cite a brand, and the judgment to separate what genuinely moves visibility from what is repackaged advice
- Fluent with AI as a working tool. You use it to investigate messy systems, establish ground truth quickly, prototype solutions, and unblock yourself rather than waiting on another team at every stage of discovery
- You get requirements implemented by teams you do not own, and you are welcome back afterward. What you write is sharp enough that a team of engineers can move without waiting on you
- Opinionated about prioritization. This space generates infinite work, and your judgment about what to ignore matters as much as what you ship

Team: Product Marketing

About the Role

6sense is the GTM Intelligence Platform, and Foundation is the layer the rest of it stands on — "platform, data, infrastructure: the backbone everything builds on." It owns account and people data, matching and identity, the APIs and MCP framework, security and connectors, signal publication, and the workflows that move data through the system. When buyers ask whether 6sense is accurate, extensible, secure, and composable, the answer lives here.

We're looking for a Principal Technical Product Marketing Manager to own positioning, messaging, and go-to-market for the Foundation pillar. This is the most technical seat on the PMM team. You'll translate deep capabilities — identity resolution, data coverage and accuracy, API extensibility, the MCP framework, security and compliance — into differentiated stories that win over the technical and economic buyers who scrutinize them: RevOps architects, IT and security teams, data leaders, and increasingly developers building agentic GTM stacks.

You'll also carry one of the most strategically important narratives in the company: that 6sense is a composable intelligence layer other systems and AI agents plug into — "AI to the data, not data to the AI" — rather than a closed destination. With the MCP framework moving to GA, this is a present-tense story, and you'll be the one who tells it credibly.

* * *

What You'll Own

- Positioning and messaging for the Foundation pillar — platform, data, infrastructure, identity and matching, APIs and the MCP framework, security and connectors, signal publication, and workflows. You set the narrative and keep it coherent with the Intelligence and Activation pillars.

- Differentiation for the data and identity layer. Make the case against point data providers and infrastructure alternatives — coverage, match rates, identity quality, enrichment, security posture — and arm the field to win on it.
- Field and partner enablement for technical evaluations. Build the battlecards, objection handling, FAQs, and solution content that win RFPs, security reviews, and technical POCs. Partner with Sales Engineering to make the technical buyer's diligence a place 6sense wins.
- Launches. Drive end-to-end GTM for Foundation releases: new data assets, API and MCP capabilities, security packages (SCIM, SSO role mapping, audit, custom roles), connectors, and workflow features.
- Cross-functional partnership. Work shoulder-to-shoulder with the Foundation Product and Engineering leaders to shape roadmap-to-market, and with Customer Success to surface the post-sale and admin/security use cases that prove the platform's breadth.
- Market and competitive intelligence for the data and platform layer, feeding insight back into roadmap and pricing/packaging conversations.

* * *

What You'll Bring

- 8+ years in product marketing, technical product management, or a closely related function, with substantial technical PMM experience for platform, data, infrastructure, API, or developer products.
- A proven ability to translate technical concepts — APIs, data pipelines, identity resolution, integrations, security, and AI/agent architectures like MCP — into crisp positioning and business value, without losing the engineers in the room or the buyers outside it.
- A track record owning messaging for technical products and enabling technical sales motions (Sales Engineering, RFPs, security reviews, POCs).
- Hands-on, not hand-wavy. You'll personally call the APIs, stand up and configure the MCP server, connect it to an agent, and build the demo — and your messaging is sharper because you've done the thing, not just read the spec.
- Strong writing — you can produce content that is technically rigorous and genuinely clear, from a one-line value prop to an architecture whitepaper.
- Fluency with the B2B SaaS buyer, ideally in martech, RevTech, or data platforms, and comfort selling to technical and economic buyers (RevOps architects, IT, security, data teams, developers).
- The judgment and presence to operate as a senior individual contributor: set strategy, lead cross-functionally without authority, and influence product and executive stakeholders.

* * *

Nice to Have

- Hands-on familiarity with data enrichment and identity (waterfall enrichment, matching, intent data), MCP and agentic AI architectures, or composable/API-first platforms.
- Experience marketing to developers or technical evaluators, including documentation-adjacent and developer-community work.
- Background in or adjacent to GTM intelligence, ABM, sales intelligence, CDP, iPaaS, or identity platforms.

* * *

What Success Looks Like

In your first 6–12 months, Foundation has a differentiated, defensible position that technical buyers recognize; the composable/MCP infrastructure story is landed with the field and the market as something that exists today, not a roadmap promise; the data and identity credibility story is substantiated with proof, not assertion; and the field has the enablement to win the technical evaluation every time it comes.

We’re hiring an Events Manager to scale these experiences and deepen our relationships with the GTM community: executive dinners, industry conferences, sponsorships, speaking moments, webinars, and ChiliPalooza. You’ll shape the annual plan, then make it happen: logistics, promotion, on-site, and follow-up, all the way through to measurable impact.

What you’ll do

- Own the annual event calendar. Decide, with marketing leadership, where Chili Piper should have a presence and why, and protect that focus as new opportunities come up

- Bring original ideas, creativity, and humor to how we show up, so our events feel like Chili Piper and not like everyone else’s

- Manage execution end to end. Logistics, budgets, venues, vendors, shipments, swag, and on-site coordination, done by you and tracked by you

- Run the debrief on every event and turn what you learn into a stronger program next time

- Builder mindset. You don’t wait for someone to tell you how, you figure it out

- Tech-savvy operator. You know your way around CRM exports, spreadsheets, event tools, and email automation

- Hands-on doer. You do the execution and track the results yourself

- Creative problem-solver. When a venue cancels or a vendor flakes, you find a workaround fast, and when the format is stale, you invent a better one

- Organized and proactive. You turn chaos into systems and think two steps ahead

- Strong communicator. You coordinate cross-functional teams, vendors, and execs smoothly

- Customer-first. You care about memorable, frictionless experiences from invite to post-event follow-up

- Curious and eager to learn. You’re always exploring new tools, trends, and ideas, including AI, to make each event better than the last

Experience

- Proven ability to plan and execute events, from small dinners to large activations

- Hands-on experience with CRM tools like Salesforce and HubSpot, and event platforms like Luma, Zoom Webinars or similar

- Comfortable building simple landing pages, managing email lists, and running event promotion campaigns

- Skilled in vendor sourcing, budget tracking, and on-site coordination

- Strong cross-functional collaboration with Marketing, Sales, and Partnerships

- Excellent organizational and communication skills, with the ability to work independently and manage shifting priorities

- Familiar with tracking and reporting event performance, including attendance, engagement, and pipeline impact

- Experience managing partner collaborations or maintaining relationships with GTM leaders and communities is a plus

Nice to have

- Experience in B2B SaaS, RevOps, or MarTech

- Prior involvement in partner activations or co-marketing events

- Comfortable using analytics tools to measure event outcomes

- A strong network within the GTM, Sales, or Marketing communities

- Background in social or content amplification around events, for example capturing and repurposing event moments

Interview process

2. Culture add interview. A first chat to get to know you: what drives you, how you like to work, and what unique perspective you’d bring to Chili Piper.

3. Assessment. A short, practical assignment to see how you think and approach a real events challenge. It’s not a test, we just want to see your creativity and thought process.

4. Executive interview. The final step. We’ll talk about your bigger picture, your passion for the space, your understanding of our product, and why Chili Piper feels like the right next step for you.

TL;DR

We’re not hiring a “planner.” We’re hiring someone who can own the full experience, from the CRM export to the on-site execution to the community that keeps growing after everyone goes home, and turn GTM moments into momentum and measurable results.

If that sounds like you, we want to talk.

Our team loves Chili Piper because we’re building the company of the future.

- Be helpful. Our first value as a company is help. Help our customers be successful. Help our prospects get the right information and make the right decision whether or not it includes our products. Help our team members reach their full potential.

- Generous health, dental, and vision insurance

The Opportunity:

Data privacy has become one of the most strategic challenges facing modern enterprises — sitting at the intersection of AI governance, data operations, and customer trust. As companies adopt AI at scale, they need new ways to automate privacy and manage risk without slowing innovation. DataGrail has launched the first agentic privacy platform, and we're entering a pivotal phase of growth as we scale toward the next stage of the business.

As a Senior Demand Generation Manager, you'll own both halves of the pipeline engine: the campaigns that create demand, and the systems that capture, route, score, and measure it. You'll lead paid media across channels like Google, LinkedIn, and YouTube and drive the event calendar, including trade shows, webinars, and executive roundtables. You'll shape HubSpot as an architect, not just a user, and build the reporting that tells our leadership team whether any of it worked. This isn't a blank slate: paid channels are already live with an agency in place, the event calendar is established, and HubSpot and attribution already exist. You're inheriting a functioning engine, with plenty of authority to make it even stronger.

It's a small team with a large surface area, so roughly two thirds of your time goes toward driving demand through campaign strategy, paid media, and events, and the other third goes toward building the systems that make that demand measurable and repeatable through HubSpot architecture, lifecycle programs, and attribution. In this role, one person connects both sides of the engine, creating a much tighter link between what we invest, what we learn, and what ultimately produces pipeline.

You'll have real authority to change what isn't working from day one, and on a team this size, a fix you make on Tuesday can be live by Friday. By the end of the year, you'll be the person leadership trusts for a straight answer on whether campaigns and events are actually working.

What You'll Do

- Translate GTM priorities, ICP definitions, and quarterly pipeline targets into integrated campaigns across paid, events, and email, then build and ship them yourself.
- Own paid media end to end, building, launching, and optimizing campaigns across Google Ads, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, and YouTube while partnering with our agency on execution.
- Drive the event calendar, including trade shows, webinars, and executive roundtables, sharpening targeting and follow-through while focusing investment on what delivers results.
- Carry a quarterly qualified-pipeline number and defend coverage, quality, and conversion with sales leadership, not just volume.
- Architect HubSpot as an owner, managing workflows, lifecycle stages, lead scoring, campaign objects, and the Salesforce sync.
- Build and defend the metrics that matter, including CPL, cost per qualified opportunity, event-sourced pipeline, and multi-touch attribution.
- Partner with Sales, Product Marketing, and RevOps internally, and agencies, venues, and sponsors externally, to run multiple concurrent campaigns and events without dropping a thread.

What You'll Bring

- A track record of hands-on HubSpot ownership, having personally architected and administered an instance, including workflows, lifecycle, scoring, campaigns, and the Salesforce sync.
- Direct paid media execution, with hands-on experience building, optimizing, and pacing campaigns in Google Ads and LinkedIn Campaign Manager, not just briefing an agency.
- Salesforce fluency, with the ability to navigate objects, fields, and reports and reason about how marketing data lands in the CRM and why it breaks.
- B2B SaaS demand generation experience, ideally within a considered, multi-stakeholder sales cycle.
- Experience owning event strategy and execution, including trade shows, webinars, and executive-level programs like roundtables or dinners.
- Comfort owning a function end to end, balancing strategy with hands-on execution in an individual contributor role.
- Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to effectively  manage internal stakeholders and external vendors and partners.

Bonus Points

- Experience in privacy, data governance, security, compliance, or another regulated, technical software category.
- Marketo or Pardot experience alongside HubSpot.
- Familiarity with account-based marketing or intent-data tools.
- Comfort using AI to speed up operational work, such as campaign QA, data hygiene, or reporting synthesis.
- Experience being the first or founding owner of a demand gen or marketing ops function, from the ground up with hands-on responsibility for building and scaling it.

What Success Looks Like

Within 90 Days You'll:

- Learn DataGrail's product, buyer personas, and ICP quickly enough to start contributing, not just observing, and meet the marketing, sales, RevOps, and customer success teams to understand what's running and where the friction is.
- Take full ownership of the paid channels and the agency relationship, and identify specific over- or under-spending by channel.
- Drive the event calendar and process, and produce a keep, fix, or cut recommendation for each program.
- Audit HubSpot and existing reporting, and deliver a written list of what's fragile, missing, or misleading in current attribution and lifecycle reporting.
- Ship at least one visible fix to a live, underperforming channel or process

Within 180 Days You'll:

- Show measurable improvement, with before and after comparisons, on two to three of the biggest inefficiencies identified in the 90-day audit, whether that's rebalanced paid spend, improved event-to-pipeline conversion, or cleaner attribution.
- Run paid media and events with full autonomy, proposing and executing budget and calendar changes without waiting on sign-off.
- Ship at least three new or rebuilt nurture and re-engagement tracks, with early performance data on each.
- Rebuild or upgrade the dashboards used for weekly pipeline calls.
- Build a working rhythm with Sales, RevOps, and Product Marketing so hand-offs, routing, and lead flow don't require chasing people down.

Within 365 Days You'll:

- Own a program for paid media, events, and HubSpot that runs noticeably better than the one you inherited, with clear before and after numbers on channel efficiency and cost per qualified opportunity.
- Be the person others trust when they want to know how well our campaigns and events are actually performing.
- Have made real budget and channel calls, moving spend into what works and cutting what doesn't, with pipeline impact you can point to.
- Have built a foundation that doesn't need rebuilding when volume doubles.
- Have identified where the team needs more support, whether that's tooling, headcount, or an agency change, and made the case for it.

Our Marketing Analytics team is a cross-functional group supporting all aspects of Gametime, partnering closely with User Acquisition to optimize mobile campaign performance across channels like Meta, TikTok, Reddit, and other paid platforms. We drive creative and spend efficiency through rigorous experimentation, advanced measurement, and granular channel analysis, and we work to strengthen the connection between platform-reported performance, attribution-based data, and internal customer economics. The team studies mobile cohorts to identify high-value opportunities across leagues, teams, performers, and user segments, with an eye toward maximizing lifetime value and durable growth.

The Role

We're hiring a Senior Data Scientist to help build and scale the analytical frameworks that power mobile marketing at Gametime, from executive-level performance narratives down to campaign, creative, cohort, and audience-level diagnostics.

The ideal candidate has hands-on experience with mobile marketing, paid social platforms, mobile attribution, experimentation, causal measurement, audience management, and financial profitability modeling in a marketplace or consumer mobile setting, and is comfortable moving fluidly between strategic and highly granular work.

What You'll Do

- Own the analytical frameworks for tracking mobile marketing effectiveness in a privacy-aware environment, bridging platform-reported data, attribution data, MMP data, and internal truth to support confident decisions despite measurement noise.

- Analyze how marketplace conditions, event demand, league mix, pricing, and seasonality influence acquisition efficiency, helping distinguish marketing execution shifts from broader marketplace dynamics.
- Partner with leadership to translate complex analyses into clear recommendations on spend allocation, channel strategy, and growth investment, communicating tradeoffs and risks to support fast decisions.
- Stay current on the evolving mobile privacy and attribution landscape (Apple ATT, MMP capabilities) to keep data science a competitive advantage in how Gametime measures and scales mobile growth.

- Hands-on experience with Meta, TikTok, Reddit, or similar paid social platforms, analyzing performance at the campaign, creative, and cohort level.

At Gong, you will join a company built on innovative products, ambitious goals, and passionate people. We are shaping the future of revenue intelligence and we want people who are excited to build what comes next. You will work with a team that dreams big, moves fast, and cares deeply about the craft and about each other. As Vice President of Product Marketing, you’ll lead the global Product Marketing function and shape the story, strategy, and go-to-market (GTM) execution that define Gong’s leadership in Revenue AI. In a market where nearly every product now claims to be “AI-powered,” your job is to establish what makes Gong defensibly different — grounded in a deep understanding of our products and technology, and mapped tightly to the value our customers care about. You’ll partner closely with Product and the broader GTM organization to drive clarity, excitement, and growth around Gong’s platform and solutions.

Reporting directly to the Chief Product Officer, this role is both strategic and hands-on, setting the vision for how Gong shows up in the market, while providing operational clarity to our teams and guiding them to win. It is a rare opportunity to lead at a company defining a new category and rewriting the rules of go-to-market success. You’ll have the platform, people, and purpose to make an impact — on our market, our customers, and our brand.

You MUST be located in one of our hub locations (San Francisco, Salt Lake City, Austin, New York City Metro, Chicago) due to our hybrid work model.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Deep Product & Customer Understanding

- Develop deep product and technical fluency. Build a hands-on, first-principles understanding of Gong’s products, AI, ecosystem, and underlying technology so you can tease out the true, defensible differentiation that generic “AI wrappers” can’t replicate. Partner with Product leadership to align roadmaps with customer needs and market trends, and ensure GTM plans are grounded in real product depth.
- Champion the customer POV and value. Immerse yourself in the customer’s world, including pain points, buying journey, and decision criteria, and translate Gong’s product value proposition into quantifiable customer value and business outcomes. Use the customer’s own language, drawn from win-loss analysis, customer interviews, and sales conversations in Gong, as the raw material for positioning and messaging.

Positioning & Differentiation

- Own Gong’s strategic narrative and positioning. Craft clear, differentiated messaging and positioning across the platform, products, and competitive landscape, and codify it in a messaging architecture and assets that the GTM and Marketing teams can carry across every marketing channel.
- Establish true differentiation in a crowded AI market. In a category still being defined, where “AI-powered” is now table stakes, define what makes Gong distinct and hard to copy. Lead with customer outcomes over technology, ground claims in measurable proof and accuracy, and sharpen positioning against both horizontal foundation-model providers and point solutions, anticipating how the competitive set will keep shifting.

GTM Execution Support

- Lead product launches that drive growth. Own launch narrative, enablement, and execution across every customer touchpoint so new products and capabilities land with the GTM team and drive customer engagement, adoption, and growth.
- Leverage AI to scale knowledge sharing. Use AI tools to scale context and content to GTM teams so reps can generate tailored, on-brand content in real time — by persona, segment, industry, and deal stage. Deliver the messaging, playbooks, demos, and more that improve close rates, win rates, and deal velocity, and close the “last-mile” gap between what marketing produces and what reps actually use.

Solution Marketing

- Tailor the value proposition by industry and persona. Develop differentiated value propositions, messaging, use cases, and proof points for Gong's priority industries and buyer personas, translating each segment's specific business challenges into measurable, role-relevant outcomes.
- Carry the solution story across the full customer journey. Ensure the tailored value proposition shows up consistently at every stage — fueling demand generation and campaigns to build awareness and pipeline, guiding buyers through evaluation, and equipping the field with the plays, business cases, and proof points needed to advance and close deals.

Brand, Communications & Thought Leadership

- Shape Gong’s external narrative. Partner with Corporate Marketing to influence Gong’s media coverage, analyst reports, and industry rankings.
- Serve as a senior external ambassador for Gong. Regularly engage with industry analysts, press, influencers, partners, and customers to build trusted relationships, shape market perception, and represent Gong’s strategy, products, and point of view with credibility and consistency.
- Develop thought leadership and demand-gen content. Work with the Content team to deliver high-impact materials that engage buyers from awareness through decision, plus speaking opportunities that reinforce Gong’s position as the leader in Revenue AI.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Partnerships

- Build deep cross-functional partnerships. Operate as connective tissue across the company, forging especially deep and durable partnerships with the GTM organization and with Product, aligning strategy, roadmap, and field execution around a shared story and shared outcomes.
- Empower channel and partner success. Partner with the Partnerships team to spotlight new integrations, MCP support, and marketplace and co-sell partnerships, turning a fast-growing ecosystem into a proof point for Gong's platform leadership.

QUALIFICATIONS

- 15+ years of Product Marketing experience in B2B enterprise software (SaaS preferred), with a proven record of creating differentiated positioning and driving measurable business impact.
- Experience positioning AI or other technically sophisticated products in a fast-moving, still-forming category, where differentiation must be earned through outcomes, proof, and depth rather than claimed.
- Deep technical curiosity and fluency: able to get hands-on with the product and technology, understand how the AI actually works, and translate that into defensible differentiation and clear customer value.
- High fluency with AI tools across the PMM workflow (research, insight synthesis, messaging, competitive intelligence, enablement, and content), and a strong point of view on using them to scale context and tailored, real-time content to GTM teams without sacrificing quality or strategic judgment.
- Experience leading large, high-performing PMM teams in scaling organizations, ideally at $500M+ ARR.
- Strong strategic thinking paired with executional excellence: you can shape a vision and roll up your sleeves to make it happen.
- Proven ability to partner cross-functionally with GTM, Product, and Marketing leaders, building deep and durable relationships that align strategies and outcomes.
- A customer-first mindset and passion for creating market-defining stories that inspire and sell.
- Bring urgency, extreme ownership, and a bias for action, staying hands-on to do whatever it takes to drive impact.
- Creative, resourceful, and energized by a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

PERKS & BENEFITS

marketing channels: email, direct mail, and digital. This role sits at the intersection of marketing strategy, data, and technical execution. You will turn raw campaign and behavioral data into clear analysis that drives decisions at every level, from channel owners to the executive team.

Our data foundation is built by our data engineering team. You will be its most demanding user. Responsibilities

Channel Performance Measurement & Analytics

Decision support for performance marketing

Data quality and the data foundation

- Question the data: find gaps, conflicting definitions, and tracking breaks, reconcile numbers across platforms, and raise issues with the specifics the data team needs to fix them
- Define requirements for data engineering, including the events, facts, dimensions, and metric definitions needed to support attribution, mix modeling, and scoring in the future, and explain why each one matters
- Document the metric definitions and logic the marketing team relies on

Data Science & Advanced Modeling

- These responsibilities build on the measurement foundation above. Expect to start by evaluating and directing this work, and to take on more of the build as the data matures.
- Own marketing mix modeling (MMM) end to end — building, validating, and refreshing models that quantify channel contribution, diminishing returns, and saturation to guide budget allocation
- Develop propensity and other scoring models to predict member behavior — conversion, churn, and engagement — and operationalize scores to drive targeting, segmentation, and lifecycle marketing
- Apply Bayesian network analysis and related probabilistic methods to model relationships between marketing drivers and outcomes, quantify uncertainty, and support causal and incrementality analysis
- Partner with data engineering to productionize models, monitor performance over time, and ensure outputs are reliable, explainable, and decision-ready for leadership

Experimentation and testing

- Design, run, and read A/B and multivariate tests, including sample sizing, significance, and interpretation, and recommend what to test next

- Insights and communication
- Present findings and recommendations to marketing leadership and the executive team in a clear, decision-ready way
- Partner with marketing, engineering, data engineering, finance, and product to align on definitions, attribution, and measurement standards
- Other duties as assigned

- Proven experience measuring email, direct mail, and digital marketing performance, including channel mix, budget allocation, CPM, CAC, ROAS, and conversion rate optimization
- Comfort writing and validating complex SQL against a cloud data warehouse (Snowflake preferred), with or without AI assistance. Data engineering is not part of this role.
- Working knowledge of attribution, marketing mix modeling, incrementality, and paid channel analysis
- Experience with scoring and predictive models, such as propensity models, marketing mix models, or Bayesian methods, and with applying them to real marketing decisions. Depth in at least one of these and a working understanding of the others.
- Working knowledge of tracking and instrumentation (UTMs, pixels, tag managers, event taxonomy) and of data modeling concepts such as facts and dimensions, enough to specify requirements and spot problems
- Solid understanding of A/B testing: experiment design, sample sizing, significance, and interpretation
- Experience using AI tools such as Claude in analysis and reporting workflows
- Excellent communication skills, with a track record of presenting analysis to senior leadership

Preferred

- Experience with SQL, Python or R for analysis

Cordance is dedicated to accelerating the growth of vertically focused business-to-business (B2B) software-as-a-service (SaaS) companies through acquisition and long-term tactical and financial guidance. We believe in elevating a company as it scales, delivering dignity to the organization and its employees, and sharing a passion for building a legacy.

Position Overview

We are seeking a strategic and results-driven Marketing Campaign Manager to lead the planning, execution, and optimization of integrated marketing campaigns across multiple business units within our Education Division. This role will act as the key liaison between each business unit and our external marketing agency to drive pipeline growth across the division’s portfolio of products and services.

Location: This role is open to candidates based in the Eastern U.S. time zone as a fully remote opportunity, with a preference for candidates based in or near Leeds, UK, where the role can be offered in a hybrid/remote capacity.

Key Responsibilities

Campaign Strategy & Planning

- Develop and lead comprehensive, multi-channel marketing campaigns aligned to business unit goals.

- Collaborate with business unit stakeholders to understand target audiences, value propositions, and key business priorities to inform marketing campaign strategy and messaging.

Execution & Project Management

- Manage end-to-end campaign execution, partnering with business unit functional teams and our external marketing agency.

- Own campaign timelines, deliverables, and budgets, ensuring on-time and high-quality execution.

Performance & Optimization

- Monitor and analyze campaign performance using marketing analytics tools and dashboards.

- Continuously test, optimize, and iterate based on data-driven insights to improve conversion rates and pipeline contribution.

Collaboration & Communication

- Partner closely with sales to ensure campaign alignment, support enablement, and accelerate opportunities.

- Communicate campaign plans, performance, and insights to key stakeholders across marketing and business leadership.

Competencies

- Strategic Execution: Able to translate business objectives into measurable marketing campaigns. Balances creative concepts with analytical rigor to ensure campaigns ladder up to pipeline, revenue, and brand goals. Demonstrates a strong understanding of audience segmentation and funnel dynamics.

- Analytical Decision-Making: Comfortable interpreting campaign data to identify patterns, draw insights, and recommend next steps. Skilled at using experimentation frameworks (A/B, multivariate, incrementality) to validate hypotheses and continuously improve performance.

- Operational Excellence: Drives campaigns from ideation through post-mortem with exceptional organization and attention to detail. Anticipates dependencies across channels, timelines, and stakeholders; maintains clear documentation and repeatable processes for scale.

- Communication and Collaboration: Communicates campaign goals, insights, and results clearly across marketing, sales, product, and leadership teams. Skilled in vendor and stakeholder management, ensuring alignment on deliverables, expectations, and optimization decisions.

- Agility and Growth Mindset: Thrives in dynamic environments. Rapidly adapts to performance trends, feedback, or market changes while maintaining focus on long-term objectives. Demonstrates curiosity and continuous learning in new platforms, tools, and testing methods.

You will move beyond traditional reporting to build a self-sustaining marketing ecosystem, leveraging Google BigQuery, Grafana, and agentic AI to create a unified source of truth and a culture of analytical rigor. Your mandate is to move the needle on demand generation across the entire marketing funnel, while raising the standard for how analytical work gets produced, challenged, and shipped across the org.

You will architect a dual-track target-setting framework that balances high-velocity top-of-funnel growth with deep-funnel quality, ensuring GTM resources are directed toward high-converting user cohorts optimized for Grafana adoption and long-term retention.

You will be expected to engineer the underlying data schemas, design predictive models, and implement the BI frameworks that shape our global GTM strategy. We are looking for a technical expert who can translate complex data into clear executive-level direction and who proactively builds systems that prevent AI-generated noise from drowning out actual signals.

What You'll Be Doing

- _Strategic GTM Partnership:_ Serve as the primary strategic partner to the GTM Leadership team (VP of Demand Gen, VP of Regional and Events, Head of Marketing Ops, CMO, Revenue Operations, Sales leadership and more), translating complex data into a clear roadmap for demand generation and revenue growth.

- _Predictive Modeling and ROI:_ Develop and maintain machine learning models (Attribution, MMM, LTV) to predict campaign impact and steer budget allocation toward the highest-ROI channels.
- _Data Warehouse Architecture:_ Oversee the structure of marketing data within Google BigQuery, ensuring a scalable single source of truth that connects product usage data with marketing touchpoints.
- _Causal Inference and Inflection Hunting:_ Move beyond descriptive analytics to perform causal inference and predictive trend analysis. When the data shows an anomaly, whether a 3-month spike, a regional dip, or a campaign that overperformed, isolate the window and dig in.
- _Executive Storytelling:_ Transform technical data outputs into clear, compelling narratives for the executive team and board. Deliver a succinct read and go deep where pushed.

Utilizing AI and Automation

- _Agentic Insights:_ Deploy LLM-powered agents (Claude Code, MCP-based tooling, or comparable) to monitor BigQuery datasets and automatically flag quality shifts in the funnel before they impact revenue.
- _Autonomous Workflows:_ Implement orchestration patterns (N8N, custom MCP servers, or equivalent) to build self-healing data pipelines and automated responses to market signals, such as automated spend shifts based on conversion anomalies.
- _Predictive Quality Scoring:_ Build and deploy AI-driven scoring models that separate high-value potential users from low-signal volume, helping Sales and Marketing prioritize effectively.

What Makes You a Great Fit

- 8+ years in Marketing Analytics, GTM Strategy, or Data Science, with at least 2 years in a lead architect capacity (IC track or player-coach; people management not required) within a high-growth SaaS or PLG environment.
- Demonstrated history as a force multiplier. You can point to specific tooling, rituals, evaluator systems, or frameworks you built that made other analysts or the broader org measurably better. A portfolio of dashboards you personally produced is not sufficient.
- Data Science and Engineering: Mastery of SQL and Python required. Deep experience architecting data environments in Google BigQuery, Snowflake, or similar warehouses.
- Hands-on AI fluency as a builder, not a user. You have built and shipped agentic systems with Claude Code, MCP, or comparable tools. You understand where LLMs fail and how to design around those limitations. You have built evaluator agents, prompt-grading systems, or analytical quality tooling in production.
- Automation Proficiency: Hands-on experience building complex logic and integrations using N8N, custom API orchestration, or MCP-based tooling.

- Strategic Acumen: Proven ability to create structure in highly ambiguous environments and build target-setting frameworks from scratch.
- MarTech Ecosystem: Deep familiarity with connectivity between Salesforce, marketing automation, and product-led data streams.
- Executive presence with experience presenting to executive and board audiences, including sound judgment about what data is and isn't ready to share up the chain.

Bonus Points For

- Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in a quantitative field (Data Science, CS, Statistics, Business Analytics). MBA or MS in Data Science is a significant plus.

The Senior Integrated Content Strategist, B2B owns the integrated content strategy for a portfolio of complex B2B accounts and sets the strategic direction and execution of deliverables. This role operates across the full integrated content ecosystem: thought leadership, sales enablement, lead magnets, whitepapers, research reports, one-sheeters, brochures, infographics, brand strategy, verbal identity, and messaging playbooks — all engineered to move a considered, multi-stakeholder buyer through a long B2B sales cycle. Senior Strategists build and defend content roadmaps directly with C-level stakeholders, translating pipeline and revenue goals into a clear content thesis that internal teams and client executives can rally behind. This is a strategist who thinks in systems: mapping content audits to the buyer journey, running audience research and stakeholder interviews to surface what actually moves a B2B deal forward, and adapting the roadmap as account performance and market signals shift. They bring product-level thinking to the content offering itself; proposing new formats and approaches before clients ask. They will also mentor and uplevel the strategists and writers who support their accounts. They are equally fluent identifying the single biggest content opportunity in a client's funnel and articulating why it matters in a room full of VPs and CMOs.

Key Responsibilities:

- Own end-to-end integrated content strategy and execution across thought leadership articles, sales enablement materials, lead magnets, whitepapers, research reports, one-sheeters, brochures, infographics, brand strategy, verbal identity, and messaging playbooks for a portfolio of B2B accounts
- Lead content audits mapped to the B2B buyer journey, using audience research, market analysis, and direct stakeholder and customer interviews to identify where content is and isn't driving pipeline
- Set the strategic direction for each account's content roadmap, aligning every deliverable to client revenue and pipeline goals rather than treating content as a standalone output
- Enhance and optimize business operations through the deployment of AI technologies
- Utilize and leverage Power Digital's nova ecosystem to benefit your department's objectives
- Ensure timely delivery of all Integrated Content workflows, maintaining 100% adherence to Power Digital's processes (Asana, Slack, Pulse)
- Proactively surface strategic insights and business-critical updates to both internal and client teams, positioning yourself as the point of authority on the account's content direction
- Stay ahead of B2B content marketing trends and AI-driven content practices, educating clients on recommended actions and future strategy
- Lead cross-functional content initiatives, coordinating with Paid Media, SEO/AEO, Creative, and Sales teams to ensure content strategy operates as the connective tissue across channels
- Independently manage a book of B2B client accounts, ensuring comprehensive strategic and operational coverage
- Execute 100% of Integrated Content deliverables with high accuracy and quality (no errors that would yield a negative impact to revenue for clients)
- Set informed content goals and forecasts based on historical client data and current audience needs, with the ability to adapt or re-forecast as market and account conditions shift
- Lead communication with internal and client teams including C-level stakeholders
- Power Circuit Completion & Adoption on applicable accounts
- On time for all deliverables & launches
- Other applicable or related duties as assigned.

Role Requirements:

- Minimum of 5 years of experience in a B2B Integrated Content Marketing role with direct client-facing experience, ideally supporting complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles
- A journalism or copywriting foundation is strongly preferred. This discipline underpins credible strategic recommendations and gives this person authority when writing or reviewing high-stakes B2B content

Remote - Brazil

Apply

Who We Are:

Power Digital is an AI-Native Growth Firm built at the intersection of world-class talent and proprietary technology. We help leading and emerging brands grow by combining deep vertical expertise, strategic thinking, and enterprise intelligence to drive measurable business outcomes.

For more than a decade, we have built our business around one belief: the best technology makes great people better. Our teams of strategists, creatives, analysts, and technologists use Omega, our AI operating system, to surface opportunities faster, investigate what is driving performance, and execute approved work with greater speed and precision. Behind Omega is Iris, our proprietary intelligence layer, built on years of real performance data, strategic frameworks, testing, and learnings from across our client portfolio. AI expands the capacity of our people to think, create, solve harder problems, and make better decisions. Human judgment, creativity, and accountability remain central to how we work.

As a people-first firm, we value diversity in backgrounds and experiences. We strongly believe our people and culture are key to our success. We partner closely with our clients as an extension of their teams, working across strategy, execution, and measurement to identify what is truly blocking growth and determine what to do next. Our culture is built on people who are curious, ambitious, accountable, and committed to delivering meaningful results for our clients and for one another.

At Power Digital, we believe the future belongs to teams that combine the best talent with the best technology. We are building that future today.

*Proficiency in spoken and written English at an advanced level is required for this role.

A day in the life:

The Senior Integrated Content Strategist, B2B owns the integrated content strategy for a portfolio of complex B2B accounts and sets the strategic direction and execution of deliverables. This role operates across the full integrated content ecosystem: thought leadership, sales enablement, lead magnets, whitepapers, research reports, one-sheeters, brochures, infographics, brand strategy, verbal identity, and messaging playbooks — all engineered to move a considered, multi-stakeholder buyer through a long B2B sales cycle. Senior Strategists build and defend content roadmaps directly with C-level stakeholders, translating pipeline and revenue goals into a clear content thesis that internal teams and client executives can rally behind. This is a strategist who thinks in systems: mapping content audits to the buyer journey, running audience research and stakeholder interviews to surface what actually moves a B2B deal forward, and adapting the roadmap as account performance and market signals shift. They bring product-level thinking to the content offering itself; proposing new formats and approaches before clients ask. They will also mentor and uplevel the strategists and writers who support their accounts. They are equally fluent identifying the single biggest content opportunity in a client's funnel and articulating why it matters in a room full of VPs and CMOs.

Key Responsibilities:

- Own end-to-end integrated content strategy and execution across thought leadership articles, sales enablement materials, lead magnets, whitepapers, research reports, one-sheeters, brochures, infographics, brand strategy, verbal identity, and messaging playbooks for a portfolio of B2B accounts
- Lead content audits mapped to the B2B buyer journey, using audience research, market analysis, and direct stakeholder and customer interviews to identify where content is and isn't driving pipeline
- Set the strategic direction for each account's content roadmap, aligning every deliverable to client revenue and pipeline goals rather than treating content as a standalone output
- Enhance and optimize business operations through the deployment of AI technologies
- Utilize and leverage Power Digital's nova ecosystem to benefit your department's objectives
- Ensure timely delivery of all Integrated Content workflows, maintaining 100% adherence to Power Digital's processes (Asana, Slack, Pulse)
- Proactively surface strategic insights and business-critical updates to both internal and client teams, positioning yourself as the point of authority on the account's content direction
- Stay ahead of B2B content marketing trends and AI-driven content practices, educating clients on recommended actions and future strategy
- Lead cross-functional content initiatives, coordinating with Paid Media, SEO/AEO, Creative, and Sales teams to ensure content strategy operates as the connective tissue across channels
- Independently manage a book of B2B client accounts, ensuring comprehensive strategic and operational coverage
- Execute 100% of Integrated Content deliverables with high accuracy and quality (no errors that would yield a negative impact to revenue for clients)
- Set informed content goals and forecasts based on historical client data and current audience needs, with the ability to adapt or re-forecast as market and account conditions shift
- Lead communication with internal and client teams including C-level stakeholders
- Power Circuit Completion & Adoption on applicable accounts
- On time for all deliverables & launches
- Other applicable or related duties as assigned.

Role Requirements:

- Minimum of 5 years of experience in a B2B Integrated Content Marketing role with direct client-facing experience, ideally supporting complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles
- A journalism or copywriting foundation is strongly preferred. This discipline underpins credible strategic recommendations and gives this person authority when writing or reviewing high-stakes B2B content
- Advanced understanding of data analysis and data visualization utilizing tools such as (but not limited to): HubSpot, Salesforce, GA4, Figma, or Unbounce
- Advanced, fluent proficiency with AI tools as a core part of the strategic workflow, specifically Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity — used for research, ideation, drafting, and content operations at scale
- Advanced knowledge of B2B Integrated Content strategy spanning thought leadership, lead magnets, sales enablement material, whitepapers, research reports, one-sheeters, brochures, brand website copy, sales and conversion-focused landing pages, and brand messaging, with a focus on aligning every deliverable to business goals and revenue priorities
- Demonstrated ability to set strategy including defining the content thesis for an account and defending it under scrutiny
- Exceptional time management, prioritization, and organizational skills for strategy planning, task delegation, and reviewing deliverables across a high-volume, high-complexity account load
- Ability to provide positive and constructive feedback to team members supporting on accounts, with proven experience training and upleveling other strategists or writers
- Proactive, solution-oriented problem solver with a team-player mentality and a bias toward original thinking over templated execution
- Exceptional presentation skills, with proven ability to present integrated content strategy and sales pitch presentations directly to C-suite executives, tailoring storytelling for the room and delivering actionable, defensible recommendations under executive scrutiny
- Forward-thinking, product-level perspective on the content offering itself; someone who proposes new formats, services, and approaches rather than only refining what already exists

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

- Client Book Revenue per Employee: $30k
- Client Retention: 90%
- Team Retention (of DRs if applicable): 90%
- Range of the number of accounts (8-12)

Most Important Things (MITs)

- Manage accounts with the highest workflow volume or complexity with positive feedback → primarily working on Enterprise and/or Growth accounts
- Deep literacy of the full B2B marketing funnel and buyer journey, and command of the role Integrated Content plays in moving multi-stakeholder deals through it
- Identifies the biggest Integrated Content opportunities based on client goals and pipeline priorities, and delivers a clear, defensible strategic roadmap for execution
- Working with the team to delegate Integrated Content tasks and receive them back with enough time to review so that you are always hitting deadlines in regards to client workflow with minimal errors (no typos, grammatical issues). Strong attention to detail with minimal review from Account Managers and Account Directors.

Benefits & Perks:

- Base salary paid in USD + commission opportunities
- Unlimited Time Off available on day one
- Fully flex work environment: full-remote, in-office, or hybrid
- Healthcare stipend: $50/month to support your healthcare or insurance costs
- National Holidays + 2 Mental Health Recharge Days per year
- Unlimited opportunities for growth & leadership within a rapidly growing firm
- Ongoing employee development programs for personal and professional growth (Hedgehog and Vital 5s)
- Quarterly awards including prize money and recognition for outstanding performance
- Opportunities to be involved in company DEI initiatives

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, and backgrounds, who strive to make an impact inside and outside of the workplace. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employees' points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility._

Prioritization matters more here because you can't fix everything at once, and trying to will burn both the client and the team.

- Help clients build measurement infrastructure from scratch when it doesn't exist, establish baselines before optimizing against them
- Coordinate paid, SEO, content, email, and creative work around a focused account strategy; scope management is part of the job
- Identify expansion opportunities that fit the client's stage, don't oversell services a brand isn't ready for
- Manage retention and expansion; lead renewals; grow MRR
- Build multi-threaded relationships with multiple layers of client contacts so no single point of contact departure puts an account at risk
- Ensure daily use of our proprietary technology (Iris and nova), Pulse (client performance and sentiment tool) cadence at 100%, and Power Circuit (our proprietary diagnostic system) compliance across managed ADs
- Manage and develop 1–2 direct reports — run regular 1:1s, build development plans, and own their performance reviews
- Coach analysts and specialists; many will be working with startups for the first time

- Has worked with founder-led businesses and understands the dynamic — decisions move fast, emotions run high, strategy and execution blur together
- Comfortable building from scratch: no brand guidelines, no historical data, no benchmark — and still making good decisions
- Understands crowdfunding-to-DTC transitions and what changes when a brand moves from Kickstarter momentum to sustainable acquisition
- Strong prioritization instincts — knows which problems to solve first and which to defer
- Comfortable with scrappy media mixes and knows how to get signal out of small budgets
- Track record of retaining and growing accounts, including accounts that went through rough patches

- Expansion to Churn Ratio (ETCR)
- Net MRR across portfolio
- Client NPS (8+ avg)
- Monthly Service Expansion pipeline generation
- Power Circuit Certification (annual)

As a Digital Marketing Manager at Array, you will be our in-house performance marketing engine — you do what a full-service agency would do, except you sit inside the GTM team, know our verticals, and are accountable to pipeline. This role reports to the Head of Marketing.

The role

You’re the person in the ad platforms, in the CMS, in the analytics. Every program you run has a goal attached: net new customers, retention, or land-and-expand. If it can’t be tied to one of those, it doesn’t run.

You will:

- Paid media — strategy and execution. Own Google Ads and LinkedIn end to end: account structure, budgets, bids, audiences, creative testing, and performance. Targeting aligned to our Tier 1/Tier 2 must-get accounts and five verticals. You build it, you run it, you hold the number.
- SEO and AI search — Build our organic program from a standing start: technical foundation, on-page work, keyword strategy mapped by vertical, and optimizing for how buyers actually search now (traditional rankings and AI/answer-engine visibility). You write the briefs; content production supports you.

- Landing pages and conversion — Own the conversion layer of the site: landing pages, A/B testing, form and funnel optimization, and our Qualified chatbot (routing through Salesforce). You own what converts.
- Measurement — Own tracking and reporting for everything above: UTM discipline, Salesforce campaign hygiene, and a pipeline-by-channel view.
- Work in the platforms daily. No vendor sits between you and the data.
- Report digital’s contribution to pipeline by vertical, in the same terms sales uses.
- Cut spend on programs that aren’t working, including the ones you built.
- Act on what you find the same week when able — a new audience, a rebuilt page, a tracking fix.
- Maintain a habit of using AI tools to think, build, and ship faster — it’s your default, not an afterthought.

Who you’ll work with

- Demand Gen, Sales and our Vertical Marketing Managers — your programs feed their pods, and account lists shape your targeting.
- Marketing Ops and RevOps — your partners on routing, attribution, and Salesforce campaign hygiene.

What great looks like

- 90 days in: you own paid spend end to end — accounts audited, broken campaigns rebuilt, underperforming spend cut. Baseline SEO is in place (technical audit, keyword map by vertical, first briefs out) and testing is running on the top conversion paths.
- 6 months in: leadership uses your pipeline dashboard in planning. Organic traffic is growing. Sales can point to deals that started with a program you ran.

You have:

- 5+ years running performance marketing hands-on for B2B, with real budget ownership — you’ve planned spend, defended it, and moved it when the data said to. Agency background is strongly welcome; you’ve run multiple client accounts and want to go deep on one.
- Platform fluency you can prove: Google Ads, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, GA4, Google Tag Manager, and a CRM/MAP stack (we run Salesforce and HubSpot; we also use, ZoomInfo, and Gong).
- Real SEO chops: you can run a technical audit, brief content, and explain search visibility — including AI search — to an executive without jargon.
- CRO experience with testing frameworks, not just hunches.
- A pipeline-first mindset: you talk in opportunities and revenue influenced, not just impressions.
- Strong project management and communication — you can run multiple campaigns and stakeholders at once with clear briefs, tight timelines, and no dropped threads.
- Comfort as a team of one with agency-sized scope — this is a build role in a fast-moving GTM org, and you’d rather own the whole engine than a slice of it.
- A belief that AI is reshaping work — you instinctively use it to accelerate everything you do: analysis, reporting, briefs, creative iteration. Our team builds this way; you should too.

Nice to have:

- Fintech experience or selling into financial institutions.
- ABM platform experience and tiered account strategy.
- Experience marketing embedded/API products or private label offerings.
- Background in growth, social, or partner marketing alongside paid — you’ve pulled more than one lever.
- Experience with behavioral and intent data for targeting (we use ZoomInfo intent).
- Enough design/creative sense to brief ad creative well.

Success means meeting defined performance standards through a six-month evaluation period — with continuous feedback and ongoing accountability as core parts of working at Array.

- Unlimited PTO and sick leave + 14 company holidays to encourage a healthy work-life blend

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara's Connected Operations platform helps organizations that depend on physical operations — fleets, construction, utilities, public works, and first responders — run safer, more efficiently, and more sustainably.

We're looking for a Group Manager, Product Marketing Manager, Public Sector to own the narrative, positioning, and enablement that will define how Samsara wins in government. You'll be the team's expert on how public sector buyers evaluate technology — from the contract vehicles they procure through, to the compliance bar they hold vendors to, to the mission outcomes they're ultimately accountable for.

This is a strategic, cross-functional role for someone who already understands government and frameworks like FedRAMP and StateRAMP/GovRAMP. The ideal candidate is someone who wants to build a public sector product marketing motion, not just execute inside one that already exists.

This is a remote position open to candidates based in the U.S. We prefer candidates based in or near Washington, D.C., or those able to work Eastern time zone hours.

You should apply if:

- You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your work will have real-world stakes — helping public agencies keep roads plowed, fleets safe, and essential services running for the communities they serve.
- You're fluent in how the government buys technology: You understand procurement cycles, contract vehicles, and compliance frameworks well enough to turn them into a go-to-market advantage rather than a blocker.
- You're energized by building, not just executing: Samsara's federal go-to-market motion is still being defined — you'll have real ownership over the frameworks, positioning, and playbooks that shape it.
- You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won't be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development.
- You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together, and support each other. You'll be surrounded by a high-caliber team that pushes you to do your best work.

In this role, you will:

- Lead as a player-coach: Manage a direct report while helping build the public sector PMM team's foundation — sharing in the strategic work, coaching for growth, and creating the frameworks that enable the function to scale.
- Own public sector positioning and messaging: Develop and evolve Samsara's core narrative for government buyers across federal, state, local, and education segments — grounded in mission outcomes rather than generic product benefits
- Build Samsara's federal go-to-market foundation: Partner cross-functionally to define how Samsara approaches the federal market, including messaging and enablement that reflect our compliance roadmap as it evolves
- Translate compliance into a sales advantage: Understand the FedRAMP authorization process and impact levels — deeply enough to explain it clearly to sales teams and prospects, and to inform internal conversations about authorization strategy and timing
- Drive product and platform launches for public sector: Localize Samsara's launches for a government audience, ensuring messaging reflects agency use cases, procurement realities, and compliance considerations
- Enable sales and channel teams: Build battlecards, objection-handling guides, RFP/RFI response content, and compliance-focused sales collateral that helps account teams and channel partners win competitive government deals
- Support competitive intelligence for public sector: Track how competitors position themselves to government buyers, and translate that intelligence into differentiated Samsara messaging and sales guidance
- Represent Samsara at public sector events and forums: Support flagship industry events and partner conferences with content, speaking support, and thought leadership

- 7+ years of product marketing (or closely related go-to-market) experience, with a meaningful portion of that focused on public sector / government technology marketing (B2G)
- Working knowledge of the FedRAMP authorization process, and general familiarity with adjacent compliance frameworks (e.g., StateRAMP/GovRAMP, NIST 800-53), with the ability to translate them into clear guidance for internal teams
- Proven ability to independently own strategic programs from conception to completion, and to influence cross-functional partners without direct authority
- Exceptional written and verbal communication skills — able to translate complex topics into clear, compelling narratives for technical and non-technical audiences alike
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

An ideal candidate also has:

- Experience managing a direct report or small team is strongly preferred
- Direct experience supporting a company through a FedRAMP or StateRAMP/GovRAMP authorization process
- Experience marketing connected devices, hardware-enabled, or physical-operations software platforms
- Prior experience in government or a public sector-focused vendor or agency role

- Experience building a public sector or new-market go-to-market motion from scratch — including positioning frameworks and playbooks designed to scale beyond your own work

Talkdesk competes in a market where the quality of execution separates companies that grow efficiently from those that spend more to get the same result. Marketing Operations is where that execution lives. This role exists to ensure that every dollar of marketing spend, every campaign, every event, and every account-based program translates into pipeline with zero friction. That requires a system built for precision where the right prospect reaches the right person at the right time, consistently and by design.

You sit inside the Marketing team, with close partnerships across Sales and RevOps. The marketers running campaigns, events, and account-based programs are your primary stakeholders. When the system works, their work converts.

In practice, that means owning the full operational surface of marketing technology: administering and continuously improving the tools that make up our GTM stack, building and maintaining the integrations that keep data moving cleanly between systems, designing the orchestrations that automate account and contact engagement, ensuring the enrichment and data integrity standards that make every downstream decision reliable. This is an interdependent system, and this person keeps it running as a coherent, high-performing whole.

What You'll Own

- Account-Based Marketing Orchestration: Serve as the technical owner of our ABM orchestration layer. Translate signals from our intent platform into automated, sequenced actions across our marketing automation platform and CRM, working closely with campaign and field marketing teams to ensure the right programs reach the right accounts at the right moment. Getting this infrastructure right is one of the highest-impact contributions this role makes to the business.

- Marketing Technology Foundation: Own the day-to-day health of our martech systems and the workflows, API calls, integrations, and syncs that connect them to keep prospect data moving accurately through the funnel. When something breaks or underperforms, you diagnose it, fix it, and document the resolution so it does not recur.

- Agentic AI Workflow Engineering: Design and build automated workflows that use AI capabilities to evaluate qualitative signals, such as demo request notes, intent activity, and unstructured form inputs, alongside firmographic data to produce dynamic lead scores and routing decisions. You write the API calls, design the orchestration logic, test against edge cases, and iterate based on conversion outcomes. Experience shipping something to production is the bar.

- Enrichment and Insights: Build and manage the workflows that construct a complete, account-level intelligence profile from the moment a prospect engages. That means aggregating first-party behavioral signals, third-party intent data, firmographic context, and web research into a unified view that captures not just the individual contact but the broader buying committee: who across the account is engaging, with what content, and what their activity suggests about organizational priorities and pain points. That intelligence surfaces in the systems where sales and marketing work, so every follow-up is informed, relevant, and timed to the account's buying journey.

- System Documentation and Enablement: Every workflow you build or modify gets documented: field mapping dictionaries, AI orchestration logic, routing rule change logs. Beyond documentation, you actively invest in making the marketing team more self-sufficient, building self-service reporting and dashboards that allow marketers to check campaign performance, list quality, or lead status independently, and creating resources that allow colleagues to troubleshoot routine tasks and leverage AI tools without filing a request. An empowered marketing team operates with greater speed and confidence, and this role contributes meaningfully to that outcome.

Who You Are

You operate with a high degree of autonomy. You are embedded in the relevant standups, attentive to system performance, and typically ahead of issues before they surface as escalations. Your manager will set context and priorities; the execution is yours to own.

You are invested in the success of the Marketing team. You understand that the campaigns, events, and programs your colleagues execute are only as effective as the systems that support them. Leads from a field event that go unrouted, an ABM sequence that executes against incomplete data, or a high-intent inbound request that experiences significant delay before reaching an SDR all represent measurable pipeline impact. You approach your work with that accountability in mind.

You are technically strong and collaborative by nature. Marketers, Sales and RevOps are close partners. You understand their workflows well enough to anticipate where system gaps will affect their work, and communicate clearly when something is broken, when it is fixed, and why. Strong cross-functional relationships are central to this role.

You see the work through to completion. You build, test, document, and close the loop. When something you own regresses, you identify it first.

What We're Looking For

_Required_

- 3 to 5 years in B2B SaaS Marketing Operations, Revenue Operations, or a systems-adjacent role
- Hands-on marketing automation and CRM administration, including configuring and maintaining MAP-to-CRM syncs
- Demonstrated ability to build and deploy an automated workflow that calls external APIs, whether webhooks, REST APIs, or LLM endpoints, in a production environment
- Native fluency in B2B funnel mechanics: MQL definitions, lifecycle stage transitions, opportunity lifecycles, and attribution models
- Experience coaching or enabling non-technical stakeholders on new tools, AI workflows, or self-service reporting

_Strong Signal_

- Hands-on administrative experience with intent data platforms, routing engines, and ABM orchestration
- Prior experience building LLM-powered workflows for lead scoring, routing, or qualification
- Comfort reading and writing JSON, working with REST APIs, and debugging integration errors independently

How We'll Measure Success

The through-line across all of it is pipeline efficiency: more of the right prospects converting into pipeline from the programs already running, with less manual intervention and less fallout.

_30 days:_ Full audit of marketing automation-to-CRM field mapping is complete, ownership of inbound routing rules is established, and current ABM workflow patterns are mapped to identify key automation opportunities.

_60 days:_ First agentic AI workflow is deployed to staging or production. At least one major ABM orchestration sequence that previously required manual steps is automated. An initial self-service enablement resource or dashboard is delivered to the marketing team.

_90 days and beyond:_ Lead sync exception rate is at target with a monitoring process that catches regressions before Sales does. ABM orchestration operates as a reliable service layer that campaign and field marketers can brief and trust to execute. Marketing colleagues actively leverage self-service tools and AI workflows independently.

_Required with your resume (200 words max):_

A high-intent prospect submits a demo request but never reaches the assigned SDR in the CRM. Walk us through your exact diagnostic process: which logs you check first, how you trace the break across the marketing automation-to-CRM sync and inbound routing rules, how you validate the fix, and how you would design an agentic step to evaluate the prospect's form submission notes for priority routing.

- Clear, direct communication; you can explain campaign performance simply and confidently to your team.

- Experience marketing to legal, professional services, or another trust-driven vertical.
