The Opportunity

Grafana's Demand Generation team creates and accelerates pipeline across the full customer journey. We run a modern, AI-forward operation: lifecycle email programs driven by an AI engine, territory-level buying signals surfaced directly to sales leaders, and agentic workflows that handle work that used to take teams of specialists.

Our webinar program is one of the highest-leverage things we run: technical, practitioner-first sessions on a weekly cadence across AMER, EMEA, APAC and LATAM, putting the product in front of the people who would actually use it. Hands-on sessions, not sales pitches.

We're hiring a Webinar Program Manager to own it. This is a specialist seat, not a generalist one. You'll inherit an established program with a documented process and a full handover from the person who built it, and you'll own the operating rhythm from there: the calendar, the presenters, the build and promotion of every session, the follow-up, and the reporting.

This is not a "run the playbook" role. Sessions run in parallel at a pace no one could manage by hand, so the way to raise quality is to keep automating the mechanics. We expect this person to build with AI as a default and treat automation as a first-class deliverable, not a side project.

You'd be joining a demand gen team that is genuinely rebuilding how the function works, where AI agents run real production programs and the people on the team design the machine rather than turn the crank. What You'll Be Doing

- Own the webinar calendar end to end. Presenter booking, registration pages, campaign setup, promotion, live delivery, follow-up, and the flip to on-demand, across multiple regions and time zones.
- Keep sessions practitioner-first. Brief technical presenters, shape the outline, and keep a session useful to the audience that registered for it.
- Bring data to topic planning. Use past performance and downstream pipeline quality to recommend what we run and what we retire, and lock the plan with demand gen and product marketing each quarter.
- Automate the production line. Extend the automation behind session setup and promotion, and keep pushing into the parts of the process a person shouldn't be doing by hand, including repurposing recordings into other content.
- Report on what happens after the session. Registrations are the input. Connect sessions to product adoption and pipeline, report it honestly, and flag what isn't producing.
- Grow the program's reach. Expand into additional languages and formats where the numbers justify it.

What Makes You a Great Fit

- 4+ years in demand generation, event marketing, or lifecycle marketing at a B2B software company (open source or developer-focused a plus).
- Hands-on ownership of a recurring webinar or virtual event calendar across multiple regions. A cadence you were accountable for hitting, not a handful of one-off sessions.
- Hands-on with a webinar platform (ON24, Zoom Webinars, Contrast, Goldcast or similar) and the plumbing behind it: CRM campaigns, registration sync, attendance data, follow-up triggers.
- Comfortable working with technical presenters. You can brief an engineer or solutions architect and hold the line on what the audience came for.
- Hands-on with AI in your actual work: you've built automations or agentic workflows (or are visibly on that path), and you think about AI as leverage, not a threat or a buzzword.
- Comfortable with data: you can pull your own numbers, sanity-check them, and build a program readout a VP would trust.
- Strong program management fundamentals. Twenty-plus moving pieces at once is a logistics job before it's a marketing job, and you ship on time without needing a coordinator.

Bonus Points For

- Content repurposing at scale: clips, blog, social, on-demand libraries.
- Localized program experience, and a view on when translation earns its cost.
- Familiarity with the observability, monitoring or open source ecosystem.
- Customer.io, Salesforce and a modern data stack (BigQuery or similar).

Senior Growth Marketing Manager, Lifecycle

Remote US

Apply

About Ethos

Ethos (Nasdaq: $LIFE) is a leading life insurance technology company on a mission to protect families by democratizing access to life insurance and empowering agents at scale. With its robust three-sided technology platform, Ethos is transforming the life insurance experience for consumers, agents, and carriers alike. Ethos offers instant, accessible products and a seamless online process that requires no medical exams and just a few health questions; it eliminates traditional barriers, making it easier than ever for everyone to protect their families. Ethos is redefining how life insurance is bought, sold, and underwritten.

About the role

We are seeking a data-obsessed, US-based Senior Growth Marketing Manager to own the lifecycle across three distinct customer journeys: converting prospects into customers, expanding existing customers through cross-sell and upsell, and scaling a recently launched product line. The through-line is conversion, retention, and maximizing long-term customer value (LTV).

These three journeys work differently, and that's the interesting part of the job. Prospect-to-customer conversion is a blend of self-serve digital and human follow-up — live agents and voice AI — so your job is to design what gets said, to whom, and when, so that confidence keeps building in the gaps between conversations. Cross-sell, upsell, and the new product line are entirely self-serve. There is no human in the loop, which means the messaging, the timing, and the on-page experience have to carry the entire decision on their own.

Life insurance is a high-consideration purchase, so lack of trust and product understanding are the biggest drivers of drop-off. Across all three journeys, you own the connective tissue that moves someone from "a company I found on the internet" to "a company I trust to safeguard my future." You will operate on shared OKRs with the product managers who own each of these three areas, and — for the conversion journey — in close working partnership with Sales leadership, agents, and our voice AI team. You need to know what's actually landing on live calls, not just what performs in an inbox.

Duties and Responsibilities:

- Own the Lifecycle Strategy and Messaging. Design the narrative, cadence, and channel mix that carries someone from first touch to funded policy, from first policy to second, and from early interest in a new product line to scaled adoption. You set the strategy and you build it.
- Convert Prospects into Customers. Own the post-lead journey where self-serve and human touch meet. Build the digital nurture that moves people forward on their own, and build the follow-up content, sequences, and talking points that make every agent and voice AI conversation land — the right articles, proof points, or next steps that can go out within minutes of a call ending, and a system that gets smarter over time rather than sending the same packet to everyone.
- Drive Cross-Sell and Upsell. Existing customers are our highest-intent audience and this motion is fully self-serve. Own identifying the right next product for the right customer at the right moment — additional coverage, product upgrades, a second policy for a spouse — and build the triggered messaging, on-page experiences, and offer structures that get them there without a human touch.
- Scale a Recently Launched Product Line. We have a new product line in market and the mandate is growth. Own its self-serve lifecycle end to end: activation, onboarding, and the messaging that turns early traction into a repeatable, scaling funnel. This is 0→1 becoming 1→10, with the ambiguity and speed that implies.
- Own Retention and LTV. Getting someone to buy is the beginning, not the end. Own the post-purchase journey that keeps policies in force and customers engaged, and be accountable for LTV as a number you move, not a metric you report.
- Build Trust Signals Across the Funnel. Partner with Marketing and Product on the things that actually move a high-consideration financial decision: credibility and social proof, carrier proof points, reviews, and transparency about what someone is actually buying.
- Own the Data Behind Conversion and Drop-Off. Be the expert on cohorts and funnel curves across all three areas. Pull your own data to find exactly where trust and momentum break down, not just where a campaign underperforms — then turn that into a concrete hypothesis and test it.
- Run Experiments End to End. Test messaging, cadence, offers, and channel mix; report on statistical significance; roll out what wins.
- Cross-Functional Ownership. Operate on shared OKRs with the product managers across all three areas, and in a real working relationship with Sales leadership on the conversion journey. Decisions get made, ownership is felt, and campaigns don't stall because nobody knows who's driving.
- Scope. Your time splits across all three journeys with the weighting shifting as each area matures.

Qualifications and Skills:

- 6+ Years of Experience. Senior-level track record in Lifecycle, Growth Marketing, or CRM at a B2C Tech, FinTech, Insurtech, or Marketplace company. Higher-consideration / higher-AOV product experience strongly preferred.
- Copywriting and Messaging Strategy. You can write subject lines that get opened and body copy that drives action — and you know how to build trust and clarity into a high-consideration financial decision, not just optimize for clicks.
- Self-Serve Conversion Instincts. You've moved customers through a purchase decision with no human in the loop and you know what that demands: the messaging, the timing, and the on-page experience all have to do the persuading.
- Comfortable Partnering with a Sales Org. For the conversion journey, you want to know what's actually said on a live call, and you can translate that into content and tools that make agents and voice AI more effective — not assets built in isolation from what's happening in the field.
- Multi-Channel Mindset. You think natively across email, SMS, voice / conversational AI, in-product, on-page, and human-delivered follow-up. You do not believe email is the center of the universe.
- Analytical Mindset. Fluent in cohort retention, statistical significance, and LTV. Ability to self service data pulls/queries to find where trust and momentum break down in the funnel.
- Technical CRM Proficiency. Hands-on expertise with enterprise marketing automation tools (e.g., Braze, Iterable, Customer.io, HubSpot, or similar).
- PM Collaboration. You've worked on a shared goal / OKR with a PM before and have a strong sense of when to lead, when to follow, and how to drive decisions across a cross-functional team. Here you'll do it with several PMs at once.

Cresta unlocks the true potential of the customer experience, turning every conversation into a competitive advantage. Cresta’s unified AI platform combines conversational AI agents, real-time human agent augmentation, and comprehensive conversation intelligence to drive revenue and efficiency gains across every channel. The world’s leading companies, including United Airlines, Cox Communications, and Marriott, use Cresta to power world-class customer experiences every day.

Over the next few years, AI is going to redefine how people all over the world interact with businesses every day. Come build that future at Cresta.

Role Overview

Cresta is looking for a Growth Marketing Manager who thrives on creativity, innovation, analytical rigor, and strategic thinking, not someone looking to run an existing playbook. This role happens to live in paid and digital (LinkedIn Ads, Meta Ads, Google Ads), but the job is to build and own a growth thesis, not to babysit ad accounts. We care more about your ability to reason from first principles and move fast than about whether you've spent years in a specific channel. If you come from a demanding, analytical field such as investment banking, consulting, or a technical or quantitative discipline, and you're hungry to build a career in growth marketing, we want to hear from you.

Responsibilities

- Own the pipeline and acquisition number for your channels and decide what to double down on and what to pull back.
- Build a growth thesis for our paid and digital mix from first principles, and bring new bets to the table rather than waiting to be told where to focus.
- Lead paid social across LinkedIn and Meta Ads and a focused paid search program alongside it.
- Partner with our brand designer on ad creative, pushing the quality bar and staying current on what's working.
- Monitor campaign pacing against budget and pipeline goals, flagging issues proactively and knowing when to kill something versus double down.
- Leverage AI tools and audience enrichment platforms (including Clay) to build precise targeting, automate workflows, and drive output at a lean-team scale.
- Collaborate cross-functionally with demand generation, content, creative, sales, etc.

Qualifications

- A track record of excellence in a demanding, analytical field such as investment banking, consulting, biz ops, a co-founder or early startup builder background, or a technical or quantitative discipline (econ, stats, math, or similar), with genuine interest in growth marketing. - Quantitative fluency; a math-first brain that reasons about performance from the data.
- Demonstrated creativity and original thinking: evidence you generate ideas rather than default to convention.
- Strategic mindset: able to connect day-to-day execution to broader business goals, and a sense of ownership over the number, not just the tasks.
- High motor with a hunger to learn. Actively experiments with AI tools and brings new ideas to the team.
- Excellent communication skills; able to synthesize performance data into clear, stakeholder-ready updates.

Nice to have (not expected on day one)

- Exposure to any paid advertising platform (LinkedIn, Google, Meta, or otherwise).
- Familiarity with CRM or marketing automation tools such as Salesforce or HubSpot.
- Experience with data or audience tools such as Clay.

About this position:

We're looking for a VP of Growth Marketing to own the marketing to revenue generation engine. This is a player-coach role: you'll lead a team of 12+ product marketers, marketing channel experts, and growth marketers, owning product marketing for both our brand and creator audiences and, on the growth side, paid media, SEO/AEO, email and in-app lifecycle, CRO and web, and ABM. You'll also carry work yourself, building the model, writing the brief, reading the attribution, and stepping directly into a channel when it needs a senior operator. You'll own the growth marketing budget and be accountable for driving measurable action across the full customer journey, acquisition, retention, expansion, and reactivation, and for pipeline, signups, and revenue across all three lines of business (Later Influence, Later Social, and Creator/Affiliate). You'll partner closely with Sales, Product, Product Marketing, RevOps, and Web, and you'll have regular exposure to executive leadership. This role is ideally a hybrid position with 3 days in office in our Boston or New York hubs, but remote applicants are considered.

What you'll be doing:

Growth strategy and ownership

- Own Later's growth marketing strategy end to end, connecting product marketing, demand generation, and lifecycle into one plan tied to pipeline and revenue targets.
- Own and allocate the growth marketing budget across channels, defending investment decisions with clear efficiency, payback math, and investment increase recommendations.
- Work with your Growth Marketing Managers to establish and refine the goals, KPIs, and reporting frameworks the function is measured on, and make the tradeoffs visible to senior leadership and executive teams.
- Refine and build net new differentiated growth motions for each line of business, recognizing that enterprise SLG, self-serve social signups, and creator acquisition do not respond to the same playbook.
- Set the annual and quarterly planning rhythm for the team, and connect it to the broader marketing calendar.

Team leadership

- Lead, coach, and develop a team of roughly a dozen marketers across three groups: product marketing, digital marketing channel experts, and growth marketers.
- Set clear ownership and success criteria for each person so channel specialists and segment-facing marketers pull in the same direction.
- Raise the technical bar of the team on measurement, experimentation, and marketing technology.
- Make thoughtful hiring and structure decisions as the org evolves, including new roles.
- Create a culture of testing and learning where a failed experiment with a clean read is treated as a win.
- Make AI a working part of how the team operates, setting the standard for where it accelerates research, campaign analysis, and lifecycle personalization, and where it doesn't, so the team ships more efficiently without lowering the bar.
- Work as a player-coach: own a channel or program directly when the team has a gap, and stay current enough in the tools that your feedback is specific rather than directional.

Channel and campaign execution

- Direct paid media strategy across paid social, paid search, video, and display, holding the team accountable to efficiency targets.
- Guide SEO and AEO strategy as search shifts toward AI answer engines, protecting and growing Later's organic visibility.
- Own strategy across email and in-app for both brand and creator audiences, driving signup to paid conversion, activation, and retention.
- Drive conversion rate optimization and web strategy in partnership with Web and Product, treating later.com as a performance surface rather than a brochure.
- Partner with the ABM and enterprise marketers to optimize existing and build net-new account-based programs that Sales actually uses, with a clean handoff and a shared definition of a qualified lead.
- Partner with the creator sales team to optimize existing and build net-new ABM motions for mid to top tier creators
- Ensure brand and product marketing work reinforces demand rather than running parallel to it.

Measurement and experimentation

- Own attribution and marketing measurement in partnership with RevOps and MarketingOps, and continuously improve the accuracy of multi-channel impact.
- Lead a quarterly testing roadmap tied to specific business metrics, with documented hypotheses, test design, and results.
- Go deep on campaign and ad group performance while also summarizing clearly for an executive audience.
- Ensure data flows cleanly between CRM, marketing automation, and analytics tools so decisions rest on numbers the team trusts.
- Optimize our always on conversion funnel for each line of business. Proactively identify and close gaps in the funnel.

Cross-functional partnership

- Partner with Sales and RevOps on pipeline targets, lead quality, routing, and a seamless handoff process.
- Work with Product and Product Marketing so campaigns reflect real product capability and land in step with launches.
- Collaborate with the Creator team so creator acquisition and education programs feed the same growth model as brand demand.
- Represent growth marketing performance to senior leadership with clarity about what is working, what is not, and what you are changing.

What you bring:

- 10+ years in growth, demand generation, or performance marketing, with experience owning a multi-million dollar budget and a revenue number.
- 5+ years leading and developing marketing teams, including managing managers or senior specialists through ambiguity and change.
- A genuine player-coach: you've led a team and personally owned execution at the same time, and you're still close enough to the tools to build the model or run the campaign yourself.
- Depth in paid media, SEO and AEO, lifecycle and email, and web CRO
- Proven track record building and scaling demand in B2B SaaS, PLG, or marketplace environments, ideally with both enterprise and self-serve motions.
- Strong command of measurement: attribution modeling, experiment design, and funnel analysis, with comfort in tools such as GA4, Amplitude, Looker, or Mode.
- Experience with CRM and marketing automation platforms (for example Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Klaviyo, Iterable, or Braze).
- Clear, direct communication with both a working team and an executive audience, including the ability to defend a plan and change your mind on evidence.
- Experience marketing to or through creators, or in the social, influencer, or commerce space, is a bonus.
- Experience partnering closely with Sales on ABM or enterprise pipeline is a bonus.

How you work:

- Driven by Impact: You deliver results that matter—prioritizing high-value work, meeting deadlines, and adapting quickly while keeping outcomes clear.
- Strategic & Customer-Centric: You anticipate risks and opportunities, connect decisions to long-term growth, and build trust through proactive insights.
- Curious & Growth-Oriented: You seek knowledge, ask sharp questions, and apply learnings fast—challenging the status quo with a mindset of improvement.
- Collaborative & Resilient: You thrive in change by staying resourceful, solution-focused, and positive—removing roadblocks, sharing insights, and keeping morale high.
- Accountable & Honest: You own your work, hold yourself and others to a high bar, and use transparent feedback to drive growth.
- Emotionally Intelligent: You build trust through empathy and collaboration, foster inclusion, and inspire others with grit, optimism, and integrity.

Our approach to compensation:

We leverage data from trusted third-party compensation sources to help us understand the market value of a role based on function, level, geographic location, and scope. We evaluate compensation bi-annually, including performance and market-related factors.

As Senior Director of Brand, you own how Fleetio looks, sounds, and shows up — everywhere. Our visual identity. Our editorial voice. Our social presence and video work. Our earned media. - Brand system and creative. Visual identity, creative direction, and design standards across web, campaign, product surfaces, events, and sponsorship — the system that makes Fleetio recognizable in a category where most brands look interchangeable.

What is a day in the life of a Senior Paid Media Manager?

- Set up and launch paid campaigns primarily across TikTok DTC and TikTok Shop, with additional support on Meta (Facebook/Instagram), aligned with brand objectives and target audiences.

- Develop and brief ad creatives (video assets, UGC-style content, copy, calls-to-action) built first for TikTok's platform, trends, and native formats — with Meta adaptations as needed.

- Optimize live campaigns to maximize ROI by adjusting targeting, creatives, bids, and placements across TikTok and Meta.

- Monitor daily performance metrics such as CPM, CPC, CPA, ROAS, and engagement rates at both the platform and account level.

- Conduct A/B testing on creatives, audiences, offers, and campaign structures — with a focus on TikTok's unique testing environment.

- Produce regular performance reports with insights and recommendations spanning TikTok Shop, TikTok DTC, and Meta.

- Coordinate with creative and content teams to maintain a constant pipeline of TikTok-native assets and Meta-ready formats.

- Stay ahead of TikTok platform updates, algorithm changes, new ad solutions, and shopping features, while keeping a working knowledge of Meta developments.

- Troubleshoot tracking, set up conversion events, and maintain pixel health across TikTok Pixel and Meta Pixel/CAPI.

- Manage budgets and pacing across channels to ensure campaigns stay within spend targets and hit efficiency goals.

What will I need to thrive in this role?

- Minimum 4-6 years' experience managing TikTok Ads campaigns; Meta experience is a plus but not the primary focus.

- Strong, hands-on knowledge of TikTok Ads Manager and TikTok Shop ad formats — In-Feed, Spark Ads, TopView, GMVmax, and more.

- Working familiarity with Meta Ads Manager and core formats

- In-depth knowledge of TikTok-specific audience targeting, bidding strategies, and campaign optimization; solid foundational understanding of the same on Meta.

- Creative mindset with an intuition for what performs natively on TikTok — short-form video, trending sounds, authentic storytelling.

- Familiarity with pixel setup, server-side tracking, and attribution best practices across TikTok and Meta

- Experience with budget management, pacing, and multi-channel reporting.

- Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

What does high performance look like?

- TikTok campaigns — across both DTC and Shop — consistently achieve or exceed KPIs for ROAS, CPA, GMV, and engagement.

- Meta campaigns are managed efficiently and support broader brand performance goals.

- Proactive and timely execution of campaign launches, creative refreshes, and optimizations, particularly within TikTok's faster-moving environment.

- Data-driven recommendations surfaced regularly to internal teams and brand partners, with TikTok insights leading the narrative.

- Consistent adoption and testing of new TikTok ad formats, Shop features, and beta opportunities, with Meta learnings incorporated where relevant.

What is my potential for career growth?

At Pattern, we are committed to employee development and recognize high performance. In this role, you will develop deep expertise in TikTok's commerce and paid social ecosystem — one of the fastest-growing areas in digital marketing — while building well-rounded paid media experience through Meta. Advancement may include progression to senior management, a specialized TikTok Shop or Paid Social lead role, or cross-functional opportunities within Pattern. You will have access to professional development resources, mentorship, and regular feedback to help guide your path.

What does success look like in the first 30, 60, 90 days?

First 30 days: Learn Pattern's systems, platforms, and workflows. Get fully oriented across active TikTok and Meta campaigns, accounts, and reporting cadences. Build relationships with your team, creative partners, and brand contacts.

First 60 days: Take ownership of day-to-day campaign management, optimization, and reporting — with a focus on TikTok DTC and TikTok Shop. Contribute to creative briefs and begin making data-driven recommendations for improvement across channels.

First 90 days: Independently manage campaigns end-to-end, with TikTok as your primary channel and Meta as a strong secondary. Consistently deliver on KPIs, bring forward new ideas for TikTok strategy or platform features, and be recognized as a reliable partner by your peers and brand contacts.

What is the team like?

- You will work alongside other TikTok Shop and Paid Social managers and be supervised by the Associate Director, Paid Social & Creative Strategy, with mentorship from the Head of Accounts for TikTok Shop. This is a data-driven, results-oriented team with a strong TikTok-first mindset. Collaboration is built into the workflow — you'll regularly partner with creative, analytics, and account teams to drive results, and your ideas and input are actively encouraged.

Sounds great! What's the company culture?

- Game Changers- A game changer is someone who looks at problems with an open mind and shares new ideas with team members, regularly reassesses existing plans and attaches a realistic timeline to goals, makes profitable, productive, and innovative contributions, and actively pursues improvements to Pattern's processes and outcomes.
- Data Fanatics- A data fanatic is someone who recognizes problems and seeks to understand them through data, draws unbiased conclusions based on data that lead to actionable solutions, and continues to track the effects of the solutions using data.
- Partner Obsessed- An individual who is partner obsessed clearly explains the status of projects to partners and relies on constructive feedback, actively listens to partner's expectations, and delivers results that exceed them, prioritizes the needs of your partners, and takes the time to create a personable experience for those interacting with Pattern.
- Team of Doers- Someone who is a part of a team of doers uplifts team members and recognizes their specific contributions, takes initiative to help in any circumstance, actively contributes to supporting improvements, and holds themselves accountable to the team as well as to partners.

What is the hiring process?

- Initial phone interview with Pattern's talent acquisition team
- Video interview with a hiring manager
- Onsite interview with a panel of department leaders
- Professional reference checks
- Executive review
- Offer

How can I stand out as an applicant?

- Discuss professional accomplishments with specific data to quantify examples
- Provide insights on how you can add value and be the best addition to the team
- Focus on mentioning how you would be partner obsessed at Pattern
- Share experience on any side projects related to data and analytics

Why should I work at Pattern?

Pattern offers big opportunities to make a difference in the ecommerce industry! We are a company full of talented people that evolves quickly and often. We set big goals, work tirelessly to achieve them, and we love our Pattern community. We also believe in having fun and balancing our lives, so we offer awesome benefits that include:

- Unlimited PTO

- Paid Holidays

We are looking for a Senior Director, Demand Generation & ABM to build and scale the signal-based, full-funnel engine that drives pipeline, bookings, and revenue for Pattern. You’ll own the demand strategy across target account identification, awareness, engagement, conversion, and post-sale expansion—bringing together paid media, outbound, content, events, lifecycle marketing, and AI-powered tactics into one cohesive motion. This is a full-time role and will work a hybrid schedule based in Lehi, UT.

The Role

- Demand Generation and ABM at Pattern is a signal-based function responsible for the full demand funnel and account lifecycle—from target account identification and awareness through engagement, conversion, and post-sale expansion. This is a full-funnel mandate focused on building pipeline and revenue, not simply generating leads.
- Success in the role will be measured by both the bookings directly sourced by marketing and the bookings marketing influences throughout the buying journey. Because Pattern’s deals often involve multiple channels and stakeholders before closing, the role requires a leader who can connect those touchpoints into a cohesive demand strategy and clearly demonstrate their impact on pipeline and revenue.

What will I need to thrive in this role?

- 15+ years of experience in digital and demand marketing, including 8+ years leading strategy and teams
- Proven experience scaling paid media programs profitably and managing multi-million-dollar budgets across multiple channels
- Experience developing multi-channel campaigns across email, content, events, outbound, and ABM, including complex, multi-stakeholder buying committees
- Proven experience developing lead scoring and lifecycle/nurture programs and driving pipeline velocity
- Strong experience with marketing analytics, attribution, and data-driven budget management
- Experience with Salesforce, Marketo, and BI/reporting platforms, including building and validating lead scoring models
- Experience applying AI and machine learning to marketing, including campaign optimization, personalization, predictive targeting, and creative production
- Proven experience partnering with Sales, RevOps, Product, and Finance, including shared ownership of marketing budgets and go-to-market strategy
- Prior accountability for marketing efficiency, ROI, and/or marketing-sourced and influenced pipeline
- Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience

What You'll Own:

- Account strategy and lead scoring. Own the ideal customer profile and target account universe, and sharpen the lead scoring model beneath Pattern's existing tiered account lists against real conversion and close behavior.

- Full funnel orchestration. Run signal based programs across every stage of the demand funnel, target account identification, top of funnel awareness, mid funnel engagement, bottom of funnel conversion, and post sale expansion, coordinating paid, outbound, content, and events into one motion rather than disconnected touches.

- Lifecycle marketing. Build and continually refresh an always on nurture motion across every channel, including email, so prospects and customers keep moving between active campaigns.

- Sales alignment and enablement. Own the operating cadence with the sales team: shared account lists, handoff SLAs, and joint ownership of go to market strategy. Partner with sales to plan and deliver content matched to every stage of the sales cycle, from early education through late stage proof points, so reps always have the right asset to move a deal forward.

- Attribution and budget partnership. Maintain a defensible, auditable view of what spend produces (anchored in Salesforce and Marketo), quantify the bookings marketing sources and influences, and partner directly with the CMO on building, defending, and reallocating the department budget.

- Team leadership. Manage a paid media manager, a team of demand and integrated marketing managers, and a lifecycle marketing manager, all against an efficiency target rather than a flat activity budget. You'll also be asked to build out an autonomous AI layer across the function.

- Martech and AI partnership. Partner with Marketing Technology leadership on the tools and AI systems the team runs on, setting the standard for how the team uses AI without compromising brand judgment or data integrity.

How You Lead:

- Move fluidly between executive level strategy and the operational detail of a single campaign, closing that gap personally.
- Ground strategy in qualitative signal, sales calls, win and loss themes, account feedback, not only dashboards.
- Build cross functional trust by understanding sales and finance priorities first, rather than negotiating from separate camps.
- Have already owned a hard efficiency or ROI target in front of leadership, not just an activity or awareness target.
- Can point to a motion you already rebuilt in response to new tooling or buyer behavior.

How We'll Measure Success:

- Marketing sourced and marketing influenced bookings growth against target
- Pipeline velocity and win rate for target accounts relative to non target accounts
- Expansion revenue within the target account universe, not only new logo acquisition
- Attribution accuracy and auditability
- Lead scoring model accuracy against actual pipeline and win outcomes
- Lifecycle and nurture engagement across channels, including email
- Department budget performance against the CMO's plan

About the Role

TurFresh is looking for a hands-on Growth & Marketing Operations Manager to improve marketing performance across multiple markets.

You will work closely with John and the President/General Manager, who will provide strategic guidance and feedback. You will be expected to turn that direction into clear plans, disciplined execution and measurable results.

You should be analytical, commercially minded, organized, technically capable and comfortable moving between strategy and execution.

You should naturally ask:

What happened? Why did it happen? Was the work executed correctly? What should we do next?

What You Will Own

- Marketing performance by market and channel

- Weekly KPI reporting and executive communication

- Lead volume, qualified leads, CPL, CAC, conversion and ROI

- Paid-media agency performance

- SEO, local SEO and Google Business Profile performance

- Lead attribution, CRM and marketing automation

- Website and landing-page conversion

- Marketing priorities, projects and vendor deliverables

- Coordination between Marketing, Sales and Operations

- Marketing processes, SOPs and quality control

What You Will Do

Performance & Analytics

Track performance across paid search, organic search, local search, email/SMS, referrals and other channels.

Connect marketing activity to:

Lead → Contact → Quote → Sale → Revenue

Investigate changes in lead volume, lead quality, cost, conversion, revenue and market performance. Determine whether problems come from strategy, execution, tracking, lead routing, follow-up, agencies or market conditions.

Translate data into clear recommendations, owners, action steps and success criteria.

Growth Management

Identify opportunities to increase profitable customer acquisition.

Evaluate:

- Market and channel performance

- Budget allocation

- Search and keyword opportunities

- Landing pages

- Local search

- Lead reactivation

- CRM and follow-up

- New tests and growth initiatives

Work with John and the President/General Manager to prioritize opportunities and execute them effectively.

Hands-On Marketing Direction

Provide practical direction to agencies, vendors and internal specialists.

You should be able to review and improve:

- Paid-search structure, targeting, bids, budgets and ad copy

- Keywords and negative keywords

- Landing pages and conversion paths

- SEO and local-search execution

- Google Business Profiles

- CRM workflows and lead routing

- Tracking and attribution

- Website forms and calls

- Marketing SOPs and quality-control processes

You do not need to perform every task daily, but you must understand the work well enough to direct it, evaluate it, teach it and step in when necessary.

Agency & Vendor Management

Set clear expectations for each agency or specialist, including:

- Objective

- Strategy

- Required work

- KPI and target

- Deliverable

- Deadline

- Result

- Corrective action

Challenge vague explanations and distinguish between poor strategy, weak execution, tracking issues, lead-quality problems and sales follow-up problems.

Marketing Operations

Create structure around the marketing department.

Maintain:

- Priorities and project ownership

- Due dates and reporting

- KPI dashboards

- Campaign calendars

- Testing backlogs

- Vendor deliverables

- SOPs and training materials

- Quality-control checklists

- Open issues and follow-up items

Eliminate, automate, delegate or simplify low-value work.

Sales & Marketing Alignment

Work with Sales to understand what happens after a lead is generated.

Use downstream results to evaluate targeting, messaging, qualification, routing, response time, follow-up and sales execution.

Marketing success is not simply generating inquiries. The goal is generating qualified opportunities that become profitable customers.

Team Coordination

Work with specialists in:

- Paid media

- SEO and local SEO

- Google Business Profiles

- Content

- Email and SMS

- Creative

- Website

- Marketing automation

- Analytics and reporting

You are not expected to own every specialty, but you must be able to evaluate the work, set direction, identify problems, coach others and hold people accountable.

Executive Partnership

Our owner and the President/General Manager are both marketers and will remain actively involved.

They will provide strategic guidance, feedback and context on priorities, positioning, messaging and customer experience.

You will be expected to present recommendations, accept feedback, revise plans when appropriate and own the day-to-day marketing operating system.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first 90 days, you will have:

- Established a reliable weekly marketing scorecard

- Created clear ownership across marketing functions

- Improved visibility into performance by market and channel

- Evaluated agency, vendor and execution quality

- Improved lead attribution and CAC reporting

- Connected marketing results to sales outcomes

- Identified priority growth opportunities

- Documented key SOPs and standards

- Created a testing and optimization roadmap

- Established an effective working rhythm with leadership

Over time, success means:

- More qualified leads

- Lower acquisition costs

- Better marketing efficiency

- Stronger attribution

- Better agency accountability

- More consistent execution

- Faster problem resolution

- Stronger internal capability

- More predictable revenue growth

Ideal Background

We are looking for someone with approximately 5–8+ years of experience in growth marketing, performance marketing, marketing operations, demand generation or digital marketing.

Strong candidates will have hands-on experience with several of the following:

- Google Ads / PPC

- SEO and local SEO

- Google Business Profiles

- GA4 and Google Search Console

- CRM and marketing automation

- Lead routing and call tracking

- Attribution and reporting

- Conversion-rate optimization

- Landing pages and websites

- Agency management

- Multi-market or local service businesses

- Executive KPI reporting

- SOP development

- Team training or coaching

Experience personally diagnosing and correcting marketing problems is especially valuable.

The Person We Are Looking For

You are:

- Analytical and commercially minded

- Highly organized

- Technically credible

- Comfortable with accountability

- Curious about why performance changes

- Able to move between strategy and execution

- Comfortable reviewing detailed work

- Strong at prioritization

- Clear with executives, vendors and teammates

- Comfortable receiving direct feedback

- Resourceful, dependable and coachable

- Focused on outcomes rather than activity

- Committed to high-quality work and continuous improvement

You should enjoy building systems, improving performance and developing people while staying close enough to the work to know whether it is being done correctly.

This Role Is Probably Not Right for You If

You primarily want to:

- Focus on brand strategy without owning performance

- Create content as your main responsibility

- Manage social media

- Review dashboards without investigating the work

- Delegate without understanding execution

- Rely entirely on agencies

- Avoid platform or implementation details

- Resist feedback

- Report metrics without owning results

- Prioritize activity over business outcomes

Reporting Relationship

Reports directly to the President/General Manager and works closely with John, Sales, Operations, internal marketing specialists and external agencies.

Qualified Lead Growth

Cost per Qualified Lead

Customer Acquisition Cost

Marketing-Sourced Revenue

Conversion Performance

Marketing ROI

Execution Quality

Attribution Accuracy

Team and Vendor Capability

Process Improvement

and the organization’s ability to understand where growth is coming from, whether the work is being executed correctly and where the next marketing dollar should be invested.

But beyond the resume, you're the kind of leader who gets energy from building. You're curious about AI search, not intimidated by it. Meeting Tomorrow is a 23-year-old company with a growing team of 90 talented, friendly people. We’re headquartered in Chicago, with about 80% of our team working remotely in cities across the country.

We are a full-service event agency with three core divisions: planning, production, and creative. We plan and produce corporate events of every shape and size, partnering with clients that include Fortune 500 companies and leading organizations across a wide array of industries.

We’re known for our exceptional customer experience, our collaborative culture, and our can-do spirit. Our culture has earned us recognition as a Top 20 Inspiring Workplace in North America, as well as the Events Industry Council's Social Impact Award. We offer great benefits, the best coworkers you’ll find anywhere, and the opportunity to work in a dynamic, team-oriented environment. We can’t wait to meet you!

The Opportunity

We’re looking for a Director of Demand Generation to own our inbound revenue number and the plan to grow it several times over in the next three years. You’ll drive leads across three channels: paid advertising (Google, LinkedIn), organic search and SEO, and AI-powered search and LLM visibility (GEO). You’ll report to the COO, and partner closely with our Sales and Marketing teams.

This is a builder role. You’ll own the strategy, run the channels, and build the agentic workflows that make the whole machine run more efficiently over time. Your success is measured in revenue, not pipeline or activity.

What You’ll Own

- Pipeline end to end: qualified leads across inbound and outbound channels, from first touch to sales handoff

- Paid advertising: Google Ads and LinkedIn, with full budget accountability and a bias toward what actually converts

- Organic search and SEO: making Meeting Tomorrow’s content and website attractive to Google and ranking for the terms that matter to our buyers

- LLM and GEO: growing Meeting Tomorrow’s presence in AI-powered search and recommendation environments

- Agentic workflows: building and managing the automations that drive campaign efficiency and compress time-to-pipeline

- Demand gen KPIs: CPL, MQL volume and quality, MQL-to-SQL conversion, pipeline contribution, and CAC, with regular visibility to leadership

- Budget decisions: full accountability for how demand gen dollars are allocated, with the COO in the loop

Key Responsibilities

- Build and execute the demand generation roadmap, aligned to revenue targets and Sales priorities

- Own SEO strategy and execution: keyword targeting, on-page optimization, content signals, and technical SEO in partnership with the web team

- Manage paid media across Google and LinkedIn: campaign structure, targeting, creative testing, and budget allocation

- Develop Meeting Tomorrow’s presence in AI-powered search (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews) through GEO strategies

- Build and iterate on agentic workflows that automate repeatable marketing functions, from lead scoring to outreach sequencing

- Run A/B tests and side-by-side comparisons across channels to continuously improve performance

- Partner with Sales on lead handoff, pipeline review cadences, and feedback loops

- Ensure all outbound programs comply with CAN-SPAM, GDPR, and CCPA

Who You Are

- You’re a builder. You see a gap, you close it. You don’t wait for someone to tell you how.

- You’re entrepreneurial about channels: when something works, you double down. When it doesn’t, you move on and find what does.

- You think in systems and automation. The goal is a demand gen function that compounds over time, not one that depends on you doing everything manually.

- You treat Sales like a partner, not an internal customer. Pipeline is a team sport.

- You can walk into ambiguity, build structure, and make progress without waiting for someone to hand you a playbook.

What You’ve Done

- Proven SEO expertise: you know how to make a website and its content rank. You’ve done it, you can show the results, and you understand the technical and content sides of the discipline.

- Hands-on experience building AI agents or agentic workflows: not theoretically familiar, not interested in learning. You have built at least one agent that automated something real and you can speak to what it did.

- A clear track record of digital lead growth tied to revenue: you can point to a channel you found or optimized and tell us what it made the business.

- Strong data fluency: you own your numbers, run your own analysis, and can walk leadership through your pipeline story without a deck full of caveats.

- Experience with paid media platforms (Google Ads, LinkedIn) and marketing automation or CRM systems (HubSpot, Marketo, ActiveCampaign, or equivalent).

- Has carried a revenue number, not just a channel number — built a multi-year revenue model and defended the acquisition budget behind it to a CEO, board, or investor.

The Impact

Within 1 month, you’ll:

- Deeply understand the brand, business, and related goals.

- Run a full audit of existing programs, stack, and agent infrastructure to understand the foundation we are working from.

Within 3 months, you’ll:

- Create first agentic workflow live and tracked against pipeline KPIs

- Create a demand gen roadmap presented to leadership with agent strategy integrated

Within 6 months you’ll:

- Have measurable pipeline impact from agent-run programs with compounding momentum

Benefits

- Medical, dental, and vision plan options

- Employer paid STD, LTD, Life Insurance, and EAP access

- 401k with employer matching up to 4%

- 16 PTO days (increases with tenure) + 9 paid holidays

- Annual profit-sharing bonus

- 12 weeks 100% paid parental leave (maternity, paternity, adoption)

- $50 Monthly fitness reimbursement

- Monthly stipends for internet and/or cell

- Company donation(s) to your charities of choice (up to $1,000 annually)

- Regular social events and learning opportunities

$140,000 - $186,001 a year

The above range is the starting salary range for this role. The final starting salary is based on individual experience and how closely it translates to the role. Once in the role, we offer annual merit increases based on performance.

At Meeting Tomorrow, our mission is to foster a culture of respect and affection. We embrace our differences and are committed to having a diverse, equitable, and inclusive environment. We’re an Equal Opportunity Employer that believes in second chances and strongly encourages BIPOC, women, LGBTQIA, veterans, persons with disabilities, formerly incarcerated and all other individuals to apply.

What makes Meeting Tomorrow’s culture so special is the people, and we look for candidates who are a match for our company’s core values: commitment, kindness and humility. If those words describe you and you see yourself in this posting, you’re ready to apply!

We’re looking for a Content Marketing Manager – Professional Learning to help build and scale Moreland University’s professional learning offering for educators.

This is an individual contributor role with meaningful ownership over a new area of growth for Moreland. We’ve spent the last several years testing professional learning experiences with educators and have seen strong interest and demand. Now, we’re ready to turn that momentum into a scalable portfolio of on-demand courses, learning journeys, live experiences, and ultimately new subscription-based offerings.

You’ll own the professional learning go-to-market calendar and help move new offerings from idea through launch — partnering closely with faculty and subject matter experts who develop the curriculum while you provide project leadership, audience insight, editorial guidance, and marketing expertise.

We’re looking for a content marketer first: someone who can write, position, launch, and promote educational offerings while keeping multiple projects, stakeholders, and deadlines moving forward. Experience working with educators, teachers, EdTech, professional learning, or another teacher-facing audience will be especially valuable.

- Own the professional learning portfolio and launch calendar, helping prioritize, plan, and bring new on-demand courses, learning journeys, certificates, microcredentials, webinars, and other educator experiences to market

- Direct experience creating marketing content and bringing programs, educational offerings, digital content, courses, events, or similar products to market not simply supporting content after launch

We're seeking a Senior Marketing Operations Specialist to own and evolve the systems, strategy, and data infrastructure that power Morning Consult's marketing and revenue engine. HubSpot Platform Ownership

- Primary HubSpot admin across Marketing, Sales, and Operations Hubs: configuration, data architecture, user management, and platform health

- Define and document the marketing data model and metric hierarchy; ensure consistency of definitions across Marketing, RevOps, and Finance

Campaign & Process Operations

- Own the operational layer of campaign execution: list pulls, workflow QA, email setup, UTM governance, suppression logic, and post-campaign reporting

- Support ABM operations for enterprise accounts using enrichment and routing tools (Clay, ZoomInfo, LeanData)

- Own the process improvement roadmap — identify, prioritize, build, and document automation initiatives with measurable time/cost impact

Cross-Functional Partnership

- Operate as the marketing systems authority for cross-functional stakeholders — shaping how Marketing and RevOps design processes together, not just implementing requests

- Help stakeholders scope requests, assess tradeoffs, and self-serve through training and documentation, and build scalable enablement resources so the team grows with you.

About You and What You've Done:

- 5–7 years in Marketing Operations, Revenue Operations, or a closely related role at a B2B SaaS, data, or technology company

- Deep HubSpot expertise and a track record of platform ownership — you've built and scaled the system, not inherited it; you can articulate architectural decisions and their tradeoffs; certifications expected

- Solid grasp of the HubSpot–Salesforce integration; comfortable in Salesforce for reports, record inspection, and joint process work

- Strong dashboard and reporting skills, advanced proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets for data manipulation and ad hoc analysis, and experience defining metric frameworks rather than just pulling numbers.

- Experience with ABM and enrichment/routing tools (Clay, ZoomInfo, LeanData), and you've operationalized ABM motions, not just supported them

- AI-native working style — you use Claude, ChatGPT, or similar to accelerate operational work and know where human judgment still matters

- Systems thinker who proactively identifies what's broken before being asked — and builds the case for fixing it

- Independent, clear communicator who can translate technical logic for non-technical partners, and you've influenced stakeholders at the Director level and above

About Morning Consult

Morning Consult is a global decision intelligence company changing how modern leaders make smarter, faster, better decisions. The company pairs its proprietary high-frequency data with applied artificial intelligence to better inform decisions on what people think and how they will act.

This role is available in any of our office locations or can be based remotely. Our award-winning and modern offices are located in Washington, DC; Chicago, IL; and New York, NY. All three offices are accessible by public transportation and in close proximity to great restaurants and shopping.

Join us in the office for catered lunch on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays, or grab a beverage from the fridge for an impromptu after-work happy hour!

The Role

Morning Consult is hiring a Director, Marketing Strategy and Operations to own the marketing organization's highest-priority cross-functional initiatives end to end — from problem definition through implementation, adoption, and the outcome each one was meant to produce. This is the kind of work that doesn't sit neatly inside a single function, requires structuring real ambiguity, and needs someone who can move fluidly between strategic planning and hands-on execution.

How ownership works:This role owns projects and supports every function across the Marketing team. On every initiative you take on, you are the accountable owner: you define the problem, build the plan, convene the cross-functional group, drive the decisions, and are measured on whether it shipped and moved the number it was supposed to move. Marketing leadership may be in the room for the first meeting — after that it's yours. Every initiative on the list below is one the business cannot execute without a dedicated owner, which is why the role exists.

This is not a conventional product marketing, growth, or operations role. You'll flex across the function to support what the business needs most in a given quarter. In one stretch that might mean rebuilding how inbound leads flow from marketing to sales; in another, it might mean helping take new AI and agentic product capabilities to market, translating strategic priorities into concrete plans and scorecards, or working through how the team's content function should evolve.

What You'll Be Working On

- Own the marketing organization's highest-priority cross-functional initiatives — scoped with the Chief Growth Officer, then run by you — the projects too multidisciplinary or consequential to sit inside a single function.

- Own communication and reporting of overall growth function performance to executive, cross-functional, and team function leaders.

- Own large-scale transformation projects end-to-end, from problem definition through implementation and adoption.

- Structure undefined, messy problems into clear plans, workstreams, timelines, and owners — and drive them to completion.

- Translate Marketing leadership's strategic priorities into concrete operating plans, targets, and scorecards, and own tracking progress against them over time.

- Build and run the operating rhythm for the marketing organization — planning cycles, leadership reviews, and the decision forums that go with them — so the team operates against real targets and a real calendar.

- Lead Marketing's role in company-level strategic efforts — the go-to-market for new AI and agentic product capabilities, our analytics investment, and Marketing's contribution to our largest enterprise and AI-partner pitches. You'll carry these with the authority to decide, not just to report back.

- Partner with functional leads to evaluate and strengthen the team's capabilities and areas for improvement.

- Build the materials and narratives for executive- and leadership-level conversations, translating complex initiatives into clear, decision-ready updates.

- Serve as a trusted thought partner to marketing leadership on prioritization, resourcing, and organizational design decisions.

- Build trust and alignment across stakeholders in Sales, Product, RevOps, and Finance, ensuring Marketing's priorities are understood and properly resourced beyond the marketing org itself.

- Move fluidly between strategy and hands-on execution — this role is built to flex toward wherever the business need is greatest.

About You and What You've Done

- 8+ years of experience spanning product marketing, growth, or business/marketing operations and strategy, ideally including time at a high-growth SaaS, data, or technology company.

- A track record of owning large-scale, cross-functional transformation projects from ambiguity through execution.

- Comfortable operating without a fixed functional lane — genuinely energized by moving between strategy, analytics, and hands-on execution as priorities shift.

- A systems thinker who can diagnose broken or informal processes and redesign them to scale.

- Strong judgment operating with significant autonomy; exercises wide latitude in determining the right approach to critical, undefined assignments.

- Experience operating as a close, trusted partner to a senior leader on strategic initiatives.

- Experience building or running planning cycles, operating cadences, or scorecards for a leadership team, and comfort acting as a proxy for senior leadership in certain settings.

- Strong analytical fluency and comfort getting into the data to inform recommendations.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to flex between detailed execution and clear, executive-level narrative.

- Genuine curiosity about applying AI to marketing and operations, with an interest in evaluating and rolling out new tools and agentic capabilities.

- Depth in B2B product marketing, data or licensing go-to-market, or enterprise growth is a strong plus — several of the first projects sit squarely in that territory.

_Note: We view the above section as a guide, not a checklist. Research shows that underrepresented/marginalized groups are less likely to apply for a job if they feel that they don’t meet 100% of the qualifications. We welcome diverse and non-traditional backgrounds and encourage you to apply even if you don’t satisfy every single bullet on this list! It’s expected that you’ll learn and grow throughout your time at Morning Consult, so if you’re open to building new skills, we’d love to hear from you._

The expected salary range for this position is $172,900 – $290,800, with a midpoint of $231,900.

In most cases, we target the midpoint of our salary ranges for new hire compensation. This placement is reflective of full proficiency in a role. This role is eligible for an equity grant, which will be discussed in your initial recruiter conversation. Please see an overview of Morning Consult’s benefits on our Career Page.

About G2 - The Company

G2 is the world's largest and most trusted software marketplace. When you join G2, you’re joining the industry’s leading team that helps businesses reach their peak potential by powering decisions and strategies with trusted insights from real software users.

Now, we have joined forces with Capterra, SoftwareAdvice, and GetApp to create the largest source of online data and software insights to fuel intelligent buying in the age of AI. Does that sound exciting to you? Come join us as we try to reach our next PEAK!

About G2 - Our People

At G2, everything we are and what we do is grounded in our PEAK values— ( _P_ erformance + _E_ ntrepreneurship + _A_ uthenticity + _K_ indness. Working at G2 means you are part of a value-driven, growing global community that climbs PEAKs together. We cheer for each other’s successes, learn from our mistakes, and support and lean on one another during challenging times. With ambition and entrepreneurial spirit we push each other to take on challenging work, which will help us all to grow and learn.

At the heart of our community and culture are our people-led ERGs, which celebrate and highlight the diverse identities of our global team. As an organization, we are intentional about our DEI and philanthropic work (like our G2 Gives program) because it encourages us all to be better people.

About The Role

At G2, our Senior Product Marketing Manager, AI Solutions owns go-to-market strategy and hands-on growth execution for G2 AI Solutions — G2’s full AI product portfolio, spanning G2.ai (our AI playground and beta testing ground for Blueprints, Agent Evals, and what’s next) all the way through their migration into G2.com. You’ll define who these products are for, build the story that makes buyers care, and personally drive the growth tactics that take an early AI product from zero traction to revenue — owning that GTM motion end-to-end, from first beta signal in G2.ai to full integration on G2.com. You will report to the Senior Director, Product Marketing, with a dotted line into the product organization, and be a key member of the PMM team.

This role owns G2 AI Solutions — G2’s newest, most ambiguous, and fastest-moving product bets — end to end, covering both sides of the merger from G2.ai (our AI playground) into G2.com, not just work happening in the AI playground. As capabilities like Agent Evals get built directly into G2.com, this person owns how the audience, story, and growth motion travel with them.

You’ll be a dedicated PMM partner for G2 AI Solutions, embedded in product roadmap and planning from the earliest stages, while also working directly with the builders behind individual solutions underneath it.

This is a blend of strategist and operator: you form a sharp point of view on audience and positioning, and you’re also comfortable rolling up your sleeves to run the campaigns, community plays, and early pipeline motions that get a new product to its first dollar of revenue.

In This Role, You Will:

_GTM Vision & Market Definition (25%)_

- Define who each AI product is for and why, and build positioning and messaging that’s differentiated and defensible — testing assumptions fast through lightweight experiments, customer conversations, and early pilots.

- Own GTM strategy for G2 AI Solutions end-to-end — from G2.ai (Blueprints, Agent Evals, and what’s next) through their migration into G2.com — with a buyer-first lens; seller-facing use cases are secondary and in service of seeding buyer adoption.

- Own the plan for how each product’s audience, messaging, and channel strategy evolves as it migrates from G2.ai into G2.com — including products like Agent Evals that are launching directly into G2.com.

_Growth Execution & Zero-to-Revenue (20%)_

- Personally own and run the growth tactics that take AI Solutions products from early access to revenue-generating — campaigns, community seeding, lifecycle nurture, and early pipeline generation — not just briefing others on what to build.

- Own pipeline and revenue visibility for the AI Solutions portfolio in its early stages, and run lightweight acquisition and activation experiments (organic, community-led, referral) to find what moves users from aware to paying.

- Partner with Sales and RevOps to define what “revenue-ready” looks like for an early-stage AI product, and drive the handoff from PMM-led growth to a scaled GTM motion.

_Early User Research & Market Validation (15%)_

- Proactively identify and engage prospective buyers before a product is ready, running lightweight discovery — user interviews, concept tests, early-access pilots.

- Stay close to the competitive landscape and category trends; feed market perspective back to Product as the informed voice of the buyer.

- Build and maintain a network of early users and prospective customers who can give honest, ongoing input as AI Solutions products evolve; synthesize findings into clear takeaways on who’s likely to buy and what’s resonating.

_Sales Enablement & Go-to-Market Readiness (15%)_

- Partner with Sales Enablement to understand what’s landing in the field and close gaps quickly with the right narrative, proof points, and collateral.

- Use G2’s existing seller and customer base to seed early adoption of AI Solutions products, rather than building net-new external communities from scratch.

- Brief the PMM team on what enablement materials need to exist across Buyer, Seller, and Reviewer audiences, and serve as a strategic driver behind early pilot and launch motions.

_Cross-Functional Partnership & Orchestration (15%)_

- Serve as Products' dedicated PMM partner for AI Solutions — embedded in product org’s roadmap and planning from the earliest stages — while also partnering directly with the builders of individual solutions underneath it.

- Translate early and often-unformed product direction into a GTM plan the PMM team can execute against; build frameworks and messaging together with PMM peers, then partner with Demand Gen, Content, and Comms to execute.

- Communicate GTM direction, experiment results, and recommendations clearly to the Senior Director, PMM leadership, and Product; flag when something upstream is broken and bring a proposed solution.

_Alignment & Market Intelligence (10%)_

- Give the team clarity on what you’re working toward and why; operate as a reliable, easy-to-trust partner across Marketing and Product.

- Maintain a current view of the competitive landscape and category trends specific to AI-powered GTM and software discovery, and use it to keep AI Solutions positioning sharp and relevant.

- Build and maintain a high hiring bar for the PMM function — attracting marketers with intellectual rigor, genuine product fluency, and GTM depth.

Minimum Qualifications:

We realize applying for jobs can feel daunting at times. Even if you don’t check all the boxes in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway.

-  7+ years of product marketing, growth marketing, or GTM strategy experience in B2B SaaS, including at least one experience getting a product off the ground with little to no playbook.

- Proven ability to take a product from zero to revenue — hands-on experience running growth or demand campaigns, building pipeline, and driving early revenue, not just strategy and orchestration.

- Experience in an early-stage or new-product environment (startup, internal venture, or skunkworks team) where you had to define the market as much as the message.

- Comfortable with data and experimentation: you understand testing frameworks, know how to build and validate a hypothesis, and use data to build a compelling story.

- A natural relationship builder who gets things done through people — across Marketing, Sales, Product, and Leadership. History of relationships strong enough that people at past companies would say you made their work better.

- Clear, confident communicator — you write sharp positioning, give a crisp verbal brief, and make meetings productive.

- Comfortable in ambiguity — you don’t need a fully-formed brief to get started, you help create it.

- Deep familiarity with or genuine curiosity about AI and how it’s reshaping software buying behavior.

- Experience with PLG or self-serve motions where understanding the buyer deeply was essential to acquisition.

- Comfortable owning a broad, evolving portfolio (multiple AI products at different maturity stages) rather than a single, narrowly-defined product.

Travel: Willingness to travel for company events, product offsites, and customer-facing meetings as needed.

Deep diving: You know the product at the level where you can demo it as well as anyone in the company. You know where the real value sits and where it breaks down. You don't mandate alignment. You create it by making the story so clear and compelling that people want to tell it.

AI builder. You build systems for the team, not just yourself. You've already offloaded the repeatable work to automation: competitive monitoring, content generation, persona synthesis. Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

- Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

- Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

- First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

- Accelerate repeatable workflows

- Structure and solve problems

- Improve output quality

- Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

- Priorities and targets to change quickly

- Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

- A high level of personal ownership and accountability

- Close collaboration across teams and functions

- Frequent, high-touch communication

- Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

- A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

- Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

- Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.
