ValPay builds embedded payments for software companies. Our PayFac-as-a-Service model lets ISVs offer payments to their merchants under their own brand, while we handle underwriting, compliance, and risk. Our partners serve healthcare, legal, hospitality, professional services, and other vertical markets.
Launching a payments product is the easy part. The value is created when ISV partners go live, their merchants enroll, and transactions flow. We’re hiring a product marketing Lead whose success is measured by adoption: how quickly and how deeply partners and merchants use our products.
You’ll own positioning, launches, and lifecycle marketing across our vertical markets and across North America, Europe, and APAC. You’ll report to the CEO and work closely with product, sales, partnerships, the ISV channel team, and operations.
AI should be part of how you work. Use it to research, draft, analyze, and automate. You’re responsible for the quality of the result.
What we value
Sound judgment and attention to detail.
Measuring success by what customers do, not by what we shipped.
Taking responsibility and finishing work without being chased.
Understanding how the business makes money and caring about results.
The honesty to say when something isn’t working, including your own work.
What you’ll do
Drive partner and merchant adoption:
You’ll own the adoption journey end to end: signature, integration, go-live, first transaction, merchant enrollment, and expansion. The hardest gap is between “integrated” and “actively transacting,” and you’ll be the person who finds out where partners and merchants stall and designs programs to close it. That means lifecycle campaigns, onboarding content, and activation playbooks for two audiences at once: the ISV partner and the merchants who use their software. With the ISV channel team, you’ll run co-marketing and merchant-enrollment campaigns that lift penetration within each partner’s customer base.
Measure adoption and act on it:
You’ll build and maintain the adoption dashboard: activation rate, time to first transaction, attach and penetration rate, volume per merchant, feature adoption, and cohort retention. You’ll use that data to segment partners and merchants, flag at-risk accounts, and surface expansion opportunities, then take what you find to the teams who can act on it.
Own positioning and messaging:
You’ll develop the positioning, value propositions, and messaging for each product and vertical, and for new verticals and markets as we enter them. A central part of this is explaining clearly how our embedded payments offering differs from horizontal PayFacs, processors, and ISOs. You’ll translate technical capabilities into the outcomes ISVs and merchants care about: revenue share, retention, cleaner reconciliation, and faster onboarding.
Run launches built around activation:
You’ll lead launch plans for new products, features, verticals, and regions. Every launch gets adoption targets and a 30/60/90-day activation plan, not only awareness goals. You’ll also make sure what we’re building is communicated publicly, online and through partners. You’ll adapt messaging to regional regulatory and market conditions, and work with product, finance, risk, and support so that each launch is commercially and operationally ready before it goes out.
Equip sales, partnerships, and support:
You’ll create the sales playbooks, pitch decks, battlecards, case studies, ROI calculators, and objection-handling guides that sales and partnership teams use, and equip support to explain the products as well. You’ll train teams to sell for activation, not just signature. You’ll run win/loss and churn analysis and feed what you learn back into positioning and the product.
Represent the market inside the company:
You’ll track competitors, pricing, interchange, and regulatory developments, and be the voice of the market and of adoption data in product planning. When acquisitions or product consolidations happen, you’ll support portfolio and integration messaging.
What you’ll bring
At least 3 years of experience in product marketing at a B2B software, fintech, or payments company.
A track record of running launches and measuring them on adoption or usage, not only on awareness.
Experience marketing to two audiences at once, such as partners and their customers, or platforms and their users.
Working knowledge of how card payments work, or the ability to learn it quickly and explain it accurately.
Comfort with data. You can define a metric, build or spec a dashboard, and draw a conclusion from it.
Strong writing. You can turn a technical capability into a clear business case for a software company or a small-business owner.
Experience building sales enablement that teams actually used.
You can take a loosely defined goal, set your own plan, and finish it.
You use AI tools every day for research, drafting, and analysis, and you check what they produce.
Useful experience
Embedded payments, PayFac, or ISV channel experience.
Lifecycle or onboarding marketing in a partner-led business.
Marketing in healthcare, legal, hospitality, or professional services software.
Launching products in Europe or APAC.
Running win/loss or churn analysis programs.
Hands-on experience with SQL, a BI tool, or marketing automation.
Portfolio or integration messaging after an acquisition.
Who will enjoy this role
You notice when a partner has been live for two months and only a handful of their merchants have enrolled, and you want to know why. Is it the pitch, the onboarding, the partner’s own sales team, or the product?
In the same week you might rebuild a merchant onboarding email sequence, pull cohort data for the CEO, train a partnership team on a new vertical, and rewrite a battlecard after a lost deal to a horizontal processor.
The scope is wide for one person, and adoption is a harder target than launch coverage. You’ll be judged on numbers you influence but don’t fully control, which means working through partners, product, and sales to move them. Priorities will shift with the roadmap and with acquisitions.
Why this role matters
ValPay is building products and features for software partners across several verticals and regions. That work has limited impact unless partners and merchants know about it, understand it, and use it.
You’ll work directly with the CEO to decide how our products are positioned and how each launch turns into transactions. Your work affects how quickly partners go live, how many of their merchants enroll, and how much volume flows through the platform. You’ll have the authority to set the story and change it when the adoption data says so.

ValPay conçoit des solutions de paiement intégrées pour les entreprises de logiciels. Notre modèle PayFac-as-a-Service permet aux éditeurs de logiciels (ISV) d’offrir des paiements à leurs commerçants sous leur propre marque, pendant que nous prenons en charge la souscription, la conformité et la gestion des risques. Nos partenaires servent les secteurs de la santé, du droit, de l’hôtellerie et de la restauration, des services professionnels et d’autres marchés verticaux.
Lancer un produit de paiement, c’est la partie facile. La valeur se crée lorsque les ISV partenaires sont mis en service, que leurs commerçants adhèrent et que les transactions circulent. Nous recherchons une personne responsable du marketing produit dont le succès se mesure à l’adoption : la rapidité et la profondeur avec lesquelles les partenaires et les commerçants utilisent nos produits.
Vous serez responsable du positionnement, des lancements et du marketing du cycle de vie dans l’ensemble de nos marchés verticaux, en Amérique du Nord, en Europe et en Asie-Pacifique. Vous relèverez du chef de la direction et travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes produit, ventes, partenariats, canal ISV et opérations.
L’IA devrait faire partie de votre façon de travailler. Utilisez-la pour faire de la recherche, rédiger, analyser et automatiser. Vous êtes responsable de la qualité du résultat.
Ce qui compte pour nous
Un bon jugement et le souci du détail.
Mesurer le succès à ce que font les clients, et non à ce que nous avons livré.
Prendre ses responsabilités et mener le travail à terme sans qu’on ait à faire de relances.
Comprendre comment l’entreprise génère des revenus et se soucier des résultats.
L’honnêteté de dire quand quelque chose ne fonctionne pas, y compris dans son propre travail.
Ce que vous ferez
Stimuler l’adoption par les partenaires et les commerçants :
Vous serez responsable de tout le parcours d’adoption : signature, intégration technique, mise en service, première transaction, adhésion des commerçants et expansion. L’écart le plus difficile à combler se situe entre « intégré » et « en transaction active », et c’est vous qui déterminerez où les partenaires et les commerçants stagnent et qui concevrez des programmes pour combler cet écart. Cela comprend des campagnes de cycle de vie, du contenu d’accueil et d’intégration (onboarding) et des guides d’activation pour deux publics à la fois : l’ISV partenaire et les commerçants qui utilisent son logiciel. Avec l’équipe du canal ISV, vous mènerez des campagnes de comarketing et d’adhésion des commerçants qui augmentent le taux de pénétration au sein de la clientèle de chaque partenaire.
Mesurer l’adoption et agir en conséquence :
Vous créerez et tiendrez à jour le tableau de bord de l’adoption : taux d’activation, délai avant la première transaction, taux de rattachement et de pénétration, volume par commerçant, adoption des fonctionnalités et rétention par cohorte. Vous utiliserez ces données pour segmenter les partenaires et les commerçants, repérer les comptes à risque et faire ressortir les occasions d’expansion, puis vous transmettrez vos constats aux équipes qui peuvent agir.
Définir le positionnement et les messages :
Vous élaborerez le positionnement, les propositions de valeur et les messages pour chaque produit et chaque marché vertical, ainsi que pour les nouveaux marchés à mesure que nous y entrons. Un volet central de ce travail consiste à expliquer clairement en quoi notre offre de paiements intégrés se distingue des PayFac horizontaux, des processeurs de paiement et des ISO. Vous traduirez les capacités techniques en résultats qui comptent pour les ISV et les commerçants : partage des revenus, fidélisation, rapprochement simplifié et intégration plus rapide.
Mener des lancements axés sur l’activation :
Vous dirigerez les plans de lancement des nouveaux produits, fonctionnalités, marchés verticaux et régions. Chaque lancement comporte des cibles d’adoption et un plan d’activation sur 30, 60 et 90 jours, et pas seulement des objectifs de notoriété. Vous veillerez aussi à ce que ce que nous construisons soit communiqué publiquement, en ligne et par l’intermédiaire des partenaires. Vous adapterez les messages aux conditions réglementaires et commerciales de chaque région, et travaillerez avec les équipes produit, finances, risques et soutien pour que chaque lancement soit prêt sur les plans commercial et opérationnel avant sa sortie.
Outiller les équipes des ventes, des partenariats et du soutien :
Vous créerez les guides de vente, présentations, fiches concurrentielles, études de cas, calculateurs de RCI et guides de réponse aux objections qu’utilisent les équipes des ventes et des partenariats, et vous outillerez également l’équipe du soutien pour qu’elle puisse expliquer les produits. Vous formerez les équipes à vendre en visant l’activation, et pas seulement la signature. Vous mènerez des analyses des gains et des pertes ainsi que de l’attrition, et réinjecterez vos apprentissages dans le positionnement et le produit.
Représenter le marché au sein de l’entreprise :
Vous suivrez les concurrents, les prix, les frais d’interchange et l’évolution de la réglementation, et serez la voix du marché et des données d’adoption dans la planification des produits. Lors d’acquisitions ou de regroupements de produits, vous soutiendrez les messages liés au portefeuille et à l’intégration.
Ce que vous apporterez
Au moins trois ans d’expérience en marketing produit dans une entreprise de logiciels B2B, de technologie financière ou de paiements.
Une expérience concrète de lancements dont le succès a été mesuré par l’adoption ou l’utilisation, et pas seulement par la notoriété.
De l’expérience à faire du marketing auprès de deux publics à la fois, par exemple des partenaires et leurs clients, ou des plateformes et leurs utilisateurs.
Une connaissance pratique du fonctionnement des paiements par carte, ou la capacité de l’acquérir rapidement et de l’expliquer avec justesse.
De l’aisance avec les données. Vous savez définir un indicateur, concevoir ou spécifier un tableau de bord et en tirer une conclusion.
D’excellentes aptitudes en rédaction. Vous savez transformer une capacité technique en argumentaire d’affaires clair pour une entreprise de logiciels ou le propriétaire d’une petite entreprise.
De l’expérience dans la création d’outils d’habilitation des ventes que les équipes ont réellement utilisés.
Vous savez prendre un objectif vaguement défini, établir votre propre plan et le mener à terme.
Vous utilisez des outils d’IA tous les jours pour la recherche, la rédaction et l’analyse, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.
Atouts
Expérience en paiements intégrés, avec des PayFac ou dans un canal ISV.
Marketing du cycle de vie ou de l’accueil et de l’intégration des clients dans une entreprise axée sur les partenaires.
Marketing de logiciels dans les secteurs de la santé, du droit, de l’hôtellerie et de la restauration ou des services professionnels.
Lancement de produits en Europe ou en Asie-Pacifique.
Mise en place de programmes d’analyse des gains et des pertes ou de l’attrition.
Expérience pratique de SQL, d’un outil de veille d’affaires (BI) ou d’automatisation du marketing.
Messages liés au portefeuille ou à l’intégration à la suite d’une acquisition.
Ce poste vous plaira si…
Vous remarquez qu’un partenaire est en service depuis deux mois et que seule une poignée de ses commerçants ont adhéré, et vous voulez comprendre pourquoi. Est-ce l’argumentaire, l’accueil et l’intégration, l’équipe de vente du partenaire ou le produit?
Au cours d’une même semaine, vous pourriez refaire une séquence de courriels d’accueil pour les commerçants, extraire des données de cohortes pour le chef de la direction, former une équipe de partenariats sur un nouveau marché vertical et réécrire une fiche concurrentielle après avoir perdu un contrat au profit d’un processeur horizontal.
La portée du poste est vaste pour une seule personne, et l’adoption est une cible plus difficile à atteindre que la visibilité d’un lancement. Vous serez évalué(e) sur des résultats que vous influencez sans les contrôler entièrement, ce qui veut dire que vous devrez passer par les partenaires, l’équipe produit et les ventes pour les faire bouger. Les priorités évolueront au gré de la feuille de route et des acquisitions.
Pourquoi ce poste est important
ValPay développe des produits et des fonctionnalités pour des partenaires logiciels dans plusieurs marchés verticaux et régions. Ce travail a peu d’impact si les partenaires et les commerçants ne le connaissent pas, ne le comprennent pas et ne l’utilisent pas.
Vous travaillerez directement avec le chef de la direction pour décider du positionnement de nos produits et de la façon dont chaque lancement se traduit en transactions. Votre travail influence la rapidité avec laquelle les partenaires sont mis en service, le nombre de leurs commerçants qui adhèrent et le volume qui circule sur la plateforme. Vous aurez l’autorité nécessaire pour définir le discours et le modifier lorsque les données d’adoption l’indiquent.

About KidKare
The people who care for and feed children every day have enough on their plates. Their software shouldn't add to it.
For more than 30 years, KidKare has built technology for the people behind childcare and child nutrition, helping them spend less time on paperwork, compliance, and administrative work and more time focused on the children and communities they serve.
Our roots run deep in the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP), a federal nutrition program that helps provide healthy meals and snacks to children and adults across the country. Today, we're building on that expertise with a growing ecosystem of software supporting childcare organizations across food program compliance, business management, professional development, and licensing.
We're growing into new products, new markets, and have a much bigger vision for what KidKare can do for the childcare community. To support these goals, we're looking for a Product Growth Marketing Manager, Lifecycle & GTM Systems to build and run the engine that turns our product value into pipeline, adoption, and revenue.
Position Summary
This is an
execution-first growth
role.
You'll partner with Product and Revenue Operations leadership to define the positioning and value proposition for each product, then put them to work: translating individual product propositions and features into audience-specific messaging and deploying that messaging through various tactics. You’ll be involved in managing the CRM, data enrichment, prospect scoring, routing, & lifecycle marketing. You'll report to our VP of Revenue Operations and work across Product, Sales, and Customer Growth to turn every launch and feature release into measurable pipeline, adoption, and expansion.
In a given week you might ship a new CRM workflow, tune a fit-and-intent scoring model, launch a demand-gen test to a newly enriched segment, build an app telemtry guide for a feature release, fix a routing rule that's sending leads to the wrong queue, or walk leadership through what moved in the funnel and why.
You'll build the machine, and you'll run it.
You'll partner closely with our Digital Marketing Manager, who owns brand, creative, content, and channel execution. You'll own the systems, segmentation, lifecycle logic, experiment design, and measurement that make that work reach the right audience at the right moment. Together, you'll turn product and market insight into demand.
Primary Responsibilities
Positioning, Feature Messaging & Launch Execution
•    Partner with product leadership to define and refine positioning and value propositions for each product and major release, grounded in customer, competitive, and market insight.
•    Translate individual product features and releases into audience-specific messaging (the value, the proof, and the call to action) for each persona and segment we serve, carrying positioning down to the feature level.
•    Execute launches through the systems you manage: target segments, lifecycle and nurture workflows, in-app guides, sales sequences and snippets, with launch tiers matched to the size of the release.
•    Package features into the battlecards, talk tracks, and objection handling our Sales and Customer Growth teams need, delivered inside CRM where reps actually work.
CRM Management & GTM Systems
•    Manage the CRM as the system of record for marketing and lifecycle: data model, custom properties, lifecycle stages, lead status, lists and segments, forms, and workflow automation.
•    Maintain CRM data quality and governance, including deduplication, field standards, consistent deal stages across pipelines, and clear documentation, so Sales, Customer Growth, and leadership trust the data.
•    Orchestrate the GTM stack (CRM, app telemtry, data enrichment, and automation tools) so product, marketing, and sales data flow cleanly between systems.
Enrichment, AI Scoring & Routing
•    Build and maintain enrichment workflows that close firmographic, contact, and segment data gaps, including vertical-specific sources relating to childcare, education, and food program participation data.
•    Design, deploy, and continuously tune fit, intent, and product-usage scoring models, using AI and predictive approaches where they outperform rules-based logic.
•    Own lead and account routing rules, handoff SLAs, and alerts to Sales and Customer Growth, and monitor speed-to-lead and conversion by route.
Demand Generation Experiments
•    Run a structured demand-gen experimentation program: define the hypothesis, audience, channel, offer, success metric, and decision rule before launch, then scale or move to the next experiment based on results.
•    Build and execute campaigns, nurture tracks, and outbound sequences against enriched, scored segments, partnering with the Digital Marketing Manager on creative and channel execution.
•    Use customer, competitive, and market insight to surface new segments and opportunities worth testing, and maintain a prioritized backlog and a visible results log so learnings compound.
Lifecycle & In-App Engagement
•    Own lifecycle programs across the customer journey: onboarding, activation, feature adoption, cross-sell and expansion, renewal, and win-back.
•    Build behavior-triggered journeys that combine CRM email and telemetry in-app guides, driven by product usage signals rather than calendar cadence alone.
•    Partner with Product and Customer Growth to identify adoption gaps and cross-sell opportunities across our product portfolio, and run the programs that close them.
Funnel Reporting & Measurement
•    Support maintenance of funnel stage definitions and conversion logic from first touch through closed-won, activation, and expansion.
•    Build and own dashboards and recurring funnel reporting for RevOps and leadership, covering pipeline, conversion rates, velocity, channel and campaign performance, and product adoption.
•    Set attribution and experiment measurement standards, and translate the numbers into clear recommendations on where to invest next. We care about great marketing, but ultimately we care about whether it drives growth.
What Success Looks Like
•
First 90 days:
You've aligned with product leadership on positioning for priority products; audited HubSpot data, lifecycle stages, and routing; published agreed funnel definitions; shipped a baseline funnel dashboard; and launched your first experiments.
•
First 6 months:
Enrichment and scoring are live and routing leads to Sales and Customer Growth against defined SLAs; core onboarding and adoption journeys are running across email and in-app; and experiments ship on a steady cadence with documented results.
•
First 12 months:
Every feature release runs through a repeatable launch playbook executed in the stack; conversion, speed-to-lead, and product adoption show measurable lift; and leadership uses your funnel reporting to make investment decisions.
You'll Probably Love This Role If…
•    You're a builder who loves making the machine work, not just drawing the diagram. You'd rather ship the test than debate it.
•    You're curious about customers, competitors, and markets and naturally find yourself asking, “Where's the opportunity here?”
•    You read a feature release and immediately think about the segment, the trigger, the channel, and the metric.
•    Messy CRM data bothers you, and you'd rather fix it at the source than patch it in a spreadsheet.
•    You think in funnels and can explain, in plain language, why a conversion rate moved.
•    You use AI as a force multiplier in real workflows, from enrichment and scoring to research and content variants, and you know where it helps and where it doesn't.
•    You’re a natural collaborative and aren’t afraid to step outside of the RevOps team to work with Product, Sales, Customer Growth, and leadership.
•    You're comfortable owning your work end to end without needing a huge team around you.
•    You're excited to build the GTM engine rather than inherit a finished one.
Required Qualifications
•    4+ years in growth marketing, lifecycle marketing, marketing operations, revenue operations, or GTM engineering or a related B2B SaaS role.
•    Hands-on CRM management/ownership as an admin or power user, including properties, lifecycle stages, workflows, lists, scoring, and reporting.
•    Experience partnering with product leadership to define positioning and value propositions, and a proven ability to translate individual features into audience-specific messaging deployed across campaigns, lifecycle programs, in-app experiences, and sales enablement.
•    Experience building data enrichment, lead scoring, and routing, including AI or predictive scoring approaches.
•    A track record of designing and running demand-gen experiments with clear hypotheses, success metrics, and documented outcomes.
•    Experience building behavior-triggered lifecycle programs across email and in-app channels.
•    Strong funnel reporting and analytics skills: defining stages and conversion metrics, building dashboards, and working comfortably with data in spreadsheets or BI tools.
•    Clear, concise writing, from lifecycle copy to experiment readouts to leadership summaries.
•    Strong project management and systems thinking, with a habit of documenting what you build.
•    A builder mentality and the ability to move comfortably between strategy and hands-on execution.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with CACFP, childcare, child nutrition, education, government programs, or other regulated industries is a huge plus, but not a requirement.
CACFP has its own language, regulations, acronyms, and complexities. If you already know it, amazing. If you don't, you'll be surrounded by an exceptional team of people who do, and we'll help you get up to speed.
A few other things we'd love to see:
•    Experience with vertical SaaS, multi-product portfolios, or marketing to both SMB and enterprise or public-sector buyers.
•    CRM certifications (Marketing, Sales, or Operations related) or hands-on experience with CRM AI and data enrichment features.
•    Hands-on experience with in-app engagement or product adoption platforms
•    Experience with enrichment and GTM automation tools
•    Technical comfort beyond the UI: SQL, APIs and webhooks, or light scripting (JavaScript or Python) to connect systems and automate workflows.
•    Comfort building AI-powered workflows for research, enrichment, scoring, and content variation. You know how to make AI your copilot, not your copywriter.
Why KidKare?
We're at an exciting inflection point, taking decades of experience in childcare and child nutrition and using it to build a broader ecosystem of products for the organizations and people who help care for our communities.
You won't be starting from scratch. We've invested deeply in understanding our customers, markets, competitors, and products. But we're not handing you a finished machine and asking you to keep it running.
We want you to build the engine that powers what comes next.
If you want to own the systems, run the experiments, build the lifecycle, measure the funnel, and see exactly how your work moves pipeline and adoption, you'll have plenty to dig into here.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
That is the whole job.
Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
Here is what "end to end" actually means.
You are the account manager. We do not have any.
You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.
Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.
We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
You can live anywhere.
We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
Requirements
What the job looks like
Own a set of DTC accounts
as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
Own the client relationship.
There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
Audit before you touch anything.
Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
Run brand and non brand as different businesses.
Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
Know what PMax is actually doing.
The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
Keep Google's automation on a leash.
Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
Own the feed.
Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
Own the tracking.
GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.
Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
Build the things the account needs.
Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
You are a fit if
You have done this with real money.
Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
You are fluent in the whole stack
, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
You are AI native, and you build.
This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.
You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
You are skeptical of your own numbers.
You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.
Where you live is up to you.
Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
You are not a fit if
"That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
You want to be told what to do this week.
You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
Benefits
Why this role is exciting
This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
That is the whole job.
Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
Here is what "end to end" actually means.
You are the account manager. We do not have any.
You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.
Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.
We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
You can live anywhere.
We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
Requirements
What the job looks like
Own a set of DTC accounts
as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
Own the client relationship.
There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
Audit before you touch anything.
Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
Run brand and non brand as different businesses.
Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
Know what PMax is actually doing.
The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
Keep Google's automation on a leash.
Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
Own the feed.
Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
Own the tracking.
GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.
Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
Build the things the account needs.
Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
You are a fit if
You have done this with real money.
Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
You are fluent in the whole stack
, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
You are AI native, and you build.
This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.
You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
You are skeptical of your own numbers.
You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.
Where you live is up to you.
Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
You are not a fit if
"That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
You want to be told what to do this week.
You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
Benefits
Why this role is exciting
This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

Dispatch is redefining how the world experiences home and field service. Founded in 2013 and trusted by leading brands and service providers, we power seamless, reliable service experiences through a modern platform built for scale. With the acquisition of Youreka in 2023, Dispatch expanded its capabilities to include a leading Salesforce-native Smart Forms application that equips mobile workers with guided workflows, improves field execution and customer service, and scales to support complex enterprise operations.
As part of Manos Software, a Valsoft operating group, Dispatch combines the focus and agility of a specialized software company with the long-term support of a global vertical SaaS organization. We're investing in our product, our customers, and our team with a focus on sustainable, profitable growth.
We're now investing in a dedicated marketing function to match the strength of our product and customer base, and we're hiring our first Director of Demand Generation to build it.
THE ROLE:
Reporting directly to the CEO, the Director of Demand Generation will own demand generation for Dispatch and Youreka, reshaping what marketing means for the company and our products. This role also owns our Business Development Representative team's strategy and targets, working primarily through our existing BDR team lead. This is a hands-on, builder role: you'll set strategy and run campaigns yourself in the early days, then pursue growth within the marketing team as the function proves out.
AS THE DIRECTOR OF DEMAND GENERATION, YOU WILL:
Demand generation & growth - assess Dispatch's situation from first principles to determine where marketing should focus (paid acquisition, lifecycle/email, organic, and other channels); own the marketing automation and CRM stack; generate and manage a healthy, measurable pipeline in close partnership with sales. Building this out is the top priority for this role.
Product-market fit & positioning - identify, through testing and analysis, which segments, use cases, and messages actually convert; use that to sharpen demand-gen targeting and messaging, and share findings with our Product Marketing team to inform their formal positioning work.
Content - build a content engine (website copy, case studies, thought leadership) that supports demand generation and conversion.
Team leadership - own strategy and targets for our BDR team, working closely with the existing Lead BDR and aligning team output with the broader demand generation strategy. You will also manage an existing marketing team resource and help define future role additions over time.
Diagnose marketing channel mix for Dispatch's products - prioritizing investment accordingly.
Establish the processes, reporting, and KPIs the function will run on.
WITHIN THE FIRST SIX MONTHS, YOU WILL:
Build a functioning marketing engine - team, tools, and process, revamped from a lean starting point and working closely with our Senior Marketing Manager.
Define a clear, data-backed point of view on where Dispatch should focus its marketing investment, measurable pipeline/revenue contribution from marketing, and BDR-driven programs.
Develop sharper product positioning and messaging along with marketing support delivered for major product launches and market expansions.
Be viewed internally and externally as a strategic leader for Dispatch's growth functions.
LOCATION:
Dispatch fully accommodates remote work, as long as you have a permanent residence in the US and reside in one of our registered states. Want to spend a month in Italy? Great, do it! Live in Idaho? Sweet, we have another team member there! As long as you are crushing your goals and helping us drive the business forward, you do you. We also have an office in Boston that is open and available for you to use.
SALARY:
The base salary range for this role is between $160,000 - $170,000 annually. Actual pay within the range is influenced by multiple factors, including but not limited to skill set, residence location, and prior work experience. In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for an annual bonus and benefits.
Requirements
5–10 years of marketing experience including specific focus on demand generation and program definition.
A startup-tested operator - comfortable being hands-on and building programs with limited resources, not just directing an existing team.
A proven track record of owning a marketing function or team from an early stage.
Proven, hands-on experience managing a demand-generation/marketing function is required. Experience managing a team on a sales-style comp plan - such as a BDR, SDR, or inside-sales function - is a plus.
An analytical, first-principles thinker who can diagnose which channels and tactics actually drive results for a given business, rather than defaulting to a standard playbook - we're counting on you to help define our ideal marketing mix, not just execute one.
A strong written communicator who can turn technical or operational product value into compelling brand and content narratives.
B2B SaaS experience preferred; experience in field service, home services, or enterprise software is a plus.
Benefits
WE HAVE:
An amazing team focused on innovating and improving every day

Rockstar is recruiting for a marketplace management firm that handles e-commerce operations for brands across major retail channels. They specialize in catalog management, content, retail operations, and advertising on platforms like Amazon, Walmart, and Target Plus. Their AI Agentic Commerce practice builds proprietary tooling for optimized performance.
About the Company
The company manages the marketplace business for brands that can't afford to get it wrong. They handle catalog, content, retail operations, and advertising across Amazon (Seller Central and Vendor Central), Walmart Marketplace, Target Plus, and other emerging channels, and they run an AI Agentic Commerce practice building their own tooling for this work.
Their clients span consumer packaged goods, cosmetics, skincare, apparel, footwear, and handbags. They hire them to operate their channel, not to advise from a distance.
The Role
Advertising Analysts run the accounts. This is the seat where the work actually happens.
Analysts own the day-to-day management of advertising for a set of client brands across Amazon, Walmart Marketplace, and Target Plus — building campaigns, managing bids and budgets, adjusting targeting, watching pacing, and finding the changes that move performance. Their manager sets the strategy and the media plan; they make it real in the platform, and they are the first person to know when something isn't working.
This is an individual contributor role, but it isn't a heads-down one. Analysts work directly with the Strategy & Implementation Team on retail readiness — inventory, catalog, promotions, detail page quality — and with the Design Team on creative for Sponsored Brands, video, and display. Advertising in these channels doesn't perform in isolation, and analysts who understand that make better recommendations than analysts who only look at ad reports.
Analysts also do a meaningful amount of thinking, not just executing. They run account audits, dig into search term and placement data to find waste and opportunity, build the analysis behind quarterly and annual business reviews, and prepare the decks their manager presents to client leadership. Where they see a better answer than the plan calls for, the company wants to hear it.
The company expects analysts to use AI in their work. The team uses AI for report analysis, bulk file preparation, keyword and search term work, audit drafting, and internal tooling. They don't need to be an engineer, but they should be comfortable working with AI tools and interested in using them to get through the mechanical parts of the job faster so they can spend more time on the parts that require judgment.
This role is a path to account and strategy ownership. The analysts who do it well are the people the company promotes.
What You'll Own
Campaign management and optimization:
Build, launch, and manage Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, Sponsored Brands Video, Sponsored Display, and Amazon DSP campaigns, plus their Walmart Connect and Target Roundel equivalents. Manage bids, budgets, negatives, placement modifiers, and dayparting against agreed targets. Keep pacing on plan and flag risk before it becomes a shortfall.
Keyword, targeting, and audience work:
Research and build keyword and product targeting sets, mine search term reports for new opportunity and wasted spend, and maintain clean negative structures. Support audience building and testing in DSP.
Analysis:
Pull and interrogate the data yourself — search term, placement, product-level, and business reports — and turn it into a recommendation rather than a summary. Understand why a number moved, not just that it did.
Account audits:
Perform structured audits on new and existing accounts: campaign architecture, targeting overlap, budget allocation, wasted spend, missed placements, and gaps between what the account is doing and what the strategy calls for. Write up findings clearly enough that someone else can act on them.
Client reporting and business reviews:
Build the reporting that keeps clients informed, and prepare the analysis and decks for quarterly and annual business reviews. Your work goes in front of client leadership, so it needs to be accurate, clear, and defensible.
AI-assisted workflows:
Use AI tools to speed up analysis, bulk file work, keyword processing, and documentation. Contribute to improving how the team works rather than just following the process you were handed.
Collaboration:
Partner with the Strategy & Implementation Team on retail readiness and the Design Team on creative. Raise the constraints — inventory, catalog, pricing, page quality — that advertising can't fix on its own.
What You Bring
Required
2+ years hands-on experience building, managing, and optimizing Amazon advertising campaigns
Amazon Ads certification in Sponsored Ads and Amazon DSP (both required; verified)
Experience with Amazon DSP campaign management, not just Sponsored Ads
Genuinely analytical: comfortable in large data sets, can build your own analysis in Excel or Sheets, and check your own math
Intellectual curiosity: want to know why something happened, and keep pulling the thread after the immediate question is answered
Strong written and verbal communication: can explain a performance change in plain language and write findings a client can read
Proficiency working with AI tools and AI-assisted workflows
Detail discipline: bulk uploads, naming conventions, and negatives done right the first time
Preferred
Walmart Sponsored Ads and Walmart DSP certification
Meta and TikTok ads experience, with certifications
Target Roundel experience
SQL, Looker Studio / Google Data Studio, or Amazon Marketing Cloud exposure
Agency or multi-brand experience across categories
Advanced Excel; Python or scripting a plus
Familiarity with retail fundamentals: Buy Box, inventory health, catalog integrity, promotions, subscriptions
Who Does Well Here
The work is cyclical and the peaks are demanding — Q4 and Prime Day compress a quarter of decisions into a few weeks. The analysts who do well here treat a bad week as something to diagnose rather than defend, and would rather find the problem themselves than be told about it.
The company also looks for ownership (escalate early and don't lose things), intellectual honesty (would rather be corrected than confidently wrong), care about accuracy, and a habit of fixing a manual process the third time you run it.
What Success Looks Like
30 days:
Managing daily optimizations on your accounts with light supervision, and you know each brand's structure, targets, and constraints.
90 days:
Running your accounts independently, delivering audits and reporting your manager doesn't have to rewrite, and surfacing recommendations rather than waiting for direction.
12 months:
Your accounts show measurable improvement you can explain, you're trusted in front of clients, and you've improved at least one thing about how the team works.
How to Stand Out
Come ready to walk through one account you improved — what you found, what you changed, and how you knew it worked.

Hi there, I'm Mehak, interim Head of Marketing at TestGorilla. We’re excited to share more about the Sr. Demand Generation Manager role and our team.

About the role

As our Sr. Demand Generation Manager, you'll be essential in achieving TestGorilla's vision of helping one billion people land their dream job. You'll own our largest acquisition lever, a multi-six-figure monthly Google Ads investment, along with the lifecycle, enrichment, and website systems that turn that spend into revenue. This isn't just a role, it's your chance to make a real difference by proving, with data, that every dollar of spend becomes pipeline. You'll directly contribute to sustainable, cost-efficient growth as TestGorilla scales.

Responsibilities

In this role, your responsibilities will include but not limited to:

- Upholding TestGorilla's behaviors and fostering an inclusive, supportive culture.

- Owning the demand generation number across paid and organic channels, including managing and scaling paid spend across Google Ads (Search, Performance Max, Display, YouTube) and adjacent channels, while testing and developing emerging acquisition opportunities such as advertising on ChatGPT and other AI-native platforms. Setting the channel mix, budget allocation, and account structure required to hit MQL, SQO, and pipeline targets.

- Building and owning source-of-truth reporting across paid and organic funnel performance, including SQL, dashboards, attribution modeling, and incrementality testing, so channel investment decisions are backed by evidence rather than platform screenshots.

- Owning the roadmap for paid landing pages, ad creative, and offers, and running rapid A/B tests to lift conversion with proper statistical rigor.

- Designing and owning automated nurture workflows and enrichment infrastructure (n8n, Make, HubSpot, Clay) so paid-sourced leads convert, and feeding that data back into targeting and ICP decisions.

- Partnering with Sales and RevOps on lead quality and conversion by campaign, and presenting performance and recommendations to marketing and GTM leadership in clear, business-first language.

- Staying ahead of advertising platform, AI ecosystem, and privacy changes, and turning successful tests into repeatable, automated systems rather than one-off wins.

What you’ll bring

We're looking for someone who:

- Is passionate about TestGorilla's mission to help one billion people find their dream jobs.

- Has excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

- Thrives in a fast-paced, async-first, remote-only environment.

- Has proven experience in performance or growth marketing, including hands-on ownership of a Google Ads budget of at least six figures per month (B2B SaaS strongly preferred), and a track record of scaling spend while holding or improving CAC and ROAS.

  - _We typically expect 7+ years of experience in performance or growth marketing to have developed the core skills necessary for this position. But it may be more or less than that, according to your career journey so far._
- Has deep expertise across the Google Ads stack, including Search, Performance Max, Display, YouTube, Smart Bidding, conversion tracking, and Google Tag Manager.

- Working knowledge and hands-on expertise of Clay, HubSpot (or a comparable CRM) and GA suite.

- Has a solid grasp of funnel and unit economics (CAC, LTV:CAC, ROAS, payback period, cohort analysis) and comfort with experimentation design, including significance, sample sizing, and reading results honestly.

- Has hands-on experience using AI/LLM tools (Claude, ChatGPT, or similar) to build real growth workflows, from lead scoring to automation logic, not just surface-level use.

- Has an ownership mentality: treats this budget like their own P&L, ships the workflow, dashboard, and test themselves, and is comfortable with ambiguity and fast iteration as pipeline needs shift.

Deseret Book is a mission-driven company, committed to being a trusted gathering place for thoughtful expressions of faith. In our work culture, we put people first. Our team members are dedicated to meeting the needs of our communities as we work together, creating an environment where collaboration is critical and personal accountability is expected. The Opportunity

Deseret Book Company is a leading retailer and publisher of faith-centered books, media, and products, operating retail stores, a robust ecommerce platform (DeseretBook.com), and Bookshelf+, our growing digital subscription service. We're looking for a Digital Marketing Manager to serve as the operational backbone of our growth and lifecycle marketing efforts.

Position Summary

We're seeking a detail-driven, analytically sharp Digital Marketing Manager to own execution of growth campaigns, lifecycle marketing, paid and organic media coordination, and cross-functional project management. This is not a strategy-only role, you'll be hands-on building launch plans, coordinating across internal teams and external vendors, managing timelines, running A/B tests, and reporting on performance with clear, actionable insights.

This role works at the intersection of ecommerce, retail, product, development, creative, and media. If marketing campaigns are the engine, this role keeps every piston firing on time, on spec, and on budget — while continuously finding ways to make the engine run faster.

Core Responsibilities

Growth Campaigns & Conversion

- Translate growth strategies into integrated launch plans across paid media, email, social, retail, and owned channels.

- Lead execution of gifting, referral, and conversion-funnel initiatives end-to-end.

- Partner with Ecommerce, Retail, Product, and Development to optimize landing pages, checkout, and post-purchase experiences.

- Own pre-launch QA — links, pixels, promo codes, UTMs confirmed before every launch.

Lifecycle Marketing & Retention

- Partner with Email Marketing Strategist on automated journeys (onboarding, post-purchase, retention, win-back) for DeseretBook.com and Bookshelf+.

- Define audience segments; develop and run A/B tests; apply findings to improve lifecycle performance.

- Track engagement, conversion, retention, and revenue across all lifecycle programs.

Paid, Organic & Traditional Media Coordination

- Coordinate paid, organic, and traditional media campaigns — deliver assets, confirm specs/timelines, ensure tracking is live.

- Evaluate channel performance (impressions, engagement, ROAS, cross-channel lift); surface insights for media mix decisions.

Marketing Promotions

- Manage print/offline placements (package inserts, magalogs, QR codes, trackable URLs) with same tracking rigor as digital.

Project, Vendor & Cross-Functional Management

- Own timelines, requirements, testing, approvals, and launch readiness across concurrent campaigns.

- Serve as day-to-day contact for developers, production partners, and media vendors.

- Maintain campaign documentation in Asana; proactively surface risks and resolve gaps.

Performance Reporting & Optimization

- Maintain weekly performance reporting across all assigned campaigns and Deliver weekly performance reports with clear insights and action plans — not just data.

- Monitor conversion rate, CPA, engagement, referral activity, scan rates, retention, and attributed revenue.

Qualifications

- 5–7 years in digital/growth/performance marketing (retail, ecommerce, or subscription preferred).

- Hands-on experience executing integrated campaigns across paid media, email, social, and owned channels.

- Strong lifecycle/retention marketing skills, automated journeys, segmentation, A/B testing.

- Proven ability to manage complex, multi-team projects with concurrent timelines.

- Proficient with GA4, UTM/conversion tracking, attribution models, and email platforms (MailChimp, Klaviyo, or equivalent).

- Comfortable with Asana (strongly preferred) and external vendor coordination.

- Detail-oriented, specs, timelines, and tracking must be right.

- Strong written communication, clear briefs, concise reports, actionable recommendations.

- Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, or related field.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience in faith-based, book/publishing, or family-oriented consumer brands.

- Familiarity with subscription business models and subscriber lifecycle management (acquisition, onboarding, retention, win-back).

- Experience with referral and gifting program mechanics.

- Familiarity with retail marketing (in-store materials, package inserts, magalogs).

- Experience with Tapfiliate or other affiliate tracking platforms.

- Exposure to app-based marketing (push notifications, in-app messaging, app store optimization).

When buyers ask whether 6sense is accurate, extensible, secure, and composable, the answer lives here.

We're looking for a Principal Technical Product Marketing Manager to own positioning, messaging, and go-to-market for the Foundation pillar. This is the most technical seat on the PMM team. You'll translate deep capabilities — identity resolution, data coverage and accuracy, API extensibility, the MCP framework, security and compliance — into differentiated stories that win over the technical and economic buyers who scrutinize them: RevOps architects, IT and security teams, data leaders, and increasingly developers building agentic GTM stacks.

You'll also carry one of the most strategically important narratives in the company: that 6sense is a composable intelligence layer other systems and AI agents plug into — "AI to the data, not data to the AI" — rather than a closed destination. With the MCP framework moving to GA, this is a present-tense story, and you'll be the one who tells it credibly.

What You'll Own

- Positioning and messaging for the Foundation pillar — platform, data, infrastructure, identity and matching, APIs and the MCP framework, security and connectors, signal publication, and workflows. You set the narrative and keep it coherent with the Intelligence and Activation pillars.

- Cross-functional partnership. Work shoulder-to-shoulder with the Foundation Product and Engineering leaders to shape roadmap-to-market, and with Customer Success to surface the post-sale and admin/security use cases that prove the platform's breadth.
- Market and competitive intelligence for the data and platform layer, feeding insight back into roadmap and pricing/packaging conversations.

* * *

What You'll Bring

- 8+ years in product marketing, technical product management, or a closely related function, with substantial technical PMM experience for platform, data, infrastructure, API, or developer products.
- A proven ability to translate technical concepts — APIs, data pipelines, identity resolution, integrations, security, and AI/agent architectures like MCP — into crisp positioning and business value, without losing the engineers in the room or the buyers outside it.
- A track record owning messaging for technical products and enabling technical sales motions (Sales Engineering, RFPs, security reviews, POCs).
- Hands-on, not hand-wavy. You'll personally call the APIs, stand up and configure the MCP server, connect it to an agent, and build the demo — and your messaging is sharper because you've done the thing, not just read the spec.
- Strong writing — you can produce content that is technically rigorous and genuinely clear, from a one-line value prop to an architecture whitepaper.
- Fluency with the B2B SaaS buyer, ideally in martech, RevTech, or data platforms, and comfort selling to technical and economic buyers (RevOps architects, IT, security, data teams, developers).

Nice to Have

- Experience marketing to developers or technical evaluators, including documentation-adjacent and developer-community work.
- Background in or adjacent to GTM intelligence, ABM, sales intelligence, CDP, iPaaS, or identity platforms.

* * *

What Success Looks Like

In your first 6–12 months, Foundation has a differentiated, defensible position that technical buyers recognize; the composable/MCP infrastructure story is landed with the field and the market as something that exists today, not a roadmap promise; the data and identity credibility story is substantiated with proof, not assertion; and the field has the enablement to win the technical evaluation every time it comes.

- Analytical Rigor: Asks the hard questions and traces discrepancies to the source before drawing conclusions.
- Reporting Ownership: Engages stakeholders to understand how reporting is used before building, i.e. creates dashboards that are adopted, not just delivered.

- Curiosity & Growth: Asks more than most and is driven to grow from technical executor into analytical partner over time.

WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. BASE SALARY: $120,000 to $150,000 per year, paid semi-monthly

MUST HAVE:

- Expert SQL & Comfortable with Unstructured Complex Data: Extracts accurate insights from raw, unstructured data without relying on clean models
- Reporting Ownership & Data Literacy: Builds, standardizes, drives adoption, and leaves teams more data-literate
- Performance Marketing Optimization: Connects data directly to levers that move the business, i.e. campaign performance, conversion rates, or revenue per session

This is NOT a role for someone who wants to build dashboards and hand them off, it's for someone who cares deeply about whether the work they build gets used, understood, and acted on.

Outcomes (Performance Expectations)

- 30 Days in: Actively engaged with stakeholders to audit what reporting the team is consuming and why, i.e. identifying discrepancies, redundancies, and inconsistencies across existing dashboards and beginning to develop a roadmap to standardize reporting across your verticals.
- 60 Days in: Bridging business context and data understanding by being able to articulate how assigned verticals make money and what the key performance levers are. Actively improving dashboard standardization while executing on ad hoc requests with accuracy and business context.
- 90 Days in: Dashboard standardization is in execution and a clear roadmap exists for how trusted data sources will be developed to improve the efficiency of data consumption. LookML structure is understood well enough to begin making changes with full awareness of downstream impacts. Working relationships with Yield, Paid Media, and Account Management are established.
- 6 Months in: Trust is built with the business team through education, best practices, and a standardized reporting suite that enables confident self-service analytics. Proactive retrospective analyses are being delivered across experiments, creatives, offers, seasonality, and CAC performance. Strong understanding of the full funnel metrics that support each team.
- Year 1: Trusted technical owner for assigned verticals end-to-end, from raw data ingestion through final dashboard. Reporting standardization is complete, retrospective analysis is a consistent output, and the business team views you as a go-to analytical partner who recommends action, not just reports findings.

Competencies

- Analytical Rigor: Asks the hard questions and traces discrepancies to the source before drawing conclusions.
- Reporting Ownership: Engages stakeholders to understand how reporting is used before building, i.e. creates dashboards that are adopted, not just delivered.
- Business Acumen: Invests in understanding the business by asking the right questions before pulling the data.
- Communication: Asks enough upfront to make sure the answer lands with the right context for the right audience.
- Proactive Ownership: Surfaces problems early, engages before being asked, and drives work forward with a clear point of view.
- Collaboration: Builds trust by asking genuine questions and showing they care about what stakeholders need, not just what they asked for.
- Curiosity & Growth: Asks more than most and is driven to grow from technical executor into analytical partner over time.

TOTAL COMPENSATION

Base salary is set according to market rates for the nearest major metro and varies based on Launch Potato’s Levels Framework. Your compensation package includes a base salary, profit-sharing bonus, and competitive benefits. Launch Potato is a performance-driven company, which means once you are hired, future increases will be based on company and personal performance, not annual cost of living adjustments.

Senior Marketing Data Analyst

Remote, USA

Apply

Twin Health

At Twin Health, we empower people to improve and prevent chronic metabolic diseases, like type 2 diabetes and obesity, with a new standard of care. Twin Health is the only company applying AI Digital Twin technology exclusively toward metabolic health.

We start by building a dynamic model of each person’s metabolism — drawing on thousands of data points from CGMs, smartwatches, and meal logs — that maps their personal path to better health. Guided by a dedicated clinical care team, our members have lowered their A1C below the diabetes range, achieved lasting weight loss, and reduced or even eliminated medications, all while living healthier, happier lives.

Working here

Our team at Twin Health is passionate, talented, and united by a shared purpose: to improve the metabolic health and happiness of our members. We believe in empowering every Twin to make a meaningful impact for our members, our clients, and each other, while enjoying a supportive, collaborative work environment.

Twin has been recognized not only for our innovation but also for our culture, including: Innovator of the Year by the Employer Health Innovation Roundtable (EHIR), selected to CB Insights’ Digital Health 150, and named one of Newsweek’s Top Most Loved Workplace® .

With more than $100 million raised in recent funding, including a $53 million Series E round in 2025 led by Maj Invest, and a $50 million investment in 2023 led by Temasek, Twin is scaling rapidly across the U.S. and globally. Backed by leading venture firms like ICONIQ Growth, Sequoia, Sofina, Temasek, and Peak XV, we are building the most impactful digital health company in the world.

Join us as we reinvent the standard of care in metabolic health.

Opportunity

marketing channels: email, direct mail, and digital. This role sits at the intersection of marketing strategy, data, and technical execution. You will turn raw campaign and behavioral data into clear analysis that drives decisions at every level, from channel owners to the executive team.

Right now, the first priority is to understand performance before we optimize it. In your first year you will establish trusted, consistent performance baselines across channels, find where the data does not add up, and tell us what is working and what is not. As that foundation matures, the role grows into attribution, marketing mix, and scoring models that guide budget allocation and targeting.

Our data foundation is built by our data engineering team. You will be its most demanding user. You will query across sources to answer marketing questions, find the gaps and inconsistencies others miss, and tell the data team what needs to be tracked, modeled, or fixed so the next question is easier to answer.

This role is for someone whose edge is judgment. You know what to ask before you write the query, you notice when an answer does not add up, and you give the marketing team a recommendation they can act on. It is a hands-on, high-impact individual contributor role for someone who works independently in a fast-moving environment and is equally comfortable digging through a warehouse and presenting to senior leaders.

Responsibilities

Channel Performance Measurement & Analytics

- Measure and report on performance across email, direct mail, and digital — defining the right metrics, building reporting, and surfacing what is working and what is not
- Own digital analytics end to end, including event tracking and tagging strategy, and partner with engineering to ensure data is captured accurately across web and app properties
- Build and maintain attribution and marketing mix models to quantify channel contribution and guide budget allocation across the marketing portfolio
- Analyze paid channel performance — spend efficiency, ROAS, and incrementality — and translate findings into clear optimization recommendations

Decision support for performance marketing

- Partner with channel owners to turn campaign goals into specific, testable questions, and answer them with analysis before launch, while campaigns are in flight, and after they close
- Analyze channel mix, budget allocation, and pacing using CPM, CPC, CAC, conversion rate, and ROAS, and recommend where to shift spend
- Profile audiences across multiple data sources to size and describe segments for targeting, and recommend who to reach and with what message
- Analyze funnels and landing page performance from impression through registration to enrollment, and recommend conversion rate improvements

Data quality and the data foundation

- Write complex SQL to explore, join, and reconcile data across the warehouse and martech platforms, and validate queries drafted with AI assistance
- Question the data: find gaps, conflicting definitions, and tracking breaks, reconcile numbers across platforms, and raise issues with the specifics the data team needs to fix them
- Define requirements for data engineering, including the events, facts, dimensions, and metric definitions needed to support attribution, mix modeling, and scoring in the future, and explain why each one matters
- Document the metric definitions and logic the marketing team relies on

Data Science & Advanced Modeling

- These responsibilities build on the measurement foundation above. Expect to start by evaluating and directing this work, and to take on more of the build as the data matures.
- Own marketing mix modeling (MMM) end to end — building, validating, and refreshing models that quantify channel contribution, diminishing returns, and saturation to guide budget allocation
- Develop propensity and other scoring models to predict member behavior — conversion, churn, and engagement — and operationalize scores to drive targeting, segmentation, and lifecycle marketing
- Apply Bayesian network analysis and related probabilistic methods to model relationships between marketing drivers and outcomes, quantify uncertainty, and support causal and incrementality analysis
- Partner with data engineering to productionize models, monitor performance over time, and ensure outputs are reliable, explainable, and decision-ready for leadership

Experimentation and testing

- Design, run, and read A/B and multivariate tests, including sample sizing, significance, and interpretation, and recommend what to test next
- Help establish testing standards and maintain a prioritized roadmap of experiments
- Insights and communication
- Present findings and recommendations to marketing leadership and the executive team in a clear, decision-ready way
- Partner with marketing, engineering, data engineering, finance, and product to align on definitions, attribution, and measurement standards
- Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

- 8+ years in marketing analytics, performance marketing analytics, data analytics, or a closely related field
- Sound analytical judgment, shown by examples where you reframed a question, found a flaw in the data, or changed a decision
- Proven experience measuring email, direct mail, and digital marketing performance, including channel mix, budget allocation, CPM, CAC, ROAS, and conversion rate optimization
- Comfort writing and validating complex SQL against a cloud data warehouse (Snowflake preferred), with or without AI assistance. Data engineering is not part of this role.
- Working knowledge of attribution, marketing mix modeling, incrementality, and paid channel analysis
- Experience with scoring and predictive models, such as propensity models, marketing mix models, or Bayesian methods, and with applying them to real marketing decisions. Depth in at least one of these and a working understanding of the others.
- Working knowledge of tracking and instrumentation (UTMs, pixels, tag managers, event taxonomy) and of data modeling concepts such as facts and dimensions, enough to specify requirements and spot problems
- Solid understanding of A/B testing: experiment design, sample sizing, significance, and interpretation

Compensation
