Company Description

Dropbox isn’t just a workplace—it’s a living lab for designing a more enlightened way of working. We’re a global community of bold visionaries and resourceful doers shaping the future of Dropbox and, in turn, the future of work. Our Virtual First model combines the autonomy of a distributed workplace with the power of human connection, creating space for meaningful work and lasting relationships. With a startup mindset and enterprise-level opportunities, we expect Dropbox employees to think critically, stay curious, and use modern tools, including AI, to improve how work gets done. Here, you can be who you are and grow into who you’re meant to be. You own your impact, helping make work more intuitive, joyful, and human for yourself and hundreds of millions of people worldwide. If you’re ready to push boundaries and challenge yourself, Dropbox is ready for you.

Team Description

The Dropbox Marketing Team shows the world how Dropbox makes work better. We're storytellers and strategists, exploring new ways to connect our products with the people who need them. From product launches to campaign strategy, message positioning to digital marketing, we blend creativity with data-driven insights to build our brand and grow our impact. Working across disciplines, you will tap into your own inventiveness while collaborating with teams throughout the organization, including Product, Sales and Engineering. If you're excited about translating complex technologies into engaging narratives and shaping how the world understands and experiences Dropbox, join our Marketing team.

Virtual First

Dropbox’s Virtual First way of working is designed to help people do their best work with flexibility, autonomy, and connection. Day to day, teams work remotely with nonlinear schedules and core collaboration hours that support deep focus and individual working styles. We prioritize asynchronous communication to improve clarity, respect deep work time, and reduce unnecessary meetings. While remote work is the primary experience for our employees, we also prioritize intentional, in-person connection. We bring teams together through regular team gatherings, on-demand workspaces, and Dropbox Neighborhood events in order to strengthen team cohesion, foster creativity, and enhance momentum. Virtual First is built to provide the same access to opportunity, growth, and impact for everyone, regardless of location.

This role requires travel to offsites and various other team gatherings (approximately 5-10% of the year or 2-3 days per quarter). We provide advance notice when possible and encourage candidates to discuss any accommodation needs during the interview process.

AI Fluency

AI fluency is a core part of how we work and grow. It’s not about being an expert—it’s about using these tools thoughtfully and effectively to improve your work and support others.

We look for four key behaviors in candidates:

- Ownership: You use AI responsibly by protecting data, applying sound judgment, and taking accountability for the quality and accuracy of your work.
- Experimentation: You explore new AI capabilities and apply them to improve workflows within approved tools and practices.
- Leverage: You use AI to enhance thinking, improve efficiency, and increase your impact and your team’s.
- Learning: You stay current on emerging AI tools and trends, continuously build your skills, and share what you learn with others.

Together, these behaviors help build a workforce where technology amplifies human judgment, creativity, and impact.

Dropbox supports responsible use of AI for preparation, but misrepresentation of skills or experience is not permitted. To learn more, see our approach to AI in hiring.

In your first year, you'll consolidate our sending onto Customer.io, map and rebuild the journeys for each owner segment, and turn a set of disconnected sends into a measured system that drives two key metrics: qualified lead conversion and six-month owner retention. This is an owner-operator role. You'll be as comfortable building and debugging a journey in the platform and writing email copy as you are presenting strategy to leadership. We are looking for a senior individual-contributor on a small, flat team where you'll lead through clarity and evidence rather than headcount.

The team

What you'll do

Lifecycle Strategy & Journeys

- Own owner lifecycle marketing end-to-end—every scheduled and triggered message an owner receives, from their first information request through onboarding, their first 180 days, and beyond.

- Expand lifecycle channels beyond email and SMS. In-product nudges, push notifications, help content, and timed sales or onboarding touchpoints should all form a cohesive journey.

Platform & Infrastructure

- Lead the migration of owner communications from legacy platforms to Customer.io, establishing build standards and governance to prevent future fragmentation.
- Build segmentation and triggers based on real-time behavior and performance signals (e.g., owner actions, listing status, drop-off points) rather than fixed send calendars.

Pre-Activation Nurture & Recovery

- Optimize conversion across under-engaged lead segments, ensuring structured touchpoints exist long after initial contact.

Analytics & Optimization

Cross-Functional Partnership

- Partner cross-functionally with sales, product, onboarding, support, and analytics to translate complex operational updates into clear owner communications.

What makes you a great fit

- 7+ years of experience in lifecycle, CRM, or retention marketing for consumer or prosumer audiences, with proven ownership of multi-stage journeys
- Hands-on expertise with enterprise marketing automation platforms (Customer.io, Braze, Iterable, Marketo, or similar), including building, deploying, debugging, and optimizing journeys directly

Opportunity

Today, Twin Health does almost no proactive marketing to our active members. Once someone enrolls, nearly every communication they receive is either a product-triggered push notification or a message from their care team. That has taken us a long way — but it leaves an entire layer of engagement unbuilt.

We are hiring our first Active Member Marketing Manager to build that layer. You will own the strategy and the execution of every proactive, non-clinically led communication a Twin member receives: email, SMS, in-app and push campaigns, direct mail testing, member webinars, and additional channel exploration we have not yet tried. You will design how those communications layer into the care team relationship and the product notification ecosystem already in place.

This is a build role requiring both strategic vision as well as executional know how. Twin members, data, clinical outcomes, and Braze infrastructure is already in place. We are looking for someone who can point to campaigns they personally built and outcomes they personally moved.

Responsibilities

Active Member Strategy and Program Ownership

- Map the member journey to build sustained engagement, as well as winback for lapsed members, and define the communication strategy for each stage, including who we deliberately choose not to message.

Integration with the Care Team and Product Ecosystem

- Inventory the existing touchpoint landscape and maintain that map as the source of truth.

- Stand up a formal testing program: subject lines and creative to start, then channel mix, cadence, timing, incentive structure, and a direct mail pilot
- Measure performance and build dashboard in partnership with Marketing operations to showcase campaign efficacy
- Report results to Growth Marketing and the broader leadership team on a regular cadence, including wins, losses and adjustments as a result.
- Maintain compliance discipline throughout — HIPAA, PHI handling, TCPA and consent management for SMS, CAN-SPAM, and internal clinical review.
- Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

Required

- Hands-on Braze expertise. You can build a multi-branch Canvas with behavioral triggers, Liquid personalization, and proper suppression logic without waiting on engineering.
- Real multi-channel experience including email plus at least one of SMS, push, or in-app
- Demonstrated experimentation rigor: you design tests with holdouts, understand what a result can and cannot support, and are comfortable reporting a null.
- Comfort building and defining processes. This program does not exist yet; you will be building the first version.

Strongly Preferred

- Exposure to offline or physical channels (direct mail, print, or member webinars) and how to measure them.

- Retention — reduced member attrition
- Clinical outcomes — increased milestone achievements directly impact the bottom line for Twin. Program maturity — a functioning lifecycle engine: documented strategy, healthy deliverability, a running test backlog, and reporting the business trusts.

By the 1970s, the travel industry had quietly figured out something that most businesses hadn't: growth at scale required three different go-to-market motions happening at once. Individual travelers booked directly — they walked in, called up, and bought. Corporate travel programs needed a sales rep to negotiate rates and sign contracts. And then there were travel agents: independent businesses with deep client relationships who effectively decided what their clients bought. The airlines and hotel chains that grew fastest were the ones that recognized all of these distribution motions and invested in each of them in the right ways.

Mercury runs the same three motions. Most of our growth is self-serve and product-led: Founders discover us, sign up, and stay. Our fast-growing sales team closes meaningful deals with larger businesses. And our partners — incorporators, accountants, investors, and platforms that already have the trust of the businesses we want to reach — refer customers to us the same way a great travel agent would: because they believe in our product and its value to their clients. We are looking for a go-to-market leader who can make all three of these motions work harder together with a data-driven strategy and consistent positioning across the customer journey.

What You'll Do

- Own end-to-end GTM strategy across Mercury's three primary growth motions — product-led, sales-led, and partner-led — including segmentation, messaging, and cross-functional execution.
- Manage and grow a team of product marketers and partner marketers supporting these motions today.
- Build and maintain the customer journey, messaging, and infrastructure that works across all three motions: shared value propositions and personas that flex appropriately for self-serve onboarding flows, sales conversations, and partner co-marketing
- Partner closely with the growth product org on strategy and execution for driving top-of-funnel, conversion, activation, and virality.
- Partner with sales leadership on messaging and enablement, from battlecards and objection-handling frameworks to segment-specific playbooks
- Develop Mercury's partner marketing strategy in collaboration with the partnerships team — including co-marketing programs, partner enablement materials, and joint GTM playbooks
- Lead customer and market research to stay ahead of competitive dynamics, identify growth opportunities across segments, and feed insights into product, pricing, and roadmap decisions
- Define and track the PMM metrics that matter for growth — from activation to adoption to advocacy — and use them to continuously improve GTM strategy

You Should Have

- 10+ years of B2B product marketing experience, with full ownership of GTM strategy — not just launch coordination
- Demonstrated experience driving growth across multiple GTM motions; you've run product-led, sales-led, and partner-led programs, and you understand how they interact
- Strong messaging and positioning craft — you can develop a compelling narrative from scratch, test it with customers, and translate it into assets that actually get used by sales and partners
- Revenue mindset — you track contribution to pipeline, activation, and retention, and you know how to use data to argue for, refine, and defend your strategy
- Experience working with sales leadership on messaging and proof points to improve their team’s ability to source pipeline and close deals.
- Ability to lead cross-functional initiatives without direct authority — aligning sales, product, partnerships, and growth teams around a shared GTM plan

- Fintech, banking*, or financial services experience — familiarity with the regulatory, trust, and competitive dynamics of this space
- Experience at a company that scaled through multiple GTM channels simultaneously, particularly one with a strong PLG foundation that was extending into enterprise and/or channel
- Data fluency — comfortable pulling your own analysis in Amplitude, Hex, Metabase, or SQL rather than waiting on a data team

- Own the senior client relationship, which often means the founder directly; QBRs should feel like a board-ready business update, not a marketing recap
- Help clients build measurement infrastructure from scratch when it doesn't exist, establish baselines before optimizing against them
- Coordinate paid, SEO, content, email, and creative work around a focused account strategy; scope management is part of the job
- Identify expansion opportunities that fit the client's stage, don't oversell services a brand isn't ready for
- Manage retention and expansion; lead renewals; grow MRR
- Build multi-threaded relationships with multiple layers of client contacts so no single point of contact departure puts an account at risk
- Ensure daily use of our proprietary technology (Iris and nova), Pulse (client performance and sentiment tool) cadence at 100%, and Power Circuit (our proprietary diagnostic system) compliance across managed ADs
- Manage and develop 1–2 direct reports — run regular 1:1s, build development plans, and own their performance reviews
- Coach analysts and specialists; many will be working with startups for the first time

Role Requirements:

- 6+ years in marketing, with meaningful experience working with early-stage or scaling consumer brands
- Has worked with founder-led businesses and understands the dynamic — decisions move fast, emotions run high, strategy and execution blur together
- Comfortable building from scratch: no brand guidelines, no historical data, no benchmark — and still making good decisions
- Understands crowdfunding-to-DTC transitions and what changes when a brand moves from Kickstarter momentum to sustainable acquisition
- Strong prioritization instincts — knows which problems to solve first and which to defer
- Comfortable with scrappy media mixes and knows how to get signal out of small budgets
- Track record of retaining and growing accounts, including accounts that went through rough patches

- Expansion to Churn Ratio (ETCR)
- Net MRR across portfolio
- Client NPS (8+ avg)
- Monthly Service Expansion pipeline generation
- Power Circuit Certification (annual)

About the role

We are seeking a data-obsessed, US-based Senior Growth Marketing Manager to own the lifecycle across three distinct customer journeys: converting prospects into customers, expanding existing customers through cross-sell and upsell, and scaling a recently launched product line. The through-line is conversion, retention, and maximizing long-term customer value (LTV).

These three journeys work differently, and that's the interesting part of the job. Prospect-to-customer conversion is a blend of self-serve digital and human follow-up — live agents and voice AI — so your job is to design what gets said, to whom, and when, so that confidence keeps building in the gaps between conversations. Cross-sell, upsell, and the new product line are entirely self-serve. There is no human in the loop, which means the messaging, the timing, and the on-page experience have to carry the entire decision on their own.

Life insurance is a high-consideration purchase, so lack of trust and product understanding are the biggest drivers of drop-off. Across all three journeys, you own the connective tissue that moves someone from "a company I found on the internet" to "a company I trust to safeguard my future." You will operate on shared OKRs with the product managers who own each of these three areas, and — for the conversion journey — in close working partnership with Sales leadership, agents, and our voice AI team. You need to know what's actually landing on live calls, not just what performs in an inbox.

Duties and Responsibilities:

- Own the Lifecycle Strategy and Messaging. Design the narrative, cadence, and channel mix that carries someone from first touch to funded policy, from first policy to second, and from early interest in a new product line to scaled adoption. You set the strategy and you build it.
- Convert Prospects into Customers. Own the post-lead journey where self-serve and human touch meet. Build the digital nurture that moves people forward on their own, and build the follow-up content, sequences, and talking points that make every agent and voice AI conversation land — the right articles, proof points, or next steps that can go out within minutes of a call ending, and a system that gets smarter over time rather than sending the same packet to everyone.
- Drive Cross-Sell and Upsell. Existing customers are our highest-intent audience and this motion is fully self-serve. Own identifying the right next product for the right customer at the right moment — additional coverage, product upgrades, a second policy for a spouse — and build the triggered messaging, on-page experiences, and offer structures that get them there without a human touch.
- Scale a Recently Launched Product Line. We have a new product line in market and the mandate is growth. Own its self-serve lifecycle end to end: activation, onboarding, and the messaging that turns early traction into a repeatable, scaling funnel. This is 0→1 becoming 1→10, with the ambiguity and speed that implies.
- Own Retention and LTV. Getting someone to buy is the beginning, not the end. Own the post-purchase journey that keeps policies in force and customers engaged, and be accountable for LTV as a number you move, not a metric you report.
- Build Trust Signals Across the Funnel. Partner with Marketing and Product on the things that actually move a high-consideration financial decision: credibility and social proof, carrier proof points, reviews, and transparency about what someone is actually buying.
- Own the Data Behind Conversion and Drop-Off. Be the expert on cohorts and funnel curves across all three areas. Pull your own data to find exactly where trust and momentum break down, not just where a campaign underperforms — then turn that into a concrete hypothesis and test it.
- Run Experiments End to End. Test messaging, cadence, offers, and channel mix; report on statistical significance; roll out what wins.
- Cross-Functional Ownership. Operate on shared OKRs with the product managers across all three areas, and in a real working relationship with Sales leadership on the conversion journey. Decisions get made, ownership is felt, and campaigns don't stall because nobody knows who's driving.
- Scope. Your time splits across all three journeys with the weighting shifting as each area matures.

Qualifications and Skills:

- 6+ Years of Experience. Senior-level track record in Lifecycle, Growth Marketing, or CRM at a B2C Tech, FinTech, Insurtech, or Marketplace company. Higher-consideration / higher-AOV product experience strongly preferred.
- Copywriting and Messaging Strategy. You can write subject lines that get opened and body copy that drives action — and you know how to build trust and clarity into a high-consideration financial decision, not just optimize for clicks.
- Self-Serve Conversion Instincts. You've moved customers through a purchase decision with no human in the loop and you know what that demands: the messaging, the timing, and the on-page experience all have to do the persuading.

- PM Collaboration. You've worked on a shared goal / OKR with a PM before and have a strong sense of when to lead, when to follow, and how to drive decisions across a cross-functional team. Here you'll do it with several PMs at once.

- Oversee and lead a collection of Paid Media accounts

- Deeply understand client positioning and unique value propositions

- Confirm lead routing is accurate within a CRM

- Understand the value of Programmatic campaigns

- Responsible for personal productivity and utilization

What You Offer:

- 3+ years experience working at a performance/digital marketing agency

- Experience working specifically with B2B SaaS/tech clients in an agency setting

- Deep expertise across paid search and paid social advertising campaigns, such as Google Ads, Facebook Ads, LinkedIn Ads and others

- Proficiency in using advertising platforms and tools such as Google Ads, Facebook Business Manager, LinkedIn Campaign Manager

- Strong understanding of PPC principles, including keyword research, ad copywriting, bid management, and campaign optimization

- Ability to analyze campaign performance data using tools like Google Analytics, GA4, Excel, or other analytics platforms to make data-driven decisions and optimize campaign performance

- Ability to drive results and measure via OCT

- Proven and measurable success with mid-market or enterprise accounts

- A unique perspective on how to drive value for SaaS

- Ability to translate and articulate strategy and tell stories with data

- Equal parts competitive and curious; you’re a true problem solver

- You live on the cutting edge of the industry, always looking for opportunities to grow and share

- Ability to organize, prioritize and manage multiple projects simultaneously

- You’re quality-obsessed and have not lost your soul for advertising

- Driven to stay ahead of industry trends, including actively learning how AI and automation can enhance marketing and operations.

- Travel to visit clients approximately once per year, per client or as needed

- You encompass our core values through every interaction; internally and externally

- Effectively manage approximately five mid-tier and enterprise accounts

- Meet and exceed department level OKRs, such as client growth and goal attainment

- Build client trust and relationships that create consistent renewals

- Cross-sell services that align with client goals and objectives

- Clearly communicate results with client point of contact and executives

- Exceptional decision making, as it relates to strategic direction for accounts

As a remote-first company, you’ll have the ability to work from anywhere in the US, with the option to enjoy our state-of-the-art offices in Irvine, California. Procurify is the agentic procurement platform that helps mid-market organizations get complete control over their spend.

We’re trusted by hundreds of companies around the world, across industries like biotechnology, education, health care, manufacturing, and software, to manage over $100B in spend.

Product marketing sits at the center of how we're understood in that market, and we're hiring a Director to lead it.

About the role

Procurify is looking for a Director of Product Marketing to define how we compete and win. You'll own the company narrative, the messaging architecture our go-to-market organization builds on, how we segment and prioritize the market, and the analyst relationships that influence how Procurify is understood.

This is a chance to help define Procurify's next stage of growth as the agentic procurement platform. You'll be at the center of translating that strategy into positioning, messaging, assets, and programs that drive demonstrable impact across our go-to-market organization.

This is a senior seat on the marketing leadership team, with full visibility across the company and regular engagement with executives. You'll lead two Product Marketing Managers. You'll raise their craft, sharpen their judgment, and expand what they're capable of owning, building both the team's impact and their careers as leaders in their own right.

This is a true player-coach role. Your PMMs own their product portfolios, and you'll guide their strategy and raise the quality of their work while directly owning company-level and cross-portfolio initiatives yourself. It's hands-on by design: you get the scope and influence of a senior leader while staying close to the craft.

AI fluency is table stakes for this role. We expect AI to be foundational to how you analyze information, build workflows, create and evaluate work, and scale the team's impact without compromising quality.

Key responsibilities

Positioning and market strategy

- Own Procurify's positioning strategy and define how we differentiate in the procurement market.

- Build and maintain the company-level narrative and messaging architecture as the single source of truth across all surfaces, and translate it into positioning teams can execute against.

- Own the AI and agentic narrative: make the platform's intelligence concrete, credible, and differentiated for finance and operations buyers.

- Own market segmentation and use it to direct where we invest and who we talk to.

- Own the voice of the customer with deep customer research and win/loss analysis.

- Use product, customer, funnel, and market data to identify patterns, test assumptions, and turn evidence into clear strategic recommendations.

- Shape Procurify's analyst relations strategy and narrative, building credible relationships with top-tier analyst firms and influencing how the company and category are represented.

- Act as a credible external voice on procurement and the agentic shift through analyst briefings, press, and webinars.

Go-to-market

About OpenRouter

OpenRouter is the open AI routing and infrastructure layer that enterprises use to access, manage, and optimize the best large language models across providers—without lock-in, capacity constraints, or unnecessary cost. About the Role

OpenRouter grows because developers find it, try it, and route more of their work through it. More than 10 million users and 250k+ apps process 200T+ tokens on the platform every month, nearly all of it starting in self-serve. You’ll own turning that reach into revenue: more of the right developers discovering OpenRouter, signing up, buying their first credits, and growing their usage.

You’ll run the self-serve growth engine: paid media and sponsorships, AEO/SEO, conversion optimization on key pages and flows, and the measurement and forecasting that keeps it all optimized. That’s roughly 75% of the role. The other 25% is partnering with our enterprise team as an execution and thought partner on demand gen.

This is a Director-level, player/coach role with a paid budget of $5M+ for 2027. In year one you’re hands-on: buying media, shipping tests, building the measurement stack, managing agencies. As the engine proves out, you build the team around it.

- Own self-serve revenue growth: build and run the marketing engine that reaches developers at scale, moves them from first touch to signup, first credit purchase, and expanding usage.

- Plan and buy paid media across channels developers respect: search, social, newsletter and podcast/creator sponsorships, audio, OOH, and event sponsorships, spanning awareness and direct response. You own the budget and the agency/vendor bench.

- Own the AEO/SEO roadmap for openrouter.ai: classic organic search plus answer-engine visibility,executing with content, engineering, and outside specialists.

- Run conversion optimization on key pages and flows (homepage, model pages, pricing, signup, credit purchase) in partnership with product and engineering, on a standing experimentation cadence.

- Own measurement for all paid activity: attribution design, incrementality and holdout testing, channel reporting, and the quarterly forecasting and planning cycle for the paid budget.

- Support enterprise demand gen as an execution and thought partner: MQL/MQA generation programs and the measurement connecting marketing touches to pipeline.

What We’re Looking For

- 8+ years in growth or performance marketing, including meaningful time at a developer tools, API-first, or technical B2B SaaS company.

- You’ve been directly accountable for self-serve or usage-based revenue (signup, activation, and spend) as your primary metric.

- You’ve owned an annual multi-channel paid budget of $5M+, or scaled a program from seven figures into that range, and can walk through your CAC, payback math, and the channels you killed.

- Hands-on with the measurement stack: product analytics (PostHog, GA4, Hex, or similar), attribution design, and at least one incrementality or holdout test you designed yourself.

- You’ve owned or directed SEO for a technical product, and you have a working point of view on AEO: what changes when the search result is a ChatGPT answer.

- You’ve built and run CRO/experimentation programs with real statistical discipline: hypothesis, test design, readout, decision.

- Player/coach: comfortable executing solo today and building the function (agencies, contractors, eventual hires) as it scales.

Nice to Have

- You’ve marketed to AI engineers specifically, or you’ve built something against an LLM API yourself (bonus if it was through OpenRouter).

- Brand campaign experience: OOH, audio, or major sponsorships, measured with brand-lift studies or geo holdouts.

- Demand gen or ABM experience feeding an enterprise sales motion.

- Time inside a consumption-pricing business (Twilio, Datadog, Vercel-style) where marketing was judged on usage rather than lead volume.

_If you don't think you meet all of the criteria below but still are interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box, and we're looking for someone who is excited to join the team._

TRM Labs is building the global standard for investigations.

We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager who understands that this role is not content production. It's market ownership. Your job is to make TRM the obvious choice for a specific set of buyers. You work closely with a Product Manager and Sales — the PM builds, Sales opens doors, and you make sure buyers arrive already convinced. AI handles the execution. You handle the judgment.

Product marketers at TRM make the category feel like TRM's home turf before a buyer ever talks to anyone.

What you'll own

You'll own the market position for TRM's AI-native investigation platform. Your buyers are investigators and analysts running complex, high-stakes cases where the quality of their tooling directly determines outcomes. Your job is to make TRM the platform they can't imagine working without. That means deep fluency with how government investigations actually run, positioning that speaks to the specific workflow pressures these buyers face, and ownership of the moments where TRM cements its position as the standard.

How you'll work

Deep diving: You know the product at the level where you can demo it as well as anyone in the company. You know where the real value sits and where it breaks down. You're in deal reviews and customer conversations often enough to know what lands, and you can hold a real conversation with both engineering and buyers.

Positioning: You find the wedge: the framing where a prospect chooses TRM every time and asking about the competition sounds like the wrong question. You build the architecture everything hangs from: the claims, the proof, the hierarchy, the words TRM owns. Tight enough that a new hire and a ten-year veteran say the same true thing.

Incepting: The story only works if the company believes it first. You get Sales carrying the message without you in the room, engineers who can explain why what they're building matters, and execs who open deals with the same frame you set. You don't mandate alignment. You create it by making the story so clear and compelling that people want to tell it.

Owning the moment: A tier-one launch, a CEO keynote, the webpage a buyer lands on before they ever take a meeting. These are the moments where TRM either makes an impression or misses one. You own the narrative, the timing, and the outcome. The bar is a defining moment the whole company points to. You don't wait for those. You go make them.

What we're looking for

Storytelling. You think in narrative, not slides. You can make something technical matter to a stranger in two sentences. Your stories are grounded in data: win/loss patterns, customer signals, market evidence, because the most persuasive narrative is one that's actually true. You translate the same story across a keynote, a one-pager, and a website without losing what makes it land.

Commercial instincts. You understand what moves a deal, not just what sounds good in a deck. You've been present enough in the sales cycle to know the difference, and you've changed your positioning because of it.

AI builder. You build systems for the team, not just yourself. You've already offloaded the repeatable work to automation: competitive monitoring, content generation, persona synthesis. You spend your time on the judgment calls that actually require you. Walk us through something you built that made the whole team faster.

Judgment. You know what good looks like across the work and you say so when it isn't: a positioning brief that almost works, a website that doesn't land, a design that misses. You hold the standard and give feedback that moves things forward, not feedback that leaves people guessing.

Hard requirements

- 5+ years in product marketing at a B2B SaaS company

- You've owned at least two tier-one launches end to end: strategy, narrative, execution, and post-launch measurement

- You've owned a website or major digital channel and made content decisions that moved pipeline, not just pageviews

- You already use AI to build workflows and systems and can walk through a real example of something you built for your team, not just yourself

Deal breakers

- Marketers who measure output in assets shipped

- Anyone who treats AI as something to explore rather than something already running in their workflow

- Candidates whose best examples inherited existing infrastructure. We need builders, not operators of programs someone else built.

About the team

TRM's product team doesn't coordinate work. It owns outcomes. Product marketers are embedded in the sales motion, in customer conversations, and in launch decisions. The team is small, the scope is real, and what you ship shows up directly in how deals close and how the market talks about TRM. PMMs here don't wait to be asked. If the standard is slipping somewhere, you say so and help. AI is how we work, not just what we build.

ValPay builds embedded payments for software companies. Our PayFac-as-a-Service model lets ISVs offer payments to their merchants under their own brand, while we handle underwriting, compliance, and risk. Our partners serve healthcare, legal, hospitality, professional services, and other vertical markets.
Launching a payments product is the easy part. The value is created when ISV partners go live, their merchants enroll, and transactions flow. We’re hiring a product marketing Lead whose success is measured by adoption: how quickly and how deeply partners and merchants use our products.
You’ll own positioning, launches, and lifecycle marketing across our vertical markets and across North America, Europe, and APAC. You’ll report to the CEO and work closely with product, sales, partnerships, the ISV channel team, and operations.
AI should be part of how you work. Use it to research, draft, analyze, and automate. You’re responsible for the quality of the result.
What we value
Sound judgment and attention to detail.
Measuring success by what customers do, not by what we shipped.
Taking responsibility and finishing work without being chased.
Understanding how the business makes money and caring about results.
The honesty to say when something isn’t working, including your own work.
What you’ll do
Drive partner and merchant adoption:
You’ll own the adoption journey end to end: signature, integration, go-live, first transaction, merchant enrollment, and expansion. The hardest gap is between “integrated” and “actively transacting,” and you’ll be the person who finds out where partners and merchants stall and designs programs to close it. That means lifecycle campaigns, onboarding content, and activation playbooks for two audiences at once: the ISV partner and the merchants who use their software. With the ISV channel team, you’ll run co-marketing and merchant-enrollment campaigns that lift penetration within each partner’s customer base.
Measure adoption and act on it:
You’ll build and maintain the adoption dashboard: activation rate, time to first transaction, attach and penetration rate, volume per merchant, feature adoption, and cohort retention. You’ll use that data to segment partners and merchants, flag at-risk accounts, and surface expansion opportunities, then take what you find to the teams who can act on it.
Own positioning and messaging:
You’ll develop the positioning, value propositions, and messaging for each product and vertical, and for new verticals and markets as we enter them. A central part of this is explaining clearly how our embedded payments offering differs from horizontal PayFacs, processors, and ISOs. You’ll translate technical capabilities into the outcomes ISVs and merchants care about: revenue share, retention, cleaner reconciliation, and faster onboarding.
Run launches built around activation:
You’ll lead launch plans for new products, features, verticals, and regions. Every launch gets adoption targets and a 30/60/90-day activation plan, not only awareness goals. You’ll also make sure what we’re building is communicated publicly, online and through partners. You’ll adapt messaging to regional regulatory and market conditions, and work with product, finance, risk, and support so that each launch is commercially and operationally ready before it goes out.
Equip sales, partnerships, and support:
You’ll create the sales playbooks, pitch decks, battlecards, case studies, ROI calculators, and objection-handling guides that sales and partnership teams use, and equip support to explain the products as well. You’ll train teams to sell for activation, not just signature. You’ll run win/loss and churn analysis and feed what you learn back into positioning and the product.
Represent the market inside the company:
You’ll track competitors, pricing, interchange, and regulatory developments, and be the voice of the market and of adoption data in product planning. When acquisitions or product consolidations happen, you’ll support portfolio and integration messaging.
What you’ll bring
At least 3 years of experience in product marketing at a B2B software, fintech, or payments company.
A track record of running launches and measuring them on adoption or usage, not only on awareness.
Experience marketing to two audiences at once, such as partners and their customers, or platforms and their users.
Working knowledge of how card payments work, or the ability to learn it quickly and explain it accurately.
Comfort with data. You can define a metric, build or spec a dashboard, and draw a conclusion from it.
Strong writing. You can turn a technical capability into a clear business case for a software company or a small-business owner.
Experience building sales enablement that teams actually used.
You can take a loosely defined goal, set your own plan, and finish it.
You use AI tools every day for research, drafting, and analysis, and you check what they produce.
Useful experience
Embedded payments, PayFac, or ISV channel experience.
Lifecycle or onboarding marketing in a partner-led business.
Marketing in healthcare, legal, hospitality, or professional services software.
Launching products in Europe or APAC.
Running win/loss or churn analysis programs.
Hands-on experience with SQL, a BI tool, or marketing automation.
Portfolio or integration messaging after an acquisition.
Who will enjoy this role
You notice when a partner has been live for two months and only a handful of their merchants have enrolled, and you want to know why. Is it the pitch, the onboarding, the partner’s own sales team, or the product?
In the same week you might rebuild a merchant onboarding email sequence, pull cohort data for the CEO, train a partnership team on a new vertical, and rewrite a battlecard after a lost deal to a horizontal processor.
The scope is wide for one person, and adoption is a harder target than launch coverage. You’ll be judged on numbers you influence but don’t fully control, which means working through partners, product, and sales to move them. Priorities will shift with the roadmap and with acquisitions.
Why this role matters
ValPay is building products and features for software partners across several verticals and regions. That work has limited impact unless partners and merchants know about it, understand it, and use it.
You’ll work directly with the CEO to decide how our products are positioned and how each launch turns into transactions. Your work affects how quickly partners go live, how many of their merchants enroll, and how much volume flows through the platform. You’ll have the authority to set the story and change it when the adoption data says so.

ValPay conçoit des solutions de paiement intégrées pour les entreprises de logiciels. Notre modèle PayFac-as-a-Service permet aux éditeurs de logiciels (ISV) d’offrir des paiements à leurs commerçants sous leur propre marque, pendant que nous prenons en charge la souscription, la conformité et la gestion des risques. Nos partenaires servent les secteurs de la santé, du droit, de l’hôtellerie et de la restauration, des services professionnels et d’autres marchés verticaux.
Lancer un produit de paiement, c’est la partie facile. La valeur se crée lorsque les ISV partenaires sont mis en service, que leurs commerçants adhèrent et que les transactions circulent. Nous recherchons une personne responsable du marketing produit dont le succès se mesure à l’adoption : la rapidité et la profondeur avec lesquelles les partenaires et les commerçants utilisent nos produits.
Vous serez responsable du positionnement, des lancements et du marketing du cycle de vie dans l’ensemble de nos marchés verticaux, en Amérique du Nord, en Europe et en Asie-Pacifique. Vous relèverez du chef de la direction et travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes produit, ventes, partenariats, canal ISV et opérations.
L’IA devrait faire partie de votre façon de travailler. Utilisez-la pour faire de la recherche, rédiger, analyser et automatiser. Vous êtes responsable de la qualité du résultat.
Ce qui compte pour nous
Un bon jugement et le souci du détail.
Mesurer le succès à ce que font les clients, et non à ce que nous avons livré.
Prendre ses responsabilités et mener le travail à terme sans qu’on ait à faire de relances.
Comprendre comment l’entreprise génère des revenus et se soucier des résultats.
L’honnêteté de dire quand quelque chose ne fonctionne pas, y compris dans son propre travail.
Ce que vous ferez
Stimuler l’adoption par les partenaires et les commerçants :
Vous serez responsable de tout le parcours d’adoption : signature, intégration technique, mise en service, première transaction, adhésion des commerçants et expansion. L’écart le plus difficile à combler se situe entre « intégré » et « en transaction active », et c’est vous qui déterminerez où les partenaires et les commerçants stagnent et qui concevrez des programmes pour combler cet écart. Cela comprend des campagnes de cycle de vie, du contenu d’accueil et d’intégration (onboarding) et des guides d’activation pour deux publics à la fois : l’ISV partenaire et les commerçants qui utilisent son logiciel. Avec l’équipe du canal ISV, vous mènerez des campagnes de comarketing et d’adhésion des commerçants qui augmentent le taux de pénétration au sein de la clientèle de chaque partenaire.
Mesurer l’adoption et agir en conséquence :
Vous créerez et tiendrez à jour le tableau de bord de l’adoption : taux d’activation, délai avant la première transaction, taux de rattachement et de pénétration, volume par commerçant, adoption des fonctionnalités et rétention par cohorte. Vous utiliserez ces données pour segmenter les partenaires et les commerçants, repérer les comptes à risque et faire ressortir les occasions d’expansion, puis vous transmettrez vos constats aux équipes qui peuvent agir.
Définir le positionnement et les messages :
Vous élaborerez le positionnement, les propositions de valeur et les messages pour chaque produit et chaque marché vertical, ainsi que pour les nouveaux marchés à mesure que nous y entrons. Un volet central de ce travail consiste à expliquer clairement en quoi notre offre de paiements intégrés se distingue des PayFac horizontaux, des processeurs de paiement et des ISO. Vous traduirez les capacités techniques en résultats qui comptent pour les ISV et les commerçants : partage des revenus, fidélisation, rapprochement simplifié et intégration plus rapide.
Mener des lancements axés sur l’activation :
Vous dirigerez les plans de lancement des nouveaux produits, fonctionnalités, marchés verticaux et régions. Chaque lancement comporte des cibles d’adoption et un plan d’activation sur 30, 60 et 90 jours, et pas seulement des objectifs de notoriété. Vous veillerez aussi à ce que ce que nous construisons soit communiqué publiquement, en ligne et par l’intermédiaire des partenaires. Vous adapterez les messages aux conditions réglementaires et commerciales de chaque région, et travaillerez avec les équipes produit, finances, risques et soutien pour que chaque lancement soit prêt sur les plans commercial et opérationnel avant sa sortie.
Outiller les équipes des ventes, des partenariats et du soutien :
Vous créerez les guides de vente, présentations, fiches concurrentielles, études de cas, calculateurs de RCI et guides de réponse aux objections qu’utilisent les équipes des ventes et des partenariats, et vous outillerez également l’équipe du soutien pour qu’elle puisse expliquer les produits. Vous formerez les équipes à vendre en visant l’activation, et pas seulement la signature. Vous mènerez des analyses des gains et des pertes ainsi que de l’attrition, et réinjecterez vos apprentissages dans le positionnement et le produit.
Représenter le marché au sein de l’entreprise :
Vous suivrez les concurrents, les prix, les frais d’interchange et l’évolution de la réglementation, et serez la voix du marché et des données d’adoption dans la planification des produits. D’excellentes aptitudes en rédaction. Vous savez transformer une capacité technique en argumentaire d’affaires clair pour une entreprise de logiciels ou le propriétaire d’une petite entreprise.
De l’expérience dans la création d’outils d’habilitation des ventes que les équipes ont réellement utilisés.

Atouts

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
That is the whole job.
Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
Here is what "end to end" actually means.
You are the account manager. We do not have any.
You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.
Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.
We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
You can live anywhere.
We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
Requirements
What the job looks like
Own a set of DTC accounts
as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
Own the client relationship.
There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
Audit before you touch anything.
Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
Run brand and non brand as different businesses.
Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
Know what PMax is actually doing.
The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
Keep Google's automation on a leash.
Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
Own the feed.
Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
Own the tracking.
GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.
Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
Build the things the account needs.
Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
You are a fit if
You have done this with real money.
Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
You are fluent in the whole stack
, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
You are AI native, and you build.
This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.
You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
You are skeptical of your own numbers.
You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.
Where you live is up to you.
Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
You are not a fit if
"That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
You want to be told what to do this week.
You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
Benefits
Why this role is exciting
This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
Requirements
What the job looks like
Own 4 to 6 DTC accounts
as the strategist, the buyer, the creative lead, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $30k/mo to $1M/mo.
Own the client relationship.
There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you're the one who answers when something isn't working.
Run the research before the ads.
Marketing is 80% research here. You mine customer reviews, ad comments, support tickets, and Reddit for the language and objections that become angles. You pull competitor ad libraries. You run our internal tooling that OCRs and transcribes the ads in your account and ties them to performance, so you know what winning and losing actually look like in
this
account.
Write the briefs and the scripts, and direct the work.
Creative direction is yours. You run revision rounds with our editors and designers and you hold the quality bar.
Ship creative on a cadence.
Roughly 8 to 10 new ad launches a week is where accounts hold, in batches every 1 to 1.5 weeks. Informed volume, not spray and pray. We want better hypotheses, not more randomness.
Build and test landing pages.
Advertorials, comparison pages, PDPs. Built in Claude Code, deployed to Vercel, tested live on a subdomain before anything gets pushed into the client's theme.
Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.
Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
Report on new customer economics.
We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended ROAS and not last click. You'll be expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.
You're a fit if
You've done this with real money.
Hands-on Meta at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them.
You're AI-native, and you build.
This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude (or equivalent) as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it. If you can research, write, and build a converting page from scratch, we can teach you the buying.
You can write direct response in English at a native or near-native level.
Hooks, scripts, ad copy, advertorial. In the customer's own words, not invented. This is the single biggest source of leverage in the role and the thing we screen hardest for. If writing persuasive English isn't a strength, this isn't the job.
You can communicate your ideas.
This matters as much as anything else on this list. You'll be in front of clients constantly with nobody in between, so you need to be able to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire.
You have taste and you know when to hand off.
You direct creative, you don't half-build it yourself. AI slop shipped to a client is a habit we break, not a shortcut we accept.
You can work US Eastern business hours
for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
Bonus:
you've built or operated your own Shopify store or eComm brand. Several of our team have, and it shows.
You're not a fit if
"That wasn't my role" is in your vocabulary.
It's the fastest way to end an interview here. If creative was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the creative.
You want to be told what to do this week.
You need a ticketing system to know what matters.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
That is the whole job.
Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
Here is what "end to end" actually means.
You are the account manager. We do not have any.
You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.
Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.
We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
You can live anywhere.
We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
Requirements
What the job looks like
Own a set of DTC accounts
as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
Own the client relationship.
There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
Audit before you touch anything.
Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
Run brand and non brand as different businesses.
Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
Know what PMax is actually doing.
The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
Keep Google's automation on a leash.
Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
Own the feed.
Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
Own the tracking.
GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.
Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
Build the things the account needs.
Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
You are a fit if
You have done this with real money.
Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
You are fluent in the whole stack
, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
You are AI native, and you build.
This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.
You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
You are skeptical of your own numbers.
You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.
Where you live is up to you.
Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
You are not a fit if
"That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
You want to be told what to do this week.
You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
Benefits
Why this role is exciting
This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
That is the whole job.
Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
Here is what "end to end" actually means.
You are the account manager. We do not have any.
You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.
Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.
We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
You can live anywhere.
We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
Requirements
What the job looks like
Own a set of DTC accounts
as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
Own the client relationship.
There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
Audit before you touch anything.
Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
Run brand and non brand as different businesses.
Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
Know what PMax is actually doing.
The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
Keep Google's automation on a leash.
Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
Own the feed.
Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
Own the tracking.
GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.
Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
Build the things the account needs.
Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
You are a fit if
You have done this with real money.
Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
You are fluent in the whole stack
, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
You are AI native, and you build.
This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.
You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
You are skeptical of your own numbers.
You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.
Where you live is up to you.
Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
You are not a fit if
"That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
You want to be told what to do this week.
You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
Benefits
Why this role is exciting
This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

Dispatch is redefining how the world experiences home and field service. Founded in 2013 and trusted by leading brands and service providers, we power seamless, reliable service experiences through a modern platform built for scale. Our platform gives businesses the visibility, communication, and control they need to manage every step of the service journey, from job acceptance through completion. With the acquisition of Youreka in 2023, Dispatch expanded its capabilities to include a leading Salesforce-native Smart Forms application that equips mobile workers with guided workflows, improves field execution and customer service, and scales to support complex enterprise operations.
As part of Manos Software, a Valsoft operating group, Dispatch combines the focus and agility of a specialized software company with the long-term support of a global vertical SaaS organization. We're investing in our product, our customers, and our team with a focus on sustainable, profitable growth.
We're now investing in a dedicated marketing function to match the strength of our product and customer base, and we're hiring our first Director of Demand Generation to build it.
THE ROLE:
Reporting directly to the CEO, the Director of Demand Generation will own demand generation for Dispatch and Youreka, reshaping what marketing means for the company and our products. This role also owns our Business Development Representative team's strategy and targets, working primarily through our existing BDR team lead. This is a hands-on, builder role: you'll set strategy and run campaigns yourself in the early days, then pursue growth within the marketing team as the function proves out.
AS THE DIRECTOR OF DEMAND GENERATION, YOU WILL:
Demand generation & growth - assess Dispatch's situation from first principles to determine where marketing should focus (paid acquisition, lifecycle/email, organic, and other channels); own the marketing automation and CRM stack; generate and manage a healthy, measurable pipeline in close partnership with sales. Building this out is the top priority for this role.
Product-market fit & positioning - identify, through testing and analysis, which segments, use cases, and messages actually convert; use that to sharpen demand-gen targeting and messaging, and share findings with our Product Marketing team to inform their formal positioning work.
Content - build a content engine (website copy, case studies, thought leadership) that supports demand generation and conversion.
Team leadership - own strategy and targets for our BDR team, working closely with the existing Lead BDR and aligning team output with the broader demand generation strategy. You will also manage an existing marketing team resource and help define future role additions over time.
Diagnose marketing channel mix for Dispatch's products - prioritizing investment accordingly.
Establish the processes, reporting, and KPIs the function will run on.
WITHIN THE FIRST SIX MONTHS, YOU WILL:
Build a functioning marketing engine - team, tools, and process, revamped from a lean starting point and working closely with our Senior Marketing Manager.
Define a clear, data-backed point of view on where Dispatch should focus its marketing investment, measurable pipeline/revenue contribution from marketing, and BDR-driven programs.
Develop sharper product positioning and messaging along with marketing support delivered for major product launches and market expansions.
Be viewed internally and externally as a strategic leader for Dispatch's growth functions.
LOCATION:
Dispatch fully accommodates remote work, as long as you have a permanent residence in the US and reside in one of our registered states. Want to spend a month in Italy? Great, do it! Live in Idaho? Sweet, we have another team member there! As long as you are crushing your goals and helping us drive the business forward, you do you. We also have an office in Boston that is open and available for you to use.
SALARY:
The base salary range for this role is between $160,000 - $170,000 annually. Actual pay within the range is influenced by multiple factors, including but not limited to skill set, residence location, and prior work experience. In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for an annual bonus and benefits.
Requirements
5–10 years of marketing experience including specific focus on demand generation and program definition.
A startup-tested operator - comfortable being hands-on and building programs with limited resources, not just directing an existing team.
A proven track record of owning a marketing function or team from an early stage.
Proven, hands-on experience managing a demand-generation/marketing function is required. Experience managing a team on a sales-style comp plan - such as a BDR, SDR, or inside-sales function - is a plus.
An analytical, first-principles thinker who can diagnose which channels and tactics actually drive results for a given business, rather than defaulting to a standard playbook - we're counting on you to help define our ideal marketing mix, not just execute one.
A strong written communicator who can turn technical or operational product value into compelling brand and content narratives.
B2B SaaS experience preferred; experience in field service, home services, or enterprise software is a plus.

About Coursedog

Experience creating email assets in Canva, Photoshop, or AI-powered creative tools.

Familiarity with using AI tools to accelerate creative production, analysis, research, and troubleshooting.
